items.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
items.summary: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models.
items.author: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek

items.title: DexLink: Synthesizing Dexterous Behaviors from Chained Hand-object Poses
items.summary: Synthesizing diverse dexterous manipulation policies is challenging: existing simulation-based approaches rely on human demonstrations which are difficult to scale, or use generic reward functions, which provide limited control over the hand-object interactions. We propose DexLink, which addresses these limitations by synthesizing diverse dexterous behaviors from sparse, reusable hand-object interaction templates.
items.author: Meenal Parakh, Deep Patel, Beining Han et al.

items.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
items.summary: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together.
items.author: Xueyang Yu, Yifan Jing, Taiming Lu et al.

items.author: USGS

items.title: MERLoc: Robust Robot Localization in Dynamic Environments with Pose-Based Retrieval over 3D Gaussian Splatting References
items.summary: Robots operating in previously mapped spaces must localize accurately despite moving people and rearranged objects. Most localization pipelines match the query against a sparse set of captured reference images retrieved by appearance, which is brittle under scene change and repeating structures.
items.author: Michael Baumgartner, Dario Mylonopoulos, Sammy Christen et al.

items.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
items.summary: We propose a background independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes. Starting from first order gravity, we solve the gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain the reduced phase space at finite $G_N$.
items.author: Venkatesa Chandrasekaran

items.title: Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions
items.summary: We show that in any $d$-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order $n$ between two disjoint balls maps to a CFT partition function on a manifold of topology $\#^{n-1}(S^1 \times S^{d-1})$, with moduli fixed by the ball configuration and single-ball modular flow.
items.author: Hewei Frederic Jia

items.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.summary: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session. We introduce $μ$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction.
items.author: Qihao Lin, Guanxu Chen, Shuhang Zheng et al.

items.title: Voltage-Enhanced Photorefractive Hysteresis in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Photonic-Crystal Cavities
items.summary: We observe voltage-enhanced photorefractive hysteresis in thin-film lithium niobate nanocavities, causing the resonance to appear at different wavelengths during increasing- and decreasing-wavelength laser scans. Their separation grows with bias magnitude and optical power, but depends weakly on scan speed over 1-200 nm/s.
items.author: Alessandro Buzzi, Bjarke A. Frederiksen, Mikkel Heuck et al.

items.title: Memory Is Not Ground Truth: Revising Navigation Authority under Unreliable VLM Evidence for Persistent Semantic Navigation
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable robots to reason about semantic and spatio-temporal context, verify task-relevant objects, and guide sensing and navigation. Persistent memory can reduce redundant search for field robots, but when should a memory continue to guide behavior? Repeated misses may suggest that a memory is stale.
items.author: Sumukh Shrote, Shenbagaraj Kannapiran, Eric Eaton et al.

items.title: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video
items.summary: How an object deforms when it hits the ground reveals what it is made of. From a single real video of a drop, we estimate a deformable object's density-normalized stiffness $E/ρ$, and its yield stress $σ_Y/ρ$ when the impact causes plastic deformation, with a feed-forward predictor trained only in simulation.
items.author: Ziyue Peng, Yanxi Hu, Junyoung Kim et al.

items.title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
items.summary: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four.
items.author: Taushif Ahmed, Syed Mehedi Hasan

items.title: Neural Network Decoders For Qubit Loss
items.summary: Qubit loss is a significant source of error in many quantum hardware platforms, requiring circuits that periodically replace or reset qubits to maintain fault-tolerance. When the reset process includes loss-resolving measurements, this information can improve decoding and substantially reduce overhead compared to the case where this information is not available.
items.author: J. Wilson Staples, Winston Fu, Yihe Dong et al.

items.title: The Price of Quantum Advantage in Computational Chemistry
items.summary: As the fault-tolerant era approaches, the question shifts from ``is it possible'' to ``is it worthwhile.'' To assess practical quantum advantage against reliable classical baselines, we examine 26 benchmark instances including FeMoco, iron-sulfur clusters, cytochrome P450, and ruthenium catalysts using two selected configuration interaction solvers, SHCI and TrimCI.
items.author: Haejung Koh, Katerina Gratsea, Hao Zhang et al.

items.title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics
items.summary: The look-elsewhere effect in searches for new physics arises when scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, requiring global correction of local p-values. A framework provides correction for continuous parameter scans, but challenges remain, particularly with machine learning-based searches.
items.author: Gaia Grosso, Sergio Rodriguez-Benitez, Louis Lyons
items.original_title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
items.original_summary: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one.
items.ai_title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics

items.title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
items.summary: Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning. Over the years, a wide variety of strategies have been proposed to define split conditions within the greedy learning framework, aiming to guide instance routing and enhance predictive performance.
items.author: Cristiano Landi, Alessio Cascione, Riccardo Guidotti

items.title: FineDex: Bridging Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation
items.summary: Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control, yet existing dexterous manipulation and human-object interaction (HOI) generation methods rarely let one specify how an interaction is performed: five-fingered hands are often reduced to grippers, or finger usage is copied from individual human demonstrations.
items.author: Yujia Zeng, Yuxin Chen, Yuzhen Song et al.

items.title: A Reconfigurable Four-State Sensor Based on Orthogonal Thermal and Chemical Stimuli
items.summary: This article presents a novel four-state refractive index (RI) sensor based on distinct phases of palladium (Pd) and vanadium dioxide (VO$_2$), controlled by orthogonal thermal and chemical stimuli. This is a numerical, simulation-only study: all results are obtained from two-dimensional finite-element method (FEM) simulations.
items.author: Ashfaq Ur Rahman Ifty, Sadia Basher, Abdullah Al Zayed et al.

items.title: Character expansion of the Itzykson-Zuber pair correlator
items.summary: We revisit a long-standing problem of correlation functions with the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber measure. The immediate goal is to reproduce the long-known answer for pair correlator in the form of character expansion - a sum over Schur polynomials with carefully adjusted coefficients.
items.author: Alexei Morozov, Hasib Sifat

items.title: New formula for holographic spectral function
items.summary: Researchers have derived a new formula for the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on an extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in AdS5, using quasi-normal modes and branch-cut data. The formula factorizes into an infinite product over QNM poles and a factor encoding the branch cut discontinuity.
items.author: Jyotirmoy Bhattacharya, Amiya Mishra, Aditya Sharma et al.
items.original_title: A Pole-Cut Formula for Holographic Extremal Correlators
items.original_summary: We show that the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in $AdS_5$ admits an elegant formula in terms of the quasi-normal modes (QNMs) and branch-cut data. items.title: Heavy-flavor transverse energy-energy correlators in the color-glass condensate
items.summary: We calculate the transverse energy--energy correlator (TEEC) for forward heavy-quark pair production in proton--nucleus collisions at leading order within the Color Glass Condensate framework. The calculation retains the heavy--quark mass, exact final-state parton kinematics and full relative azimuthal-angle dependence, without imposing a back-to-back approximation.
items.author: Zhong-Bo Kang, Carlos Lamas, Jani Penttala

items.title: NASA Explores New Crop Options for Deep Space Missions
items.summary: As NASA prepares for upcoming space missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are actively evaluating various crops to supply astronauts with fresh food and essential nutrition. Expanding menu variety is vital for long-term space exploration, with recent testing pointing toward options like strawberries.
items.original_title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
items.original_summary: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving.

items.title: Diagnosing internal leakage currents through magnetometry of lithium-ion cells
items.summary: Internal leakage currents are difficult to detect and to localize through measurements at the terminals of lithium-ion cells. We measured the magnetic fields of pouch cells non-invasively with a magnetometer while a battery cycler set the current and recorded the voltage.
items.author: Shaurya Shukla, Chengtong Zhang, Yinan Hu et al.

items.title: Childhood Connections Lead to NASA Career
items.summary: Growing up with parents who worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, Ashley Knight experienced space agency discussions around the dinner table daily. These early experiences included significant family dialogues following historical events like the space shuttle Challenger disaster, shaping her future career path.
items.author: Rob Garner

items.original_summary: Conversations about NASA were the norm around the dinner table during Ashley Knight’s childhood. Her parents worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and discussions about happenings at the agency continued even when they came home from the office.

items.title: Transverse Shifts Driven by Geometric Orbital Torque in Altermagnets
items.summary: Anomalous transverse shifts in interface reflection are conventionally attributed to spin-orbit coupling or its pseudospin analogue. Here, we uncover a distinct geometric mechanism driven solely by an orbital torque arising from Fermi-surface anisotropy. During total reflection, an incident wave packet penetrates the anisotropic transmitted medium as an evanescent wave.
items.author: Runze Li, Yugui Yao, Zhi-Ming Yu

items.title: International Space Station Captures the Eye of the Sahara
items.summary: The International Space Station photographed the Richat Structure, widely known as the Eye of the Sahara, from orbit on November 14, 2026. Located in Mauritania, this eroded geological dome formed approximately one hundred million years ago through a combination of igneous activity and regional uplift.
items.author: HQ Web Team
items.original_title: Eye of the Sahara
items.original_summary: The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in the nation of Mauritania.

items.title: Frozen Phonons on Dense $\mathbf{q}$-Grids Using Set Covers
items.summary: Phonon dynamics determine a vast number of properties in the solid state, such as the heat capacity, thermal expansion, and thermal conductivity. Phonons are obtained through the dynamical matrix, which, in the frozen phonon approach, is calculated as a finite difference derivative of the analytical Hellmann-Feynman force.
items.author: Sebastian Riis Thomsen

items.title: Blind spatially varying PSF estimation for fluorescence microscopy
items.summary: Optical aberrations degrade fluorescence microscopy images and measuring the underlying point spread function (PSF) often requires dedicated acquisitions or isolated emitters. Here we introduce DeepBlur, a neural network that estimates spatially varying two-dimensional PSFs directly from single images of biological structures.
items.author: Minh Hai Nguyen, Florian Sarron, Paul Escande et al.

items.title: Theory of Observability of Voigt-Wave Propagation in a Homogeneous Dielectric Material
items.summary: A Voigt wave can propagate in a dissipative anisotropic dielectric material when a 4$\times$4 propagation matrix is defective, as happens for a uniform plane wave along a singular axis, and the field depends on the propagation distance linearly as well as exponentially.
items.author: Akhlesh Lakhtakia, Tom G. Mackay

items.title: Arbitrarily Weak Losses Destroy Fractal Bandstructure in Temporal Fibonacci Quasicrystals
items.summary: Lossless photonic crystals with weak refractive index contrasts block limited frequencies. However, the same materials arranged in a non-periodic Fibonacci quasicrystal block all but infinitely rare fractally-distributed frequencies. Similar analysis shows that weak quasiperiodic refractive index variation in time should achieve infinitely broadband gain.
items.author: Calvin M. Hooper

items.title: Pipeline Uncovers Tumor Heterogeneity Drivers in Agent-Based Models
items.summary: Researchers introduced a likelihood-free discovery pipeline using approximate Bayesian computation, sequential Monte Carlo, and distributed random forests to uncover parameter combinations driving tumor heterogeneity in spatiotemporal agent-based models. Applied to breast cancer data, the method successfully identifies parameter relationships that reproduce target tissue dynamics.
items.author: Po-Hao Chiu, Jacob I. Evarts, Jason Y. Cain et al.
items.original_title: A discovery of emergent drivers pipeline uncovers parameter hierarchies in spatiotemporal agent-based tumor models
items.original_summary: Tumor heterogeneity is a confounding factor that stems from individual cell decisions, regulation among diverse cells, and regulation between these cells and the tumor microenvironment. Identifying cellular and microenvironmental factors that drive tumor heterogeneity is critical to effective therapeutic targeting.

items.title: Bulk2SC Generates Single-Cell RNA-Seq Data from Bulk RNA-Seq
items.summary: Scientists developed Bulk2SC, an innovative modular framework that leverages generative artificial intelligence and existing single-cell datasets to produce representative single-cell RNA sequencing data directly from abundant bulk RNA sequencing. This approach utilizes a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder to help overcome high sequencing costs and limited sample sizes.
items.author: Myles Kim, Corey M. Williams, Guangzhi Xiong et al.
items.original_title: Generating scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq using a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder
items.original_summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides detailed, genome-wide gene expression profiles at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of disease-driving cell types and genes. However, scRNA-seq remains costly, and there are extremely limited samples generated in even the most extensive human disease studies.

items.title: Contact-Network Responsiveness Atlas Maps Human Protein Structures
items.summary: Researchers created Contact-Network Responsiveness, a structure-derived framework converting residue-level protein coordinates into response descriptors. Analyzing thousands of human protein models revealed contact density baselines and systematic graph-dependent deviations, linking these descriptors to known disorder annotations and non-local contact availability within protein structures.
items.author: Ran Huang, Xin Ma, Dean Ta
items.original_title: A structure-derived contact-network responsiveness atlas of human proteins
items.original_summary: Protein structures encode non-local contact organization, but static coordinates do not directly quantify how a contact network responds when effective stabilizing interactions are strengthened or weakened. Here we introduce Contact-Network Responsiveness (CNR), a structure-derived framework that converts residue-level protein coordinates into density-controlled and topology-corrected response descriptors.

items.title: New Metric Reveals Missense Oncogenic Mutation Fitness Effects
items.summary: Researchers created a metric to quantify how selection biases observed missense variants in cancer driver genes. By estimating potential driver variants and fitness effects, they found most oncogene variants are already observed, whereas most tumor-suppressor variants remain undiscovered, highlighting differences in mutation and selection across gene classes.
items.author: Anastasia V. Stolyarova, Georgii A. Bazykin
items.original_title: Deviation from the neutral mutational spectrum in driver genes reveals the distribution of effects of missense oncogenic mutations
items.original_summary: Although many cancer driver genes have been identified, the full set of variants within these genes that can promote tumorigenesis remains unknown. The contribution of a variant to cancer depends on both its probability of occurrence and the selective advantage it confers.

items.title: Sec61-EMC Complex Drives SARS-CoV-2 Non-Structural Protein Biosynthesis
items.summary: Researchers discovered that SARS-CoV-2 utilizes the host Sec61-endoplasmic reticulum membrane complex to synthesize vital viral polyproteins. The complex specifically engages transmembrane protein NSP3 during translation, revealing an essential mechanism for viral replication and offering potential new targets for anti-SARS-CoV-2 therapeutic interventions.
items.author: Whitney Reid, Yu-Jie Chen, Jeffrey M. Williams et al.
items.original_title: The Sec61-EMC complex promotes biosynthesis of the SARS-CoV-2 non-structural proteins
items.original_summary: The genomic RNA of SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for the global COVID-19 pandemic, encodes polyproteins pp1a and pp1ab which contain 16 non-structural proteins (NSPs) that support critical steps in infection. Despite this, how the polyproteins are synthesized and membrane-inserted in the host cell is unclear.

items.title: Viral Infection and Barrier Disruption in Freshwater Prawns
items.summary: Researchers investigated how Decapod iridescent virus 1 affects the intestinal peritrophic matrix in giant freshwater prawns. Findings show that viral envelope proteins interact with host integrins and trigger signaling pathways that increase barrier permeability, contributing to tissue damage and higher infection severity.
items.author: Yijie Wu, Zhimin Lv, Qiang Yao et al.
items.original_title: Viral envelope protein engagement of host integrin signaling for intestinal peritrophic matrix disruption
items.original_summary: The intestinal peritrophic matrix (PM) is a chitin-rich barrier that protects arthropods from enteric pathogens, but how crustacean viruses alter this structure during infection remains poorly understood. In the giant freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii , Decapod iridescent virus 1 (DIV1) infection coincides with progressive changes in PM architecture and permeability.

items.summary: A recent study evaluated prenatal developmental toxicity in rats administered oral doses of defatted Lepidium sativum seed extract during gestation. Results revealed that higher doses caused significant embryonic morphological defects, developmental delays, low birth weights, and an increased incidence of stillbirths.

Therefore, this study evaluated the prenatal developmental toxicity of Lepidium sativum seeds in rats.

items.title: Evaluating Emodin Breast Cancer Gene Expression Signatures
items.summary: Scientists analyzed how comparator choice and data preprocessing affect public breast cancer emodin signatures using array datasets. The results demonstrate that while active compound genes are partially retained, low overlap and weak genome-wide recurrence indicate that observational patient data cannot confirm emodin treatment efficacy.
items.author: Liang Cai, Quanlei Wang, Jingxian Cao et al.
items.original_title: Control choice and reproducibility of dataset-specific emodin expression signatures in breast cancer

We examined the dependence of breast cancer emodin signatures on comparator choice and preprocessing, using 212 GSE85871 arrays and a fixed 77-gene signature from two emodin arrays compared with other active compounds.

items.title: Monitoring Tailings Dam Failure Using InSAR Technology
items.summary: Researchers utilized Small Baseline Subset Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar technology and an improved displacement tangent angle method to monitor deformation at the Tonglüshan tailings dam. The analysis successfully identified distinct stages of dam movement, linked precipitation and underground collapse to deformation, and established effective safety monitoring techniques.

The safety issues of tailings dams have emerged as significant potential hazards that affect the ecological environment, human life and property.

items.title: Dietary Diversity and Cognitive Impairment in Older Adults
items.summary: A longitudinal cohort study tracked dietary diversity trajectories among older Chinese adults from 2008 to 2018. Using group-based trajectory modeling, researchers found that participants maintaining moderate or high dietary diversity experienced a significantly lower risk of developing cognitive impairment compared to those in low stability groups.
items.author: Zheng Shao, Zhiying Chen, Shiyi Xu et al.

Methods This study used longitudinal data from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS) collected between 2008 and 2018, including 2455 participants.

items.title: New 2.5D Framework Enhances Coronary Artery Calcification Segmentation
items.summary: Researchers proposed a 2.5D segmentation framework that improves coronary artery calcification analysis on computed tomography scans by integrating a multi-slice feature fusion module into standard networks. The approach successfully captures essential inter-slice continuity without full volumetric processing, yielding better accuracy and competitive inference times.
items.author: Sun-Woo Pi, Jun-Hyeon Sim, Byoung-Dai Lee
items.original_title: Segmentation of sparse coronary artery calcifications in computed tomography via 2.5D multi-slice feature fusion
items.original_summary: Objective Accurate segmentation of coronary artery calcification (CAC) on computed tomography (CT) is critical for reliable cardiovascular risk assessment but remains challenging due to the small and sparse nature of calcified lesions. Although 3D models improve inter-slice consistency, their computational and memory demands motivate alternatives for high-resolution CT segmentation.

items.title: Kidney Function Declines Linked to Heart Failure Therapy Changes
items.summary: A retrospective study of heart failure patients evaluated the impact of guideline-directed medical therapy on kidney function. Findings reveal that estimated glomerular filtration rate declines of twenty percent or more following treatment initiation are associated with a significantly higher likelihood of medication discontinuation or dose reduction.
items.author: Carine E. Hamo, Nathalia Ladino, Yunan Zhao et al.
items.original_title: Discontinuation or downtitration of guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure after changes in kidney function
items.original_summary: Background Initiation of guideline directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) can cause acute declines in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) that are often reversible and clinically inconsequential yet may prompt premature therapy discontinuation.

items.title: Study Compares Chlorine-Based Irrigants and EDTA in Root Canal Cleaning
items.summary: An in vitro study examined root canal irrigation protocols using sodium hypochlorite or hypochlorous acid, combined with ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid. Results showed that neither chlorine-based irrigant removed the smear layer effectively without a chelator, supporting traditional sodium hypochlorite and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid sequences.
items.author: Nuria Simo, Ana Paredes, Álvaro Villanueva et al.
items.original_title: Effects of hypochlorous acid and sodium hypochlorite irrigation protocols, used alone or combined with ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, on root canal dentin: An in vitro study
items.original_summary: Objective This in vitro study evaluated the effect of irrigation protocols based on 5.25% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) or 200 ppm hypochlorous acid (HOCl), used alone or combined with 17% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), on smear layer removal, open dentinal tubules and erosion of root canal dentin.

items.title: Trial Evaluates Active and Passive Therapy for Older Hip Fracture Patients
items.summary: Researchers outline a randomized controlled trial protocol comparing active resistance training and passive neuromuscular electrical stimulation against standard care for older adults recovering from hip fractures. The study aims to address venous thromboembolism and muscle atrophy while gathering qualitative data on patient experiences.
items.author: Haowei Du, Xin Chen, Minghui Wang et al.
items.original_title: “Mind or machine?”: Study protocol for a mixed-methods study evaluating the effectiveness and lived experience of active versus passive prophylaxis in older hip fracture patients
items.original_summary: Background Hip fracture in older adults causes a “dual crisis” of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and rapid muscle atrophy. Pharmacological prevention is effective but carries significant bleeding risks for these frail patients. Current physical prophylaxis is often too weak to restore muscle pump function.
items.ai_title: Trial Evaluates Active and Passive Therapy for Older Hip Fracture Patients
items.ai_summary: Researchers outline a randomized controlled trial protocol comparing active resistance training and passive neuromuscular electrical stimulation against standard care for older adults recovering from hip fractures. The study aims to address venous thromboembolism and muscle atrophy while gathering qualitative data on patient experiences.

Administer the respective active or passive rehabilitation interventions during the recovery period.
Assess primary outcomes such as ultrasound-confirmed venous thromboembolism and secondary hemodynamic metrics.

items.title: Optimization of a Locally Shielded 16-Channel Transmit Array for Human Brain MRI at 10.5 T via Electromagnetic/Circuit Co-Simulation and Parallel Transmission Strategies
items.summary: Modern neuroimaging and neuroscience increasingly demand high spatial and temporal resolution, driving the use of ultrahigh-field (7 T and above) MRI for improved signal-to-noise ratio. Realizing this advantage depends critically on advanced radiofrequency (RF) and gradient technologies, particularly multi-channel transmit arrays and high-performance head-gradient systems.
items.author: Mengxuan Zheng, Xin Shao, Matt Waks et al.

items.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
items.summary: We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted.
items.author: Mihály A. Csirik

items.title: Search-for-Gradient: Search-Based Restarts for Optimisation in Structured Flat Landscapes of Variational Quantum Algorithms
items.summary: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a promising class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms that involve parameterised quantum circuits and classical optimisation. VQAs have found applications in simulation, optimisation, and machine learning. However, their scalability is hindered by flat landscapes-regions in the parameter space where gradients vanish exponentially small.
items.author: Subham Das, Bikash K. Behera, Andrés Camilo Granda Arango et al.

items.title: Ancilla-Assisted Accelerated Readout of Transmon Qubits
items.summary: We present a scheme for accelerating dispersive readout of superconducting transmon qubits. Dispersive readout works by weakly coupling the target transmon to a resonator, such that the resonator experiences a state-dependent frequency shift, which can then be read out. Our scheme introduces an ancillary transmon coupled to the same resonator.
items.author: Christopher Corlett, Noah Linden, Paul Skrzypczyk

items.title: Coefficient-Range Mitigation on an 8-Bit Coherent Ising Machine
items.summary: Mapping optimization problems to the restricted coefficient range of an 8-bit CIM can distort their encoded energy landscapes. We investigate whether three coefficient-range mitigation techniques previously studied for quantum annealing---interaction extension, bounded-coefficient encoding, and augmented Lagrangian penalties---improve end-to-end optimization outcomes.
items.author: Manuel Radons, Lars Simon, Raoul Heese et al.

items.title: Pseudospin-mediated broadband hypersonic phonon transport beyond localized Berry curvature
items.summary: Phononic nanostructures offer compact and highly confined control of elastic waves for signal transport, filtering, and quantum transduction. More recently, topological phononic structures have been explored as a route to robust waveguiding around defects and sharp bends, offering a promising basis for scalable and reliable phononic circuitry.
items.author: Byunggi Kim, Michele Diego, Yohei Ogawara et al.

items.title: Remote and Noncontact Acceleration and Suppression of Heat Convection on Object Surfaces using Intensity-Adjusted Acoustic Streaming
items.summary: The temperature of objects in an environment is often controlled by accelerating or suppressing heat convection. Conventional methods generally involve insulation for heat retention and forced convection for cooling. However, there is no practical method for remotely and target-selectively controlling heat convection in objects in room environments.
items.author: Yuki Yuzawa, Keisuke Hasegawa

items.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
items.summary: Clients of closed-weight LLM APIs cannot verify whether a provider ran the advertised model, precision, hidden prompt, and reasoning budget. Existing approaches either trust hardware or third parties, or re-prove every layer of an integer surrogate at high cost while diverging from native floating-point serving.
items.author: Liang Song

items.title: Verifiable but Not Predictable: What Sentence Embeddings Know About Propositional Decomposition
items.summary: Quality control for proposition decomposition by large language models (LLMs) raises two asymmetric questions. After decomposition, one can verify: given a sentence and a candidate proposition, does the proposition belong to that sentence? Before decomposition, one would like to predict: how many propositions should the sentence yield?
items.author: Qingan Li, Tianxiao Wu, Xiling Cui

items.title: Strong 5.9 Magnitude Quake Hits Balleny Islands Area
items.summary: A strong magnitude 5.9 earthquake was documented in the Balleny Islands region on November 25, 2026. The seismic event took place at a depth of approximately ten kilometers. items.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations.
items.author: Masahiro Tadokoro, Tetsuo Kodera

items.title: Single-dose neonatal gene therapy preserves motor coordination and extends survival of Polg-deficient mice
items.summary: POLG mutations are the most common single nuclear gene cause of mitochondrial disease. POLG disease spans a spectrum of clinical presentations with variable age of onset and severity. Early-onset disease is often severe and fatal (e.g., Alpers syndrome, myocerebrohepatopathy), while late-onset disease can be relatively mild (e.g., progressive external ophthalmoplegia).
items.author: Zanin, S., Moriceau, S., Afram, E. et al.

items.title: FastHer: a fast and accurate estimator of local heritability from summary statistics
items.summary: We present FastHer, a method for estimating local heritability using GWAS summary statistics and linkage disequilibrium (LD) matrices. FastHer performs exact restricted maximum-likelihood estimation matching the accuracy of individual-level methods. Analytical transformations ensure high computational efficiency. FastHer incorporates SNP weights that define the contribution of each SNP to heritability.
items.author: Svishcheva, G. R., Tsepilov, Y. A., Axenovich, T. I.

items.title: Convergent Genomic Signatures of Selection in Thar: Genetic trade-offs for desert survival
items.summary: Background: Desert environments provide a setting for natural biological experiments to cope up with simultaneous stressors of extreme temperatures, aridity, UV exposure, and limited food resources. Biological adaptations that support living in such an environment could become liabilities when the environment and lifestyle change due to gene-environment mismatch.
items.author: Rathod, S. M., Jain, R., Mukerji, M.

items.title: Auxin and cytokinin antagonistically regulate Arabidopsis root distal stem cell fate through opposing pairs of HD-Zip II transcription factors
items.summary: The antagonistic action of auxin (IAA) and cytokinin (CK) regulates several aspects of plant development including stem cell specification and maintenance. In the Arabidopsis thaliana root, the fate of distal stem cells (DSCs) is mainly regulated by IAA, while the function of CK is still ill-defined.
items.author: Sessa, G., Possenti, M., Brozzi, I. et al.

items.title: Structured stabilization in recurrent neural circuits through inhibitory synaptic plasticity
items.summary: In cortical circuits, inhibitory interneurons play a dual role: they regulate overall activity levels to prevent runaway excitation, and contribute to diverse computations. While unstructured inhibitory synaptic connections achieve the first role by homeostatically regulating firing rates, computational tasks often require structured excitatory-inhibitory (E/I) connectivity.
items.author: Festa, D., Cusseddu, C., Gjorgjieva, J.

items.title: Common excluder barley has more than one mechanism to remove Cd from chloroplasts.
items.summary: Chloroplasts comprise photosynthesis and other important processes. Plants protect chloroplasts from stresses including Cd accumulation. Common terrestrial plants, excluders apply a set of mechanisms to restrict Cd penetration to chloroplasts. Removal of accumulated Cd from chloroplasts should also be a beneficial strategy.
items.author: Lysenko, E. A., Seregina, I. F., Klaus, A. A. et al.

items.title: Dysregulated SETX activity at R-loops links transcriptional and splicing alterations to compromised neuronal identity in ALS4
items.summary: RNA dysregulation is an increasingly recognized driver of neurodegenerative diseases, yet the mechanisms linking defects in RNA metabolism to selective neuronal vulnerability remain poorly understood. Alterations in R-loop homeostasis have been observed in neurodegeneration, but it is unclear how these contribute to neuronal dysfunction.
items.author: Giannini, M., Gostan, T., El Aabidine, A. Z. et al.

items.title: Pollinator specificity among three co-flowering Mediterranean Aristolochia species pollinated by Diptera
items.summary: Attracting species-specific pollinators can be favoured by natural selection to avoid reproductive interference between sympatric plant species. However, the ways in which fine differences in floral traits lead to the attraction of species-specific pollinators are diverse and unknown in most pollination interactions.
items.author: Vrecko, V., Lapeyre, B., Buatois, B. et al.

items.title: A spatially patterned Gdf15 response links maladaptive nephron remodeling to polyuria during toxic exposure
items.summary: Lithium impairs renal water conservation and induces microcystic remodeling. Whether these functional and structural complications of treatment share a common mechanism is unknown. Using high-definition spatial transcriptomics, we identify renal growth differentiation factor 15 (Gdf15) induction in vivo along a corticopapillary gradient paralleling lithium accumulation.
items.author: Zerarga, L., Himbert, M., Try, M. et al.

items.title: Space-based and object-based saccadic selection in visual working memory
items.summary: Saccades made during memory maintenance prioritize memory for the saccade target, but it is unclear if this benefit is specific to a location or extends across memorized objects. In three experiments, we examined whether saccadic selection spreads to other locations within the same object.
items.author: Shurygina, O., Wirth, L. A., Rolfs, M. et al.

items.title: Development of microsatellite markers with the SSRseq method on Glossina palpalis gambiensis, and G. p. palpalis, and analysis of corresponding field samples from three sleeping sickness foci: Boffa, Dubreka (Guinea), and Bonon (Cote d'Ivoire).
items.summary: Tsetse flies are strictly found is sub-Saharan Africa where they are responsible for the transmission and maintenance of African trypanosomiases in humans (HAT) and animals (AAT). Vector control has been recognized as an essential tool to fight against these diseases.
items.author: DE MEEUS, T., Ravel, S., Kagbadouno, M. et al.

items.title: Transcriptomic-Methylation Integration and Machine-Learning Prioritization of Candidate Prognostic Biomarkers in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: A Retrospective Computational Study
items.summary: Background: Triple-negative breast cancer is molecularly heterogeneous, complicating prognostic stratification. We aimed to derive a gene panel and clinical-genomic survival nomogram and assess cross-platform performance. Methods: This retrospective computational study analyzed The Cancer Genome Atlas breast cancer data, identifying 197 primary-tumor transcriptomic aliquots from 190 patients.
items.author: MANNEKUNTA, N., NATRAJAN, E.

items.title: Developmental timeline of the lateral olfactory tract innervation of piriform cortex
items.summary: The development of the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) begins embryonically and is closely linked to the differentiation of olfactory bulb (OB) projection neurons, mitral and tufted cells, whose axons form the LOT. Here, we implemented calretinin (CR) as a proxy to characterize LOT development.
items.author: Martin-Lopez, E., Li, H., Spence, N. J. et al.

items.title: Sex differences in corticostriatal regulation of alcohol drinking following chronic intermittent alcohol exposure
items.summary: Researchers investigated the neural circuits regulating alcohol intake in males and females after chronic intermittent alcohol exposure. They found that activity in certain neurons constrained alcohol intake in males but not females, highlighting the need for sex-informed therapies for alcohol use disorder.
items.author: Hewitt, K. A., Nicholson, S. E., Logan, D. et al.
items.original_title: Sex differences in corticostriatal regulation of alcohol drinking following chronic intermittent alcohol exposure
items.original_summary: Background: Sex differences in alcohol use disorder (AUD) suggest that the neural circuits regulating alcohol intake may differ between males and females. We examined whether infralimbic neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens shell (IL-NAcSh) regulate alcohol self-administration and anxiety-related behavior following chronic intermittent alcohol (CIA) exposure.
items.ai_title: Sex differences in corticostriatal regulation of alcohol drinking following chronic intermittent alcohol exposure
items.ai_summary: Researchers investigated the neural circuits regulating alcohol intake in males and females after chronic intermittent alcohol exposure. They found that activity in certain neurons constrained alcohol intake in males but not females, highlighting the need for sex-informed therapies for alcohol use disorder.

items.title: Supplier-associated variation in motor performance and cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neuron anatomy in C57BL/6 mice
items.summary: Cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs) are an evolutionarily conserved population of spinal sensory neurons positioned around the central canal and characterized by expression of the ion channel PKD2L1. CSF-cNs contribute to locomotor control, but little is known about variation in this sensory system among commonly used laboratory mouse populations.
items.author: Luther, M. J., Stanchak, K. E., Perkel, D. J.

items.title: Mitochondrial Lon protease couples substrate translocation to proteolytic activation.
items.summary: Human LonP1 is an ATP-dependent mitochondrial protease that degrades damaged or redundant proteins. Indiscriminate proteolysis by LonP1 is limited through tight coordination of substrate recognition, unfolding, translocation, and catalytic cleavage, yet the role of ATP hydrolysis in these individual steps remains unclear.
items.author: Schenck N, Ahrensback Roesgaard M, Abrahams JP.

items.title: Autoimmunity after immunization: a case of insulin resistance due to insulin antibodies following COVID-19 vaccination.
items.summary: Autoimmune insulin resistance due to insulin autoantibodies (IAAs) is a rare phenomenon. Exogenous insulin autoimmune syndrome, a type of autoimmune insulin resistance triggered by exogenous insulin, has been reported after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection or vaccination, starting days to weeks after the event.
items.author: Chaudhry Z, Harber I, Variar V, Rene J, Habib Z.

items.title: Successful treatment of symptomatic locally recurrent unresectable pheochromocytoma with percutaneous ablations.
items.summary: Metastatic or locally recurrent pheochromocytomas (PCCs) present significant therapeutic challenges, particularly in patients with symptomatic or progressive disease. Current treatment options, apart from surgery, are predominantly palliative. Minimally invasive percutaneous ablative techniques have emerged as promising treatment modalities for selected patients with unresectable or metastatic PCCs.
items.author: Diaz Perez R, Marty CD, Kis B, Hallanger-Johnson J, Tarasova VD.

items.title: Pituitary Hyperplasia Mimicking a Macroadenoma
items.summary: A 39-year-old woman with autoimmune primary hypothyroidism developed pituitary hyperplasia mimicking a macroadenoma, which was initially misdiagnosed as a macroadenoma. The condition was caused by pseudomalabsorption due to Helicobacter pylori infection, and was treated with levothyroxine, resulting in normalization of pituitary hormone levels and resolution of the hyperplasia.
items.author: Maschietto Boff L, Molina GM, Francisco SM, Marui S, Padula M, Glezer A.
items.original_title: Pituitary hyperplasia mimicking a macroadenoma in refractory primary hypothyroidism due to pseudomalabsorption.
items.original_summary: Pituitary enlargement is often attributed to an adenoma, yet reactive hyperplasia can produce a sellar mass indistinguishable from a macroadenoma on imaging. We describe a 39-year-old woman with 19 years of autoimmune primary hypothyroidism, never biochemically controlled despite levothyroxine dose escalation.

items.ai_summary: A 39-year-old woman with autoimmune primary hypothyroidism developed pituitary hyperplasia mimicking a macroadenoma, which was initially misdiagnosed as a macroadenoma. The condition was caused by pseudomalabsorption due to Helicobacter pylori infection, and was treated with levothyroxine, resulting in normalization of pituitary hormone levels and resolution of the hyperplasia.

items.title: Management of type 1 diabetes with iLet while receiving peritoneal dialysis.
items.summary: Glycemic management in patients with diabetes complicated by end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) with dextrose-based dialysates presents unique challenges. Thus far, there are limited data on how to effectively manage hyperglycemia and minimize risk of hypoglycemia in this population.
items.author: Gu C, Ishola A, Caldwell J, Brady B, Tan M.

items.title: A unique case of pregnancy-induced parathyroid hormone hypersecretion with severe recurrent refractory hypercalcemia.
items.summary: A 30-year-old woman presented at 24 weeks of gestation with severe hypercalcemia (albumin-adjusted calcium, 19.20 mg/dL [4.79 mmol/L]; reference range, 8.30-10.22 mg/dL [2.07-2.55 mmol/L]) with very high parathyroid hormone (PTH; 292 pg/mL [31 pmol/L], reference range, 15-65 pg/mL [1.6-6.9 pmol/L]) refractory to conservative treatment.
items.author: Nicolas N, Dandurand K, Fortier PH, Roy-Lacroix MÈ, Sauvé N, Carpentier AC.

items.title: A microexon confers functional divergence of the actin nucleator Arp2/3.
items.summary: Actin-related protein (Arp2), a subunit within the actin nucleator Arp2/3, encodes two splice variants that differ by five residues in the D-loop, a critical element for catalyzing actin polymerization. It is unknown if this alternative exon, or "microexon," impacts Arp2/3 function.
items.author: Powell J, Palafox MS, Schroeder CM.

items.title: Pulmonary embolism and pulmonary infarction triggered by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia during physical restraint in a psychiatric inpatient: A case report.
items.summary: Background Psychiatric inpatients have a high risk of venous thromboembolism because of physical restraint, reduced mobility, and sedation. Although subcutaneous unfractionated heparin (UFH) may be used for thromboprophylaxis during physical restraint, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) can occur even during prophylaxis and remains underrecognized.
items.author: Inaguma T, Maruyama J, Amemiya K, Sugihara T, Fukuda Y, Shimada M.

items.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Semaglutide and Tirzepatide Versus Metformin for Adults on Antipsychotics.
items.summary: Objective Evidence for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1s) to treat antipsychotic-associated weight gain is limited. A comparison of 52-week weight loss with semaglutide/tirzepatide versus metformin in adults taking antipsychotics was conducted using nationwide electronic health record data. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Truveta database.
items.author: Chao AM, Wu M, Tong J, Levy J, Allsop K, Ghobadi K, Daumit G, Slade EP.

items.title: A case of dissociative disorder with attenuation of EEG alpha power during a depersonalization episode.
items.summary: Background Dissociative disorders are characterized by disruptions in consciousness, memory, identity, and perception. Similar symptoms can occur in patients with frontal lobe epilepsy. Although dissociative disorders are generally classified as psychiatric conditions, several studies have reported electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities in only a small proportion of affected patients.
items.author: Kato T, Soga K, Sakuma K, Mizuno M.

items.title: Anti-Reflection Coatings for Highly Anisotropic Materials in the Mid Infrared.
items.summary: We develop and optimize thin anti-reflection coatings (ARCs) for highly anisotropic materials in the mid infrared. Unlike conventional ARCs that assume nearly isotropic refractive indices for the substrate being coated, this work fully integrates the anisotropic nature of all materials into the design process.
items.author: Mei H, Cho JW, Yu JS, Chen H, Singh S, Zhao B, Ravichandran J, Kim SK, Kats MA.

items.title: Multisectoral Collaboration in Partnership With the Community in Promoting Health Equity.
items.summary: This article examines the indispensable role of multisectoral collaboration (MSC) in advancing health equity through community health models. Despite significant advancements in healthcare, persistent health disparities, rooted in the social determinants of health (SDOH), necessitate a shift from reactive care to proactive, integrated approaches.
items.author: Edward M, Tibenderana J, Peter IH, Musa J, Stephen Gwimile M.

items.title: What Drives Minimum Dietary Diversity Among Children Aged 6-23 Months in Bangladesh? Socioeconomic Inequality, Spatial Variation, and Policy Insights From a Multilevel and Decomposition Analysis of the 2022 BDHS.
items.summary: Background Minimum dietary diversity (MDD) is a critical indicator of complementary feeding quality, yet socioeconomic and geographic disparities remain poorly understood in Bangladesh. This study examined the prevalence, determinants, inequality, and spatial variation of MDD among children aged 6-23 months using the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS).
items.author: Hossain MM, Alam R, Jahan I, Rabab AF, Hasan MDS, Bushra T, Sultana S, Haque MA, Rois R.

items.title: Unhealthy Dietary Practices Among Children in Bangladesh: A Growing Concern
items.summary: Unhealthy dietary practices among Bangladeshi children aged 6-23 months are prevalent, with 31.8% consuming sweet beverages, 49.84% eating unhealthy foods, and 44.63% having zero vegetable or fruit intake. Mixed-effects logistic regression found associations with maternal education, media exposure, and breastfeeding.
items.author: Turin HM, Alam MI.
items.original_title: Unhealthy Dietary Practices Among the Children in Bangladesh: An Analysis of Cross-Sectional Data.
items.original_summary: This study examined the prevalence and determinants of unhealthy dietary practices among Bangladeshi children aged 6-23 months using data from the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey 2022. Three outcomes were assessed: sweet beverage consumption, unhealthy food intake and zero vegetable or fruit consumption.

items.title: Real-World Treatment Trajectories and Outcomes in Adult Secondary Hemophagocytic Lympho-Histiocytosis Identified Through Bone Marrow Hemophagocytosis.
items.summary: Introduction Adult secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) remains a diagnostically complex syndrome with heterogeneous triggers and treatment strategies. Methods We performed a retrospective observational cohort study of adult patients with HLH identified through a hematology laboratory database of bone marrow aspirates showing hemophagocytosis at a tertiary university hospital (2014-2019).
items.author: Allemand A, Martel N, Fauter M, Fiscus J, Woestelandt S, Dumas C, Seve P, Jamilloux Y.

items.title: Self-Care Practices and Influencing Factors Among Adults With Diabetes Mellitus in Rural Vhembe District, South Africa: A Qualitative Study.
items.summary: Introduction Diabetes mellitus remains a major public health challenge in South Africa, with rising mortality and complications despite the availability of effective self-care strategies. This study explored and described self-care practices and influencing factors among adults with diabetes in rural Vhembe district.
items.author: Mmapula HE, Stella MN.

items.title: Molecular epidemiology of ESBL and carbapenemase genes in clinical Shigella isolates from Uzbekistan.
items.summary: Background No contemporary data exist on extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)- or carbapenemase-producing Shigella from Uzbekistan, a high-burden Central Asian setting. We characterized the prevalence of 8 clinically important resistance genes in 49 clinical Shigella isolates from 4 Uzbekistani regions and contextualized isolates within a global phylogenetic framework.
items.author: Yodgorova NT, Abdurakhimov AA, Rakhmatullaev AI, Komilov NO, Ismailova GA, Fayzullaeva ZR, Abdullaeva DG, Sharipova ZO, Nematov AS, Nuruzova ZA.

items.title: A Narrative Review on Cleft Lip and/or Palate: Epidemiology, Burden, Outcome Measurement and the Imperative for a Region-Specific Utility Index in Ghana.
items.summary: Globally, cleft lip and/or palate (CL/P) affects 4.6 million people. CL/P occurs in approximately 1.4 per 1000 live births, making it one of the most prevalent congenital craniofacial anomalies. Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is no exception, with cleft accounting for 13.11 disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) per 100,000 population.
items.author: Okyere Boadu KA, Frimpong P, Danquah EPB, Okyere Boadu R, Agyei-Baffour P.

items.title: Georgia's Fertility Decline Raises Concerns About Population Aging and Public Health
items.summary: Georgia's birth rate has declined, raising concerns about population aging, workforce contraction, and public health sustainability. Multiple factors, including delayed parenthood and changing gender roles, are contributing to this trend. Addressing the issue will require comprehensive policies that extend beyond financial incentives.
items.author: Zhonzholadze L, Nadareishvili I.
items.original_title: Georgia's Fertility Decline: A Public Health Challenge With Global Relevance.
items.original_summary: Georgia, a country in the Caucasus region, is experiencing a sustained decline in birth rates, raising concerns about population aging, workforce contraction, and long-term public health sustainability. In 2025, the country recorded its lowest number of live births since 1994, whereas deaths have exceeded births since 2020.

items.title: Efficacy of radionuclide therapy in the treatment of inoperable or metastatic pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
items.summary: Context Inoperable or metastatic pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PC/PGL) present a management challenge with high variability in response to systemic therapies. The aim of this study was to assess the efficacy and toxicity of 2 therapeutic radiopharmaceutical agents: iodine-131 metaiodobenzylguanine and lutetium-177 DOTA-octreotate.
items.author: Seabrook A, Chan D, Hsiao E, Roach P, Bernard E, Clifton-Bligh R.

items.title: Services domestic regulation disciplines enter into force for Kazakhstan
items.summary: On 25 November, Kazakhstan notified WTO members that, following conclusion of its domestic approval procedures, the disciplines on services domestic regulation had taken legal effect and had been incorporated into Kazakhstan's schedule under the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) as of 27 October 2026.

items.summary: Ensemble-based methods provide a practical framework for history matching, prediction, and optimization of subsurface models. In methodological studies, however, performance is rarely assessed from a single run. Comparisons typically span cases, configurations, and random seeds, while each evaluation may require an expensive external simulator.

items.title: Physics-Based TCAD Modeling of Nanowire Cryotrons with Coupled Superconducting and Thermal Dynamics
items.summary: Nanowire cryotrons (nTrons) provide gate-controlled superconducting switching, current gain, and high-impedance outputs for cryogenic computing, detector readout, and superconductor-semiconductor interfaces. We develop a physics-based Sentaurus TCAD framework that couples time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau dynamics, separate electron and phonon energy equations, and mixed-mode circuit simulation.

items.title: Thanksgiving Travel Disrupted by Coastal Storms and Pacific Systems
items.summary: Millions of holiday travelers across the United States face major weather disruptions. A powerful coastal storm impacts the eastern half of the country, while a Pacific system brings rain and mountain snow to the western region. Meanwhile, a developing autumn storm produces scattered showers and thunderstorms across the Southeast.

Here’s your Thanksgiving week forecast from NOAA’s Weather Prediction Center : Wednesday: Storms on the horizon A developing autumn storm will bring scattered showers and a few thunderstorms across the lower Mississippi Valley and Southeast for the busy pre-Thanksgiving travel day.

items.title: Amateur Astronomers Join NASA Network to Detect Kilonovas
items.summary: Amateur astronomers with telescopes and cameras are joining NASA's Kilonova Catcher network to help locate fleeting cosmic events. Volunteers track rapid flashes of light caused by colliding neutron stars and other cosmic phenomena, working alongside professional researchers to contribute valuable data for peer-reviewed scientific studies.
items.original_title: Amateur Astronomer? Be a Kilonova Catcher!
items.original_summary: Neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars. When they collide, they can release a brief flash of light called a kilonova. These immensely powerful events forge much of the universe’s gold, platinum and other heavy elements. Since a kilonova fades within days, astronomers have to find it fast, and no single observatory […]

items.title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission Overview
items.summary: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft.
items.author: Joseph Zakrzewski

items.title: OmniAct Policy Enables Cross-Embodiment Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Researchers introduced OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that adapts robot behavior based on specific kinematics and scenes. By training across one million simulated robot embodiments, the system successfully controls diverse hardware configurations, outperforming existing baselines in both simulated tasks and unseen real-world environments.
items.author: Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Jiayuan Yan et al.
items.original_title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
items.original_summary: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies.

items.title: Realizing Topological Insulators on Fractal Lattices
items.summary: Researchers successfully realized canonical topological insulators across various dimensional fractal lattices using site elimination, projection, and spatial patterning approaches. By computing topological invariants and analyzing gapless boundary modes, the team established topological phases on fractal structures such as the Cantor set, hexaflake, Sierpiński carpet, and Menger sponge.
items.author: Aiden Mains, Danile Salib, Christopher Leong et al.
items.original_title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
items.original_summary: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions.

items.title: The double copy and perturbative teleparallel gravity
items.summary: In this paper we analyze the double copy between gluon and graviton amplitudes within the context of teleparallel gravity. We first set up an effective Lagrangian based on minimal assumptions which reproduces the on-shell amplitudes stemming from the double-copy procedure.
items.author: Georg Stettinger

items.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
items.summary: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints.
items.author: Xingjian Ran, Xiaoye Mo, Sihao Liu et al.

items.title: VENUS: A Census of Strong Lensing in a 60-Cluster JWST Survey
items.summary: We present strong-lensing models for the 57 galaxy clusters observed in Cycle 4 out of the 60 targeted by the JWST Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS) program. Models for the remaining three clusters will be incorporated after their observations.
items.author: Joseph F. V. Allingham, Lukas J. Furtak, Miriam Golubchik et al.

items.title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
items.summary: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass.
items.author: Oleg Andreev

items.title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability
items.summary: The search for quantum advantage in average-case problems is a pressing open question in physics and computer science. The widest conjectured example of such an advantage is in simulation of quantum many-body systems, where sign problems and entanglement growth cause the breakdown of many classical methods.
items.author: Matthew Ding, Robbie King, Thomas Schuster

items.title: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From $π^0\toγγ$ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum
items.summary: We review the chiral anomaly from a historical perspective, from the $π^0\toγγ$ puzzle and the work of Adler, Bell and Jackiw, to the Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term. We then describe how the WZW term was motivated from quantum chromodynamics in 1983-85.
items.author: Spenta R. Wadia

items.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation. We present \textsc{MetaFORGE}, an execution-grounded meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes persistent natural-language skill specifications for MPI C code generation.
items.author: Scott Piersall, Yang Gao, Shenyang Liu et al.

items.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
items.summary: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock. However, time pressure is a major determinant of human decision-making quality, and temporal state is a missing dimension of human behavioral modeling.
items.author: Victor Dziwniel, Tianxiang Lu

items.title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks
items.summary: Can randomly parameterized neural environments supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm? We investigate this question using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework, replacing human-designed training games with sixteen selected neural environments. Each game combines bounded vector dynamics with a random strategy-based reward and an independent outcome reward.
items.author: Octave Gaspard

items.title: CANON: Agent-Assisted Construction of Canonical Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals
items.summary: The construction of canonical basis is an important procedure in the calculation of multi-loop Feynman integrals via the canonical differential equation methods. Currently, there are various different methods for this purpose. Among them, no single method is universally applicable. Thus, obtaining a valid basis often requires repeated attempts and verification.
items.author: Dong-shan Jian, Yuanche Liu, Yan-qing Ma et al.

items.title: A model colloidal gel former for the measurement of inter-particle forces
items.summary: Tracking of particle coordinates in colloidal model systems is an established technique. Recently, an emulsion system has been introduced where not only the coordinates, but also contacts and compressive forces between the droplets can be determined [Dong et al. J.
items.author: Rui Cheng, Kristian Thijssen, Abraham Mauleon Amieva et al.

items.title: Anharmonic enhancement of thermal conductivity in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$: A consistent picture from molecular dynamics and Wigner transport
items.summary: Anharmonicity limits heat conduction in crystals, but its role in amorphous solids, where heat is carried mainly by tunneling between quasi-degenerate vibrations, remains unsettled. Here we disentangle the contributions of structural disorder, quantum statistics, and anharmonicity to the thermal conductivity of amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (aGST), the prototypical phase-change memory material.
items.author: Luiz Felipe C. Pereira, Kamil Iwanowski, Michele Simoncelli et al.

items.title: Holographic ensembles and giant gravitons at the Leigh--Strassler fixed point
items.summary: Finite-rank observables in holographic quantum field theories provide stringent tests of string and M-theory, but remain challenging to compute when supersymmetry is non-maximal. In this paper, we study the finite rank partition function of the $\mathcal N=1$ Leigh-Strassler CFT, which admits an interacting Fermi-gas description.
items.author: Jesse van Muiden, De-liang Zhong

items.title: Finite-Temperature Superradiant Criticality and Thermal Emission in the Open Dicke Model
items.summary: Near the superradiant phase transition of the Dicke model, the lowest-frequency excitation softens and its losses can no longer be treated as a weak perturbation. We develop a finite-temperature theory of this transition in the open system, with no restriction on the strength of the system-bath coupling.
items.author: Gabriele Orlando, Samuel Napoli, Salvatore Savasta et al.

items.title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI
items.summary: Progress in embodied foundation models is largely measured by task success, while the physical safety of their decisions remains underexamined. Safety evaluations centered on rule following and binary judgments do not adequately assess whether embodied models understand environmental hazards and make safe decisions.
items.author: Erfei Cui, Shengjia Zhao, Yan Qin et al.

items.title: Polynomial Master Equations of Open Quantum Systems and an Analysis on the Critical Solutions
items.summary: The dynamics of open quantum systems exhibits in general a non-Markovian behavior, lying typically beyond the description of first-order differential equations. Traditional methods commonly turned to first-order integro-differential equations, which allowed for the standard interpretation of non-Markovianity as having its origin in the global history of the system evolution.
items.author: Miku Ishizaki, Jaeha Lee

items.title: Z-Boson Production in Proton-Lead Collisions with MRW Nuclear TMDs
items.summary: The production of dileptons in proton-lead collisions probes the transverse-momentum structure of partons in a nuclear environment. We summarize a $k_t$-factorization study of $Z$ boson production at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16\,\mathrm{TeV}$, comparing transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions constructed with leading-order and Next-to-leading-order Martin-Ryskin-Watt (LO-MRW and NLO-MRW) prescriptions.
items.author: S. Rezaie, K. Azizi

items.title: Nanoparticles with a BANG: Detonation-Driven Synthesis of Metals and Metal Oxides
items.summary: Bristol Accelerated Nanoparticle Generation (BANG) method is a solvent- and capping-agent-free nanoparticle synthesis. Previous work was limited mostly to gold, silver and copper particles. Here, the method is extended to ten further elements, including Pb, Bi, Tl, Mn, Fe, Zn, Pt, Ni, Cd and Pd.
items.author: Jan Maurycy Uszko, Robert Matyáš, Naoto Shirahata et al.

items.title: Multi-Component Axion Dark Matter Revisited and the Role of Ultralight ALPs
items.summary: In this work, we revisit the multi-component axion dark matter (DM) scenario and explore the role of ultralight axion-like particles (ALPs). After briefly reviewing maximal axion mixing, we incorporate a stochastic axion mixing mechanism that generalizes it by relaxing the requirement of a uniform hierarchy among the axion decay constants.
items.author: Hai-Jun Li

items.title: Recipe for near-unity efficient frequency conversion via transient molecular modulation
items.summary: Frequency transduction technologies are an essential element for interfacing devices operating at distinct spectral regions. Specifically, the conversion of weak signals between different wavelengths is a fundamental requirement of quantum networks, where conversion efficiency is critical for preserving the statistical properties of light.
items.author: Arturo Mena, Pau Arcos, María Sánchez-Hernández et al.

items.title: M 4.7 - 18 km ESE of Güvercinlik, Turkey
items.summary: A magnitude 4.7 earthquake was recorded 18 km ESE of Güvercinlik, Turkey. The event happened on 24 November 2026 at 15:39 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. About 1 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Packing the Bragg sphere: complete three-dimensional photonic band gaps at the refractive index of polymers (1.55)
items.summary: Complete 3D photonic band gaps have so far been found only at refractive-index contrasts of about 1.9 and above, reached by rod-connected diamond lattice structures. Reciprocal-space design of quasiperiodic structures recently achieved considerable emission attenuation at much lower contrasts [L.
items.author: Alexander Itin

items.title: Heat Reduction in Erbium-Doped Microresonator
items.summary: We investigate anti-Stokes fluorescence in a 106-micrometer-diameter silica whispering-gallery-mode microresonator coated with erbium-doped sol-gel, assessing its potential for reduced optical heating. Near-infrared fluorescence spectra acquired under pulsed excitation near 1.55 micrometers exhibit a mean emitted photon energy above the pump photon energy.
items.author: Nitzan Shani, Bar Favelukis, Menachem Guttmann et al.

items.title: Nonreciprocal state-selective splitting of eigenstates at a polarization exceptional point
items.summary: Non-Hermitian photonic systems can be engineered to exhibit exceptional points (EPs), where eigenvalues and eigenstates coalesce. Although perturbations near EPs have mainly been characterized through eigenvalue splitting, the branch-resolved evolution of the coalesced eigenstates under a tunable reciprocity-breaking perturbation remains less systematically explored.
items.author: Zhuofan Yu, Soojeong Baek, Puxuan Jiang et al.

items.title: Distinct trajectories and predictability of individual grouping patterns in dolphins link social ageing to longevity
items.summary: Recent work has unearthed strong relationships between ageing and average sociability. Clear patterns of decreases in average sociability are observed across taxa; many of these are sex-specific. Individuals, however, generally deviate from population averages, and discounting individual variance in behaviour could disguise mechanisms of adaptation, selection, and developmental stability.
items.author: Kelley C. Meehan, Barbara Class, Shinichi Nakagawa et al.

items.title: Beyond profiles: Supervised repeat annotation using protein embeddings
items.summary: Protein repeats give rise to diverse protein structures and functions, yet their sequence-based detection is often challenging because individual repeat units can diverge substantially in sequence while retaining similar structures. Most sensitive approaches rely on sequence information directly represented by alignments or derived profiles, thereby limiting flexibility and scalability.
items.author: Kaiyu Qiu, Jan Ludwiczak, Andrei N. Lupas et al.

items.title: The Aspergillus fumigatus C2-domain protein SppA is required for septal integrity and alters susceptibility to echinocandins and neutrophil killing during infection
items.summary: Aspergillus fumigatus is a major opportunistic fungal pathogen whose ability to maintain hyphal integrity and withstand host defenses is critical for virulence. Septal pores, which connect hyphal compartments, are dynamically regulated to preserve cellular integrity under stress, yet the molecular components governing this process remain incompletely defined.
items.author: Dante G. Calise, Madeline L. Michaelis, Jin Woo Bok et al.

items.title: Human papillomavirus vaccination coverage among adolescent girls and young women living with HIV in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Introduction Human Papilloma Virus (HPV)-attributable cancers disproportionately affect adolescent girls and young women living with HIV (AGYWLHIV) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet HPV vaccination coverage in this subpopulation remains suboptimal. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the pooled prevalence of HPV vaccination coverage among AGYWLHIV in LMICs.
items.author: Ifeyinwa Lilian Ezenwosu, John Olajide Olawepo, Jane Nnedinma Ohaekweiro et al.

items.title: Bayesian generative modeling for heterogeneous wastewater data applied to COVID-19 forecasting
items.summary: Infectious disease forecasts can inform public health decision-making. Wastewater monitoring is a relatively new epidemiological data source with multiple potential applications, including forecasting. Incorporating wastewater data into epidemiological forecasting models is challenging, and relatively few studies have assessed whether this improves forecast performance.
items.author: Kaitlyn E. Johnson, George Vega Yon, Samuel P. C. Brand et al.

items.title: Shaping the spread: Influence of distributor vane design on fertilizer distribution uniformity
items.summary: Achieving uniform fertilizer distribution with disc-type spreaders is critical for both crop nutrition and environmental sustainability, yet it remains challenging due to the numerous influencing parameters. This study specifically investigates the impact of distributor vane geometry on the coefficient of variation (CV, %) of twin-disc broadcasters.
items.author: Fırat Kömekçi, Erkan Urkan, Ceren Kömekçi et al.

items.title: Occupational stress and its association with nurses productivity in the Buea Health District, Cameroon: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: Background Occupational stress is a major concern among healthcare workers, particularly nurses, due to its negative impacts on mental health and productivity. Nurses face multiple stressors including heavy workloads, long hours, exposure to infectious diseases, and the emotional toll of patient care.
items.author: Akah Thelma Eni, Kelly Tabe Takang, Odette Dzemo Kibu et al.

items.title: Topical vancomycin powder and surgical site infection in cranial and spinal surgery: A prospective cohort study from Pakistan
items.summary: Background Surgical site infection is a major complication of neurosurgery, and its incidence is higher in low- and middle-income countries. Topical vancomycin powder has shown potential for preventing surgical site infection in high-income settings, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited.
items.author: Ihsan Ullah, Syed Shayan Shah, Muhammad Nawaz Khan et al.

items.title: The influence of green organizational culture on task performance of non-teaching staff of higher educational institutions: Mediating role of contextual performance in Gandaki Province of Nepal
items.summary: Organizational greening is receiving more attention these days. A green organizational culture is essential to saving our ‘home’, the globe, as it promotes environmentally friendly practices across institutions. Because of severe environmental deterioration, not only humans but also day-to-day profit- or non-profit-oriented institutional environments suffer.
items.author: Nabin Bahadur Adhikari, Bharat Ram Dhungana, Bipin Bahadur Adhikari

items.title: Predicting farmers’ crop choice between hybrid and indigenous varieties based on socio-ecological context and perceived crop advantages in Nepal
items.summary: Farmers in Nepal increasingly combine market-sourced improved seed with indigenous seed that is traditionally saved and shared across local communities. This study aims to examine associations between crop choice, household social-ecological characteristics, and farmers’ concurrent perceptions of the comparative advantages of improved and indigenous crops.
items.author: Prience Shrestha, Sujata Shrestha, Tulasa Chaudhary et al.

items.title: Genetic and clinical spectrum of infantile-onset Pompe disease: A Vietnamese cohort study
