items.summary: Background Infantile-onset Pompe disease (IOPD) is the most severe form of Pompe disease, resulting from pathogenic GAA variants that cause lysosomal acid α-glucosidase deficiency. Although molecular diagnosis has improved substantially, comprehensive genotype–phenotype data from genetically confirmed IOPD cohorts in Southeast Asia remain limited.
items.author: Giang Thi Kim Dang, Khanh Ngoc Nguyen, Mai Thi Thanh Do et al.

items.title: Audiological manifestations of Fabry disease in South Korea: A single-center cohort study on hearing impairment and tinnitus
items.summary: Fabry disease (FD), a rare X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by α-galactosidase A deficiency, leads to progressive accumulation of globotriaosylceramide and globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) in various tissues. Hearing loss has been reported in FD internationally; however, data on Korean patients are lacking.
items.author: Hae Jin Oh, Jae Hyuk Choi, Seok-Hyun Kim et al.

items.title: Mitigating regional bias in Vietnamese hate speech detection via contrastive learning with adversarial fairness
items.summary: Vietnamese hate speech detection (HSD) models can inadvertently latch onto regional dialect cues as spurious shortcuts, producing unfair performance gaps across the country’s language varieties. Prior fairness work, however, has largely targeted gender or race in English, and existing Vietnamese HSD resources carry no regional annotation, leaving dialect-driven bias unmeasured.
items.author: Trong-Chi Duong, Anh-Cuong Le, Thang V. Q. Le et al.

items.title: Species diversity increases information flow about predation in bird communities
items.summary: by Agnishikhe Kumar, Jiahao Wu, Ping Ding, Jakob Bro-Jørgensen, Mylène Dutour, Ari E. Martínez, Xingfeng Si, Qiang Zhang, Eben Goodale The Biodiversity-Ecosystem Functioning (BEF) literature has shown species diversity to be essential for ecosystem functioning and services. Yet this concept has not been extended often to behavioral ecology, so that although it is understood that acquiring social information from heterospecific individuals is an important component of ecosystem functioning, it is unclear how animal signaling at the community level, and subsequent information flow, is related to increased species diversity. Eliciting vocal responses using predator models across 10 nature reserves on a latitudinal gradient, we first show that the species diversity of birds is correlated with signaling about predation, both in the low-risk system of mobbing and in the higher-risk system of alarm calls.
items.author: Agnishikhe Kumar, Jiahao Wu, Ping Ding et al.

items.title: Vascular modelling of peripheral ischaemic disease response
items.summary: by Lachlan Arthur, Michele Carrabba, Paolo Madeddu, Steven McDougall, Vassilis Sboros Ischaemic disease presents a significant challenge in medical science due to its widespread manifestations in the body and its tendency to only become overt in its late stages, beyond where current intervention methods are effective. Diseases such as coronary heart disease and peripheral artery disease (PAD) represent leading causes of death and are detrimental to quality of life. Focussing on the latter, PAD incurs an amputation rate of around 25%, largely owing to microvascular disease that prevents tissue recovery even after revascularisation. Current methods for investigating PAD either cannot chart specific vascular determinants, such as with in vivo imaging, or deform and remove subjects from longitudinal studies, such as with ex vivo tissue sampling.
items.author: Lachlan Arthur, Michele Carrabba, Paolo Madeddu et al.

items.title: CoEVFold suite: User friendly pipelines to visually represent protein coevolution
items.summary: by Chris L. B. Graham, Liam Cremona, Robin Little, Christopher D. A. Rodrigues Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data underlies current principles in protein folding and protein-protein interaction prediction, from which deep-learning models trained on protein sequence and structure datasets can predict protein structure. However, what is missing are user-friendly tools that enable researchers to identify and visualise coevolution, the principal signal that these MSAs encode. Here we present tools to identify and visualize coevolution, through a pipeline (CoEVFold) that uses basic direct coupling algorithms derived from GREMLIN and an input alignment of sequences from MMseqs2. We also provide notebooks to calculate coevolution with alternative methods such as CCMpred or plmc.
items.author: Chris L. B. Graham, Liam Cremona, Robin Little et al.

items.title: Deciphering the replication-division coordination in E. coli : A unified mathematical framework for systematic model comparison
items.summary: by Alexandre Perrin, Marie Doumic, Meriem El Karoui, Sylvie Méléard Despite extensive research, the quantitative principles that govern the coordination between DNA replication and cell division in bacteria remain debated. Multiple theoretical models have been proposed, some postulating that a single regulatory process is sufficient to ensure replication–division coordination, while others argue that two concurrent processes are required for robust control. In this work, we develop a unifying mathematical framework within which models can be consistently formulated, qualitatively analysed and quantitatively compared. This framework also allows us to propose a new double-process model. Through theoretical analysis, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which single-process models can reproduce physiological cell behaviours.
items.author: Alexandre Perrin, Marie Doumic, Meriem El Karoui et al.

items.title: Differential vulnerability of stimulus-locked and persistent gamma oscillations: Implications in schizophrenia
items.summary: by Daniel W. Chung, G. Bard Ermentrout Working memory depends on gamma oscillations generated across sensory and prefrontal cortices. In primary visual cortex (V1), stimulus-locked gamma oscillations encode stimulus information, while in prefrontal cortex (PFC), persistent gamma oscillations maintain this information after the stimulus is removed. In schizophrenia (SZ), gamma power is reduced in both V1 and PFC, consistent with deficits in sensory encoding and working memory maintenance. Both oscillation regimes arise from a canonical microcircuit involving pyramidal neurons (PNs) and parvalbumin-expressing interneurons (PVIs). Yet, whether the two regimes are similarly or differentially vulnerable to synaptic alterations within this circuit in SZ remains unknown.
items.author: Daniel W. Chung, G. Bard Ermentrout

items.title: TRAFIKK: Systematic prediction and mechanistic interpretation of anticancer drug synergies
items.summary: by Marco Fariñas, Viviam Bermúdez, Eirini Tsirvouli, Kristine Lippestad, John Zobolas, Tero Aittokallio, Kaisa Lehti, Åsmund Flobak Effective drug combination therapies can improve cancer treatment, yet the mechanistic basis of drug synergy remains poorly understood. Most computational approaches prioritise predictive accuracy over molecular mechanistic interpretability, providing limited insights into how synergistic effects emerge across signalling contexts. We developed Trafikk, a molecular-signalling network-based framework that simulates drug perturbations in cell-line-specific computational models to mirror functional outcomes in experimental combination screens. Across two independent large-scale datasets, Trafikk identified synergistic combinations with >77% recall. Functional response predictions revealed both conserved and context-dependent mechanisms.
items.author: Marco Fariñas, Viviam Bermúdez, Eirini Tsirvouli et al.

items.title: RNA deaminase modulates metabolic stress-induced longevity in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.summary: by Jingyi Ke, Zi Wang, Ming Li, Zhengyang Guo, Di Chen, Wei Li, Guangshuo Ou Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing expands transcriptomic diversity, yet its contribution to organismal aging remains unclear. Here, we show that ADAR enzyme ADR-2 is specifically required for lifespan extension under metabolic stress. Loss of adr-2 abolished the longevity of mitochondrial dysfunction ( isp-1 ) and dietary restriction ( eat-2 ) mutants, while leaving lifespan extension mediated by reduced insulin/IGF-1 ( daf-2 ) or mTOR ( rsks-1 ) signaling intact. RNA editome analysis revealed increased ADR-2-dependent editing of three paralogous transmembrane genes, trel-1 , trel-2 , and trel-3 , in long-lived isp-1 and eat-2 animals.
items.author: Jingyi Ke, Zi Wang, Ming Li et al.

items.title: Electrical, mechanical, and morphological properties of nano-filled HTV-SR/EPDM blends under AC corona aging
items.summary: by Muhammad Zaheer Saleem, Zulkarnain Ahmad Noorden, Lau Kwan Yiew, Ali Ahmed Salem, Abdullah S. Algamili Among the various factors, corona discharge is recognized as one of the most threatening to degrade polymeric insulators. Over time, corona-induced deterioration has become a more dominant phenomenon in extra- and ultrahigh-voltage transmission lines. Therefore, this study investigates the aging effects on optimally balanced weight-percentage samples of high-temperature-vulcanized silicone rubber/ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (HTV-SR/EPDM) incorporating boron nitride (BN) and silicon carbide (SiC) fillers to identify the most desirable composition for resistance to degradation. The nano-sized fillers were loaded at 1, 3, and 5 wt.%. The test samples were subjected to an AC corona discharge for 72 h, utilizing a multi-needle high-voltage electrode and a plane-grounded electrode arrangement.
items.author: Muhammad Zaheer Saleem, Zulkarnain Ahmad Noorden, Lau Kwan Yiew et al.

items.title: Reversal in HIV testing uptake among adolescent girls in Zambia, 2007–2024: A decomposition analysis of four Demographic and Health Surveys
items.summary: by Samson Shumba, Maureen Aongola, Deborah Tembo Background Zambia expanded HIV testing substantially during the 2010s, but testing strategies changed after 2018 with the shift to targeted testing and the COVID-19 pandemic. We examined trends in HIV testing among adolescent girls between 2007 and 2024, and whether changes reflected shifts in the characteristics of adolescent girls or in how those characteristics related to testing. Methods We pooled data on 11,717 girls aged 15–19 years from the 2007, 2013/14, 2018 and 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Surveys. Outcomes were ever having been tested for HIV and having been tested in the past 12 months and received the result.
items.author: Samson Shumba, Maureen Aongola, Deborah Tembo

items.title: Influence of the Fe 3 O 4 /SiO 2 ratio on the strength and fracture mechanisms of magnetite ore like materials under uniaxial compression
items.summary: by Tao Yuan, Tianhong Yang, Zhenqi Yang, Qianbai Zhao, Yong Zhao, Jinduo Li, Ke Luo, Yuan Gao The Fe 3 O 4 /SiO 2 ratio is an important compositional factor affecting the mechanical behavior of magnetite ore like materials. In this study, uniaxial compression simulations were carried out using particle flow models with different Fe 3 O 4 /SiO 2 ratios, and the simulated crack evolution and acoustic emission (AE) responses were interpreted together with SEM-EDS observations. The uniaxial compressive strength varies non monotonically with the Fe 3 O 4 /SiO 2 ratio. As the ratio decreased from 3.00 to 1.00, the peak strength decreased from 131.64 MPa to 81.95 MPa.
items.author: Tao Yuan, Tianhong Yang, Zhenqi Yang et al.

items.title: Barriers and facilitators along the continuum of care among people living with hepatitis B in EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK: A scoping review
items.summary: by Rigmor C. Berg, Miroslav Kojic, Asgeir Johannessen, Vegard Skogen Hepatitis B virus (HBV) represents a significant global health burden, with approximately 14 million infected individuals in EU/EEA countries. The alarmingly low proportions diagnosed, linked to, engaged and retained in care underscore the necessity for further evidence on HBV care continuum dynamics, as emphasized in the new World Health Organisation guidelines for HBV. We conducted a scoping review to identify and describe research addressing modifiable barriers and facilitators related to the care continuum for people living with HBV infection in EU/EEA countries, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. We pre-specified our methods in a protocol, conducted the review in line with a methodological guide, searched six databases, selected eligible studies in duplicate, and summarized data descriptively.
items.author: Rigmor C. Berg, Miroslav Kojic, Asgeir Johannessen et al.

items.title: Prevalence of diarrhea and its determinants among children under five years of age in rural Kebeles of East Gurage Zone, central Ethiopia: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Melaku Tesfaye, Seid Tiku Mereta, Dessalegn Dadi Introduction Diarrheal disease remains a major cause of death among children under five, particularly in resource-limited settings. Despite the availability of effective water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions, the burden of diarrhea remains high in Ethiopia. This study aims to assess the prevalence of diarrhea and its associated factors among under-five children in East Gurage Zone, central Ethiopia. Methodology This baseline survey was part of a four-arm cluster randomized trial (cRCT). Using the Hayes and Bennett formula, we set the sample size at 840 participants (210 per arm) with 95% confidence and 80% power.
items.author: Melaku Tesfaye, Seid Tiku Mereta, Dessalegn Dadi

items.title: Association between duodenal mucosa-associated periodontal bacteria and advanced liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
items.summary: by Kazuki Niida, Yasunori Yamamoto, Teruki Miyake, Mirai Hayashi, Kazuhiro Tange, Takao Watanabe, Osamu Yoshida, Yoshio Tokumoto, Hideomi Tomida, Eiji Takeshita, Yoshio Ikeda, Yoichi Hiasa Gut microbiota and periodontal diseases are potential risk factors for duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota in fibrosis progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease; however, the specific contribution of duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota remains unclear. Therefore, in this prospective study, we investigated its association with liver stiffness to elucidate its role in disease progression. Duodenal brush samples were collected during endoscopy from patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, classified by liver stiffness measurement into advanced (liver stiffness measurement>8.7 kPa, n = 10) and non-advanced (n = 20) groups.
items.author: Kazuki Niida, Yasunori Yamamoto, Teruki Miyake et al.

items.title: The buffering role of perceived servant leadership in the association between attachment avoidance and contextual job performance
items.summary: by Martin Seitl, Daniel Dostál, Roman Mraček Attachment avoidance, characterized by deactivation strategies that prioritize self-reliance over collaborative engagement, has been identified as a negative predictor of contextual job performance. However, the situational conditions that mitigate this relationship remain understudied. Drawing on trait activation theory and adult attachment theory, this study examines the buffering role of perceived servant leadership, an attachment-responsive behavioral repertoire conceptualized as a potential situational distractor, in the association between trait-like workplace attachment avoidance and contextual job performance. Using a cross-sectional employee self-report design, we examined a sample of employees in the Czech Republic with measures of workplace attachment avoidance, perceived servant leadership, and two facets of self-reported contextual performance: job dedication and interpersonal facilitation.
items.author: Martin Seitl, Daniel Dostál, Roman Mraček

items.title: Add-on DMARDs and interstitial lung disease in methotrexate-treated rheumatoid arthritis: A prevalent new-user design study using a large regional Japanese claims database
items.summary: by Daito Funaki, Eiji Nakatani, Koichi Miyashita, Kentaro Minowa, Ryo Watanabe, Akinori Miyakoshi, Hideaki Kaneda, Hironao Hozumi, Akira Sugawara, Yoshihiro Tanaka Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by joint inflammation, destruction, and systemic complications including interstitial lung disease (ILD). We conducted a prevalent new-user design study using the Shizuoka Kokuho Database in Japan to examine ILD incidence after addition of non-methotrexate (MTX) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) to MTX therapy. Patients receiving sulfasalazine, tacrolimus hydrate, etanercept, iguratimod, bucillamine, or denosumab were compared with time-conditioned MTX controls using propensity score matching. Death was treated as a competing event. Among 63,952 patients with RA, 11,430 who received MTX were included in the source cohort.
items.author: Daito Funaki, Eiji Nakatani, Koichi Miyashita et al.

items.title: Lexical variety versus syntactic processing load in nineteenth-century children’s and adult literature
items.summary: by Demei Yang, Shilong Tao Children’s literature, written by adults for young readers, is widely assumed to be linguistically simpler than literature for adults, yet this assumption has rarely been tested along separate dimensions of complexity. We compared lexical variety and syntactic processing load in all 100 texts of two CLiC corpora: the 19th Century Children’s Literature Corpus (ChiLit, 71 texts) and the 19th Century Reference Corpus (19C, 29 adult novels). Lexical variety was measured with the Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR) at window sizes from 50 to 1000 tokens, and syntactic processing load with mean dependency distance (MDD). Mixed-effects models treated author as a random effect and adjusted for publication year, and equivalence tests asked whether the corpora differed negligibly in MDD.
items.author: Demei Yang, Shilong Tao

items.title: Influence of CO 2 /CH 4 production ratios on the isotope signature of methane
items.summary: by M. Elizabeth Holmes, Alexis E. Slentz, Samantha H. Bosman, Yueh-Fen Li, Rachel M. Wilson, Apryl L. Perry, Ruth K. Varner, Scott R. Saleska, Virginia I. Rich, Suzanne B. Hodgkins, Derek A. Smith, Sarah C. Bagby, EMERGE Field Team , EMERGE Institute Coordinators , Jeffrey P. Chanton Stable carbon isotopes are often used to infer dominant methanogenic pathways in wetland ecosystems. We performed closed system incubations with Sphagnum bog peat, monitoring CO 2 and CH 4 production and isotopic composition across incubation temperatures and over time. We observed higher CO 2 production relative to CH 4 production (CO 2 /CH 4 > 1).
items.author: M. Elizabeth Holmes, Alexis E. Slentz, Samantha H. Bosman et al.

items.title: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the Medical Leadership Competence Scale among residents
items.summary: by Di Xue, Aijun Zhu, Zhijun Wu, Huaijie Yang, Jian Zheng, Li Li, Min Hu, Man Hu Objective To translate the Medical Leadership Competence Scale (MeLeCoS) into Chinese, culturally adapt it, test its reliability and validity among resident physicians, and provide a tool for assessing resident physicians’ medical leadership competence. Methods We translated, back-translated, and culturally adapted the scale using Brislin’s method to form the Chinese version of the Medical Leadership Competence Scale. In Phase 1, we used cluster sampling to conduct a questionnaire survey among 242 resident physicians at a national-level standardized residency training base in the Yichang area from March to April 2025, and we used these data for exploratory factor analysis.
items.author: Di Xue, Aijun Zhu, Zhijun Wu et al.

items.title: An efficient framework for uncertainty propagation in nonlinear reinforced concrete analysis using multiplicative dimension reduction and laplace-transform maximum entropy
items.summary: by Marzieh Allahyari, Masoud Soltani Uncertainty in material properties, member geometry, and modeling assumptions can strongly affect the predicted response of reinforced concrete (RC) structures, especially after cracking, yielding, and other nonlinear mechanisms develop. Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) provides a direct reference for uncertainty propagation, but its computational cost can become prohibitive when each realization requires an iterative nonlinear finite-element analysis. Dimension-reduction methods can estimate response moments using fewer deterministic analyses, while maximum-entropy methods can reconstruct probability distributions from limited probabilistic information. However, the accuracy, computational efficiency, and practical applicability of an integrated dimension-reduction and maximum-entropy workflow have not been sufficiently established for nonlinear fiber-based RC member and frame analysis.
items.author: Marzieh Allahyari, Masoud Soltani

items.title: Geopolitical zone disparities and correlates of minimum adequate antenatal care utilization in Nigeria: A multilevel analysis of the 2024 NDHS
items.summary: by Abdirasak Sharif Ali, Uthman Okikiola Adebayo, Mohamed Abdirahim Omar, Olalekan John Okesanya, Yahye Sheikh Abdulle Hassan, Jamilu Sani, Mohamed Mustaf Ahmed Background Antenatal care (ANC) is a fundamental component of maternal healthcare that is critical for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes. Although the 2016 World Health Organization (WHO) model recommends a minimum of eight contacts, the four-or-more-visit indicator remains widely used in Demographic and Health Survey (DHS)-based monitoring and permits comparability with previous Nigerian and regional evidence. This study examined geopolitical zone disparities and individual- and community-level correlates of minimum adequate antenatal care utilization, defined as four or more antenatal care visits, using the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS).
items.author: Abdirasak Sharif Ali, Uthman Okikiola Adebayo, Mohamed Abdirahim Omar et al.

items.title: The impact of Generative AI chatbots on behavioral intention in travel planning: A theory of consumption value perspective
items.summary: by Ying Wei, Jialin Zhang Generative AI (GenAI) chatbots are revolutionizing online travel planning by transitioning travelers’ focus from merely gathering information to obtaining personalized recommendations and facilitating seamless bookings. Grounded in the Interactive Technology Acceptance Model and Consumption Value Theory, this study investigates how the attributes of GenAI chatbots, specifically personalization and anthropomorphism, alongside user traits such as self-efficacy and personal innovativeness, influence travel planning intention through perceived value. Data collected from a questionnaire survey were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that GenAI chatbot attributes (personalization and anthropomorphism) and user traits (self-efficacy and personal innovativeness) exert significant direct positive effects on perceived values.
items.author: Ying Wei, Jialin Zhang

items.title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the π-conjugated spacers
items.summary: The nature of the π-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca.
items.author: Laurette-Apolline Jerro, Imen Hnid, Imane Arbouch et al.

items.title: Hurricane season wrap-up: El Nino fueled record number of Pacific storms but calmed Atlantic
items.summary: Hurricane season wrap-up: El Nino fueled record number of Pacific storms but calmed Atlantic November 24, 2026 A NOAA satellite view of the eye of Hurricane Isaias approaching the U.S. Gulf coast in daytime on October 9, 2026. (Image credit: NOAA Satellites) Download Image The 2026 hurricane season, which officially ends November 30, will be remembered as a year of contrasts between the Atlantic and Pacific, a classic indication of a hurricane season influenced by a very strong El Nino. Below normal activity across the Atlantic basin was offset by above-average activity in the Pacific, including two disasters in Hawaii.
items.author: genevieve.contey

items.title: M 4.8 - 71 km W of Vallenar, Chile
items.summary: A magnitude 4.8 earthquake was recorded 71 km W of Vallenar, Chile. The event happened on 24 November 2026 at 13:22 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 33 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: M 5.0 - 24 km WNW of Piti Village, Guam
items.summary: A magnitude 5 earthquake was recorded 24 km WNW of Piti Village, Guam. The event happened on 24 November 2026 at 11:55 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 108 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: M 5.2 - 93 km WSW of Puerto Madero, Mexico
items.summary: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake was recorded 93 km WSW of Puerto Madero, Mexico. The event happened on 24 November 2026 at 11:51 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 35 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Within-task hazards of AI agents: unidentified by time-horizon curves, identified by repeated runs
items.summary: The time horizon of an AI agent is read off a curve: the probability that the agent completes a task, plotted against the time a human needs for it. Several recent analyses fit survival models to this curve and conclude that agents' hazard of failure declines as a task goes on. The curve cannot support that conclusion. Every log-logistic horizon curve with slope $β\le1$ is a mixture of constant-hazard curves, and in a proportional-hazards frailty model the same curve is produced by every within-task Weibull shape $k\geβ$. If runs of a task are conditionally independent, repeated runs restore identification within this model: the probability that two runs both succeed is the single-run curve shifted by $1/k$ on the $\log_2$ time axis.
items.author: Ruiqi Zhao

items.title: A Face Robot which Imitates Human Musculoskeletal Skin System and Its Evaluation on Basic Movement of Facial Expression
items.summary: Facial robots require many coordinated, smallamplitude motions, but accommodating these motions in a compact face remains difficult. This paper presents an anatomically inspired facial-robot platform that reproduces the layered organization of the human facial musculoskeletal system. The platform comprises bone, muscle, and skin components whose geometry, shape, and attachment locations are derived from three-dimensional anatomical data. Wire-driven, compliant muscle components are routed through PTFE tubes, allowing actuation to be placed away from the face. We describe the selection and fabrication of 65 muscles (34 muscle types) required to reproduce the 47 target action units (AUs) in the Facial Action Coding System (FACS).
items.author: Shun Kaneko, Shunnosuke Yoshimura, Akihiro Miki et al.

items.title: Continuum model for disconnection structures of hetero-interfaces
items.summary: Hetero-interfaces, as planar defects between dissimilar materials, accommodate the lattice misfit through networks of line defects of disconnections (a combination of structural ledges/step and dislocation characters). We develop a continuum model that predicts the hetero-interface structures, including disconnection networks, the interface inclination and misorientation angles. The model is based on the interfacial energy minimization with respect to all possible disconnection modes, subject to the interface structure constraint of the generalized Frank-Bilby equation that describes the lattice correspondence across the interface including both dislocation and step characters of disconnections and the inclination and misorientation angles. Numerical simulations are performed to determine the equilibrium configurations of three different types of hetero-interfaces: the $α$/$β$ (orthorhombic/monoclinic) interface in ZrO$_2$, $α$/$β$ hetero-interfaces in Ti and Au/Pd (001) twist-misfit interfaces.
items.author: Luchan Zhang, Xiaoxue Qin, Dongsong Tao et al.

items.title: Delay-Tolerant Formation Tracking for Multi-AGV Systems via Reference-Shift Coupling
items.summary: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) that transport a load together must keep a formation while each vehicle tracks its own reference, and they coordinate over wireless links with link-dependent, time-varying and jumping delays. We propose a cascade design for differential-drive AGVs modelled as kinematic unicycles: delayed data from the neighbours drive only a second-order filter that shifts each vehicle's own reference, and an unmodified gain-scheduled tracking law follows the shifted reference. A saturation keeps the shifted reference feasible, and the feed-forward is exact, so the tracking loop never sees the network. We prove that tracking and formation errors remain bounded for arbitrary delays and converge for every bounded delay and every directed, possibly switching, graph.
items.author: Yunfei Bi

items.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy
items.summary: Fluorescence microscopy drives much of modern life science, but accessible imaging setups often yield images degraded by out-of-focus light, limited resolution, and strong signal-dependent noise. Computational restoration can recover high-quality images from such data, enabling cheaper and faster imaging at lower light dose, provided biologically meaningful structures are preserved. Guided conditional flow matching has recently shown strong results for microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution by learning distributions of plausible restorations. However, it pairs each clean target with an independent standard Gaussian sample, so the starting point of every training path does not leverage the degraded observation. This arbitrary noise--target coupling can produce conflicting velocity targets and makes the conditional velocity field harder to learn.
items.author: Anirban Ray, Florian Jug

items.title: CPU-Eval: Evaluating Large Language Models for CPU Hardware Code Generation
items.summary: Benchmarks such as VerilogEval have supported rapid advances in hardware description language (HDL) generation by large language models (LLMs). However, recent HDL-generation systems achieve pass rates above 90% on VerilogEval, leaving limited headroom for revealing further advances. To provide a challenging target for further progress on a practically important hardware-development task, we introduce CPU-Eval, a benchmark of 339 HDL-generation problems constructed from six CPUs. Drawn from practical CPU designs, including families fabricated in silicon, the problems span CPUs from small embedded cores to Linux-capable out-of-order cores and cover diverse CPU functions written in SystemVerilog, Chisel, and SpinalHDL. In each problem, an LLM performs the real CPU-development task of generating HDL.
items.author: Yuisei Iwata, Yutaka Masuda, Tohru Ishihara

items.title: A Framework for Graph Node Symmetric Quantification under Dataset Shift
items.summary: Graph node quantification is the supervised learning task of estimating the prevalence of different classes within an arbitrary sample of unlabelled nodes from a graph, subject to some form of dataset shift. Existing approaches to graph node quantification typically follow the standard aggregative paradigm, i.e., they use labelled nodes from the graph to train an intermediate node classifier, and obtain an estimated class distribution for the sample by aggregating the classifier's predictions for the individual nodes and then correcting the result via some adjustment strategy that accounts for dataset shift. In this work we propose a framework for graph node quantification that does away with both node-level supervision, since its training phase only requires node samples labelled by their class distribution, and node-level predictions, since it estimates class prevalence values directly, without the need of any intermediate node classifier.
items.author: Alessio Micheli, Alejandro Moreo, Marco Podda et al.

items.title: M 6.4 - Mauritius - Reunion region
items.summary: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake was recorded Mauritius - Reunion region. The event happened on 24 November 2026 at 11:06 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Optimal Transport Meets t-SNE: Integrated Visualization without Batch Effects in OT-tSNE
items.summary: Visual exploration is an integral step in understanding the structure of datasets. However, systematic variation between datasets collected under different conditions, known as batch effects, can obscure shared structure and complicate their joint visualization. Existing methods often rely on cross-batch nearest-neighbor relations to integrate the batches. Yet, these local correspondences can be unreliable for challenging cross-batch geometries. We propose optimal-transport t-SNE (OT-tSNE), which replaces nearest-neighbor-based matching with globally coupled affinities derived from entropic optimal transport. Controlled synthetic experiments demonstrated that nearest-neighbor-based methods can deteriorate, while optimal-transport affinities and OT-tSNE embeddings remain robust. Across seven real single-cell datasets, we benchmarked OT-tSNE against a broad range of integration and visualization methods and found that it achieves a Pareto-efficient trade-off between batch mixing and biological conservation, and integrates batches particularly well.
items.author: Azhar Akhmetova, Edward Eichhorn, Boris Landa et al.

items.title: Verify then Steer: Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery for Continuous Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.summary: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an agent to follow language instructions to reach a target in an unseen 3D environment. However, existing methods still struggle to recover from route deviations at test time. We investigate this limitation through the lens of instruction progress, and trace it to a phenomenon we term progress hallucination: agents misinterpret off-route observations as evidence of task progress, causing their internal instruction progress to advance beyond the actual task stage and hindering recovery based on earlier sub-instructions. To address this failure mode, we propose PHAR (Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery), a test-time recovery framework following a verify-then-steer paradigm. The verifier examines residual-stream representations of the Vision-Language Model (VLM) to identify mismatch of cross-modal evidence along the trajectories, and uses split conformal calibration to control false alarms.
items.author: Jiewen Hou, Guanxiang Qi, Meina Kan et al.

items.title: Not All Pairs Align: Caption-Guided Audio-Visual Contrastive Learning
items.summary: We address the problem of learning audio-visual representations from co-occurring modalities. Multimodal contrastive learning typically assumes that paired observations provide shared views of the same underlying information. While this may be true for datasets collected in constrained environments, it does not always hold. For instance, co-occurring audio and visual signals can differ substantially in their content due to off-screen sounds. Nevertheless, standard contrastive objectives treat all paired samples as equally aligned. In this work, we propose Caption Guided Alignment Aware Loss (CGAAL), a model-agnostic objective that leverages modality-specific captions to estimate semantic agreement between audio and video. CGAAL uses these agreement scores to weight the contribution of each positive pair.
items.author: Omar Emara, Nan Lu, Dima Damen et al.

items.title: Second-order asymptotics for the quantum and private capacities of the erasure channel
items.summary: An erasure channel either delivers a quantum system intact or tells the receiver that it was lost. How much quantum information, or secret classical information, can a finite block transmit without assistance? We determine the optimal second-order coding rates for input dimension $d\ge2$, erasure probability $0<p<1/2$, and fixed infidelity (one minus fidelity) $0<\varepsilon<1$. For $n$ channel uses, the optimal base-two logarithmic code size is \begin{equation}\tag{A}\label{eq:abstract-rate} n(1-2p)\log_2d +2\sqrt{np(1-p)}\log_2d\,Φ^{-1}(\varepsilon) +O((\ln n)^2), \end{equation} where $Φ$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and $Φ^{-1}$ is its quantile function. The square-root term is the second-order correction. This formula holds for entanglement transmission, entanglement generation, and private classical communication.
items.author: Mark M. Wilde

items.title: Fractal Neural Synthesis: Constant-Storage Procedural Weight Derivation via Complex Quadratic Boundary Dynamics
items.summary: Conventional neural networks store synaptic parameters as explicit tensors whose persistent Flash footprint scales linearly (O(W)) with parameter count, constraining resource-limited edge microcontrollers. We formulate and systematically evaluate Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), a procedural weight derivation architecture that replaces hidden-layer matrices with a constant 24-byte coordinate seed Theta = (c_x, c_y, ell) in F_64^3 anchored near the complex quadratic bifurcation boundary dM of f_c(z) = z^2 + c. We introduce a large-bailout (R = 256) smooth escape kernel, four zero-overhead geometric sampling apertures--Cartesian Grid, coprime 3x3 Rule-of-Thirds (Z/9Z), phi-Vogel spiral, and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod--and prove conditional Kolmogorov (K_Kolm <= 192 + c_0 bits) and Shannon entropy bounds.
items.author: Volkan Dagli, Zerrin Dagli, Daghan Dagli

items.title: Latent Class Mixed Model Variational Autoencoders for Scalable Phenotyping of Health Trajectories
items.summary: Clustering longitudinal health trajectories requires handling high-dimensional measurements, irregular visit times, and subject-level heterogeneity while retaining clinically interpretable structure. Existing methods address this only partially: latent-class mixed models yield an interpretable, covariate-driven partition but do not scale past a handful of markers, while deep time-series clustering scales at the cost of that structure and generally requires a common time grid. We introduce the Latent Class Mixed Model Variational Autoencoder (LCMM-VAE), a deep generative model whose latent prior is a mixture of class-specific linear mixed models, so that each subject's latent trajectory decomposes into its class mean trajectory and a subject-specific deviation.
items.author: Philomène Letzelter, Violaine Courrier, Sandrine Katsahian et al.

items.title: Evolve to Learn: Gradient-aligned experience evolution for model self-improvement
items.summary: Self-evolving language models can continuously acquire useful experience through test-time interaction, reflection, and prompt optimization, yet turning such experience into model itself to ensure self improvement remains challenging. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides a natural mechanism for internalizing test-time information into model parameters, yet it largely assumes that the gener- ated experience is worth learning. We show that this assumption does not always hold: experiences that improve test-time performance may provide limited or even harmful training signals. To better characterize which experience should be inter- nalized, we systematically analyze diverse mutated experiences across multiple tasks and reflection models, and find that gradient-based alignment is a more reli- able indicator of downstream distillation gains than immediate test-time improve- ment.
items.author: Haoyuan Li, Gangyi Zhang, Dong Wang et al.

items.title: Thermal state preparation with shallow quantum circuits
items.summary: Preparing thermal states on noisy quantum hardware requires circuits that remain shallow at low temperatures. Even when accurate classical state representations are available, compiling them into suitable circuits can be costly. We introduce PP-VarQITE, combining Pauli propagation with variational quantum imaginary-time evolution to determine circuit parameters entirely classically, with target temperatures encoded in the angles of a fixed circuit architecture. In numerical studies of Ising and frustrated Heisenberg models, we recover low-temperature energies and correlations using up to 100 qubits. Across the frustrated chain and two-dimensional lattice, our circuits are approximately two to ten times shallower than the lowest-depth circuits from sequential tensor-network compilation.
items.author: Cenk Tüysüz, Simon Deconihout, Enrico Rinaldi et al.

items.title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules
items.summary: Neural architecture search and LLM-driven evolution often reduce evaluation to a scalar fitness score, discarding failures that could explain why designs succeed or fail. We present a hypothesis-driven architecture discovery loop in which LLM agents diagnose structured error patterns, formulate falsifiable hypotheses, test counterfactual controls under a frozen nnU-Net pipeline, and distill validated mechanisms into executable trigger-to-action rules. Across eight search waves, the loop identifies two principles for 3D medical image segmentation. First, reallocating computation from high-resolution decoders to the mid-encoder preserves thin-anatomy boundaries while reducing cost. Second, support-confined region contrast addresses errors between nested anatomical compartments, with anatomy-dependent triggers selecting when the rule applies.
items.author: Songtao Jiang, Yuan Wang, Fucheng Niu et al.

items.title: Does Research-Paper Context Improve LLM-Generated Quadruped Navigation? An Exploratory Simulation Study
items.summary: Large language models can write competent robot navigation code, but not only does the research on the topic advance, a model may also, due to the volume of findings, fail to recall relevant findings and apply them to the task at hand. In this work, we test whether providing particular research papers as context improves the LLM-written navigation code for the Go2 quadruped, with the LLM (Claude Opus 5) and locomotion policy frozen. Specifically, we compare the navigation controllers the LLM writes when provided with and without particular papers across three settings: behavior trees, navigators edited from a shared base, and controllers written from scratch.
items.author: Barnabas Juhasz, Rolf Pfister

items.title: The Activity Geometry of Discrete Generative Sampling
items.summary: Iterative refinement is a key capability of diffusion-based generation and has motivated growing efforts to bring similar behavior to discrete diffusion and flow models. A growing line of work enables such refinement by allowing previously generated tokens to be revised during sampling, thereby shaping the coupling between successive sampling states. Despite its growing role in sampler design, this coupling freedom remains insufficiently characterized. We introduce Activity Geometry to study these finite-step couplings through expected transition cost, which we call activity. We show that activity decomposes into the minimum required by the induced marginal transport and an excess term arising from the coupling.
items.author: Xinlong Guo, Jie Zhang, Lingyou Zhou

items.title: The DBI critical electric field in stationary non-diagonal geometries
items.summary: We investigate the critical electric field for the holographic Schwinger effect in general stationary non-diagonal geometries. We show that, in such backgrounds, the DBI reality condition must be formulated in terms of the electric field measured in a local orthonormal frame, since the coordinate components of the field strength need not represent a purely electric field in that frame. The critical field measured in the orthonormal frame takes the universal value \(E_{\mathrm{proper},c}=T_F\), while its coordinate expression depends on the background geometry. The resulting critical field is independently confirmed by the holographic potential analysis, through the disappearance of the potential barrier.
items.author: Leila Shahkarami

items.title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
items.summary: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom.
items.author: Miguel A. L. Marques, Irene D'Amico, Stefano Pittalis

items.title: Quantum Coherence and Basis-Dependent Correlations in Quantum Systems
items.summary: Quantum coherence and quantum correlations are two fundamental features of quantum systems and are closely related in various quantum information tasks. In general, due to the existence of correlations, the amount of coherence in a bipartite state should be no less than that in the reduced states. We focus on what types of states have an equal amount of coherence in the global state and the local states. For such states, the basis-dependent correlations (the difference between the coherence of a bipartite state and its reduced state with respect to a set of standard orthogonal local bases) vanish. Based on the Tsallis relative entropy coherence measure, we prove that block-diagonal product states exhibit vanishing basis-dependent correlations.
items.author: Zi-Han Chen, Hui Zhao, Shao-Ming Fei et al.

items.title: Any2Act: Scaling In-Context Robot Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrations
items.summary: Robot in-context learning (ICL) enables a policy to perform unseen tasks by following contextual demonstrations, without task-specific fine-tuning. This is increasingly valuable as large language models reasoning at low frequency can specify tasks through demonstrations and delegate high-frequency execution to such a policy. However, methods conditioned on human videos are bounded by scarce human-robot pairs, while those conditioned on robot demonstrations accept only one or two source types at limited scale. We present Any2Act, a foundation model for robot ICL. Our key insight is that a demonstration should be expressed in the camera layout and action space of the robot that performs it (the executor), not of whoever provided it (the demonstrator).
items.author: Ziang Ren, Zifan Wang, Zhuoyang Li et al.

items.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
items.summary: Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP).
items.author: Weicong Zhang, Yuan Huang, Yu Zheng et al.

items.title: D0-brane bound states in Matrix theory: nonperturbative bounds on matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape
items.summary: In Matrix theory, a single eleven-dimensional supergraviton is associated with a BPS bound state of D0-branes. Assuming the existence of a normalized physical BPS state, we derive nonperturbative bounds on its matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape from supersymmetry in the BFSS model. The probability of matrix configurations smaller than a fixed fraction of an explicit extent scale is exponentially suppressed in the square of the number $N$ of D0-branes. In Yang-Mills variables, this scale for the trace-normalized extent is of order the cube root of the 't Hooft coupling. Relative noncommutativity, measured by a dimensionless commutator ratio, has an expectation bounded by a quantity of order the inverse of $N$, and its probability of exceeding a sufficiently large fixed multiple of the inverse of $N$ vanishes at large $N$.
items.author: Tetsuyuki Muramatsu

items.title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
items.summary: Resolving local atomic structures such as defects and interfaces from electron microscopy contrast relies heavily on researcher judgement, leading to low efficiency and subjective standards. Here we present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided and expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that turns one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable capabilities by updating executable operators, parameters and routing rules with versioned inheritance. Given researcher-defined tasks, the system selects analysis paths from image features without expert labels, while testing and inheriting code updates under fixed budgets. Combining physical priors with expert feedback improves atomic point-defect detection over larger models and raises cross-material interface coverage from 5.13% to 72.11% within a 10% area budget.
items.author: Yaotian Yang, Sijia Tao, Yuping Zhang et al.

items.title: Quantum Tautochrone for photons and atoms
items.summary: The tautochrone problem, in which the travel time to a common point is independent of the starting position, has served as a foundational model in classical mechanics. Here we establish its quantum counterpart in engineered photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices, where nonuniform couplings drive photons and particles launched from different positions to converge simultaneously at a common site. Using higher-order correlation functions, we show that this quantum tautochrone effect holds for both bosons and fermions, with quantum statistics governing the character of the convergence: bosons converge onto the same site, while fermions, constrained by Pauli exclusion, gather at neighboring sites.
items.author: Georgios K. Simopoulos, Georgios E. Pavlou, Ioannis Kiorpelidis et al.

items.title: Putting a Robot on a Phone Call: Layered Signaling, Bounded Occupancy and Turn Arbitration over WebRTC
items.summary: We put a Thor robot on a browser voice call, with speech sent from Safari, answers played through the robot's loudspeaker and transcripts returned to the phone. We separate HTTPS signaling, relayed WebRTC media and speech generation into independently observable routes. The browser prefetches relay credentials and allows a 500 ms window after its first relay candidate. The backend starts speech and WebRTC-answer preparation concurrently within a 55 s deadline. A session slot and a non-blocking speaker lock coordinate calls with local voice access. A 2 s gate gives the controller an opportunity to suppress chat before playback. Fifteen of sixteen first dials reached ready-to-speak, comprising seven of eight Wi-Fi calls with a median of 5.57 s and eight of eight cellular calls with a median of 6.76 s.
items.author: Zheyuan Zhang, Zaide Zhang

items.title: Curvilinear nanomagnets of non-trivial geometric topology
items.summary: In this Chapter, we focus on the question of how the global geometric characteristics given by the topology of the sample's shape are reflected in the properties of the magnetization field of the given curvilinear nanoarchitecture. We start with a brief introduction to differential geometry and topology, giving their connection to the specific properties of the vector field represented by the magnetization field defined at the specific manifold. Then we discuss modern fabrication and characterization techniques that make analysis of a sample's topology not only an interesting theoretical concept but also a directly accessible and practically relevant topic. The main attention of the Chapter is dedicated to the theoretical and experimental analysis of nanostructrures with the topology different from the extended films beyond the in-depth studied topic of tubes of the constant radius.
items.author: Vagson L. Carvalho-Santos, Luke A. Turnbull, Naëmi Leo et al.

items.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
items.summary: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it.
items.author: Andrea Pelissetto, Davide Rossini, Ettore Vicari

items.title: Covalent Welding of Two-Dimensional Molecular Sheets into Ultra-Stiff, Super-Tough Polymeric Networks
items.summary: Since the inception of macromolecular science, polymers have been constructed from zero-dimensional monomers, a paradigm that funnels all stress through discrete one-dimensional chains. Driven by conformational entropy, polymer chains inevitably coil in three-dimensional space, precluding effective stress transfer, thereby compromising the ultimate mechanical performance. Two-dimensional (2D) molecular sheets, with intrinsic in-plane rigidity, could in principle circumvent this constraint. Yet in existing assemblies, where stress transfers efficiently within each molecular sheet but poorly between them, their exceptional properties fail to translate to the macroscale. Here, we demonstrate a 2D highly oriented molecular network (2D HOMN), an ultra-stiff, super-tough polymeric material constructed by the solid-state covalent welding of assembled 2D polyaramid sheets with flexible linkers pre-grafted at their peripheries.
items.author: Xiaoli Gong, Guohu Luo, Jiaxin Wu et al.

items.title: Assessing the total mass of the Planck protocluster candidates with CMB lensing stacking
items.summary: Galaxy clusters in formation, or protoclusters, are important sites regarding the evolution of large scale structures and the star formation history of the Universe. With a few exceptions, only their member galaxies have been routinely observed so far. The majority of their mass is expected to be under the form of non baryonic dark matter and cold intergalactic gas. The Planck high redshift star-forming field sample compiles 2151 protocluster candidates, among which 1012 fall within the footprint of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). The lensing of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) by foreground structures allows us to try and assess the total mass of these protoclusters for the first time.
items.author: Tanguy Dusserre, Hervé Dole, Mathieu Langer et al.

items.title: Studies of dual ions arriving time reconstruction in N$ν$DEx time projection chamber
items.summary: The N$ν$DEx experiment aims to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of \(^{82}\)Se with a high-pressure \(^{82}\)SeF\(_6\) negative-ion time projection chamber. In the assumed two-carrier model, the arrival-time separation of SeF\(_5^-\) and SeF\(_6^-\) can estimate the longitudinal coordinate without an external trigger. We compare FFT deconvolution and direct waveform fitting on simulated Topmetal-S charge-sensitive-amplifier waveforms. With the fixed amplifier response, direct fitting and FFT accepted 873 and 855 of 873 geometry-selected single depositions, respectively. On the 855 common events, the arrival-time separation RMSEs were 0.180 and 0.222 ms. Numerical depth calibration gave mean \(z\) residuals of 0.036 and 0.075 cm and RMSEs of 0.192 and 0.208 cm on 848 common events.
items.author: Tianyu Liang, Hulin Wang, Kai Chen et al.

items.title: Periodic and quasiperiodic structures produced by microphase separation in one-component simple liquids with competing interactions
items.summary: Competing interactions can generate frustration which suppresses macroscopic-scale phase separation, superseding it with separation patterns on the microscopic scale. This phenomenon, referred to as microphase separation, produces thermodynamically stable mesoscopic-scale periodic patterns in systems of different physical nature. The studies of this effect follow two paradigms. First, in block copolymers, the macroscopic-scale separation of chemically distinct components is prevented by the covalent bonds between them. In the other, the microscopic-scale separation is produced in simple single-component liquids by the competition between a short-range attraction and a long-range repulsion (SALR) in the pair potential, the separation occurring between a dense phase and a gas.
items.author: Lorenzo Agosta, Alfredo Metere, Mikhail Dzugutov

items.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
items.summary: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). The 1T-derived structures remain metallic and magnetic throughout, with $U$ acting mainly as a spectral renormalization.
items.author: Rashmi Ranjan Routaray, Ali Ghojavand, Eric Bousquet

items.title: A quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder for robust anomaly detection at the LHC
items.summary: Model-agnostic searches for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider utilise unsupervised anomaly detection, where quantum and neuromorphic detectors represent potential approaches. We develop the first fully spiking variational autoencoder, a quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder (QSVAE), built on the quantum-inspired leaky integrate-and-fire (QLIF) neuron. In this work we recast the neuron from a measurement-based circuit to a differentiable computational unit. This neuron is benchmarked against other classical, spiking, and quantum models on an LHC di-jet latent space. We show that under noise perturbations the QLIF network retains $0.95$ of its clean accuracy, while accuracy retention for twelve classical models falls to $0.74$-$0.85$.
items.author: Dean Brand, Donovan Slabbert, Chanelle Matadah Manfouo et al.

items.title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
items.summary: Training humanoid vision-language-action (VLA) models relies heavily on costly real-robot teleoperation. Recent efforts convert egocentric human demonstrations into humanoid training data. However, most methods still require wearable motion trackers and leave important hand-object interaction cues implicit. Many also mix in real-robot teleoperation data for VLA post-training. These dependencies limit scalable data collection, while implicit interaction cues make precise contact harder to learn. To overcome these limitations, we propose EgoLoAF, the first paradigm to derive all training data for humanoid loco-manipulation directly from egocentric demonstrations without wearable motion trackers. We post-train the VLA on the converted data alone, without real-robot teleoperation demonstrations, and use explicit hand-object interaction cues to guide action generation.
items.author: Yiming Zeng, Jiangyuxuan Dai, Yuheng Na et al.

items.title: Rydberg Constraint Ensembles for Nonnative Binary Optimization
items.summary: Rydberg blockade can exclude the configuration that minimizes a binary objective. We expand its finite penalties into a weighted ensemble of exclusion graphs. The full ensemble preserves the ground energy, and the interactions remaining on each graph set its local detunings. In simulations of two coupled squares, reversing a target coupling leaves the single-site energy slopes at uniform occupation unchanged, yet a collective mode of the residual interactions switches the favored diagonals from aligned to opposed. On 32 held-out twelve-site targets, the simulated probability of recovering a ground state in 128 shots averages 69.82\% with residual detunings and 24.31\% with a tuned uniform pulse.
items.author: Zecheng Shen

items.title: RoboDemo: Reconciling Demonstration Intent and Execution Progress for Long-Horizon Manipulation
items.summary: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires more than predicting the next action from the current observation. The policy must maintain a global procedural prior that specifies the expected progress of each subtask stage, while also tracking the realized progress produced by its interactions. To this end, we propose RoboDemo, a demonstration-augmented manipulation framework built on Dual-Cascaded Test-Time-Training. RoboDemo accepts either a task-relevant human demonstration video or a semantically compatible robot video retrieved from simulation corpus as reference, allowing us to evaluate its applicability with and without paired human demonstrations. Task semantics and physical motion information from the reference video are then transferred into persistent demonstration-intent memory.
items.author: Xiangkai Ma, Zhihao Yuan, Linbo Zhai et al.

items.title: Symmetry-dependent field-induced elastic renormalization in the quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy NiCoCr$_{0.8}$
items.summary: We investigate the elastic response of cubic NiCoCr$_{0.8}$, a quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy, by high-precision ultrasound velocity measurements. At zero magnetic field, the three symmetrically independent elastic moduli $C_{11}$, $(C_{11}-C_{12})/2=C_t$, and $C_{44}$ monotonically harden upon cooling without pronounced elastic softening or anomalies. In magnetic fields applied along [110], however, a minute but systematic elastic renormalization of the order of $10^{-5}$ is resolved at low temperatures. The tetragonal $E_g$ mode $C_t$ softens with increasing field, whereas the derived bulk $A_{1g}$ mode $C_B$ hardens, revealing an opposite field response between the two strain-symmetry channels. Comparison with the previously reported quantum-critical-Fermi-liquid crossover scale shows that the field-induced elastic renormalization develops already in the quantum-critical regime and evolves continuously across the crossover region, without a sharp elastic anomaly or threshold behavior.
items.author: Tadataka Watanabe, Mai Watanabe, Brian C. Sales

items.title: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
items.summary: While quantum protocols for oblivious transfer can be built from weaker assumptions than classical ones, the current protocols remain highly impractical due to stringent security bounds that demand a large amount of quantum communication. In this work, we propose an enhancement to quantum oblivious transfer protocols by leveraging zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs). At a high level, we modify the protocol such that the receiver proves that they are following honestly some crucial steps of the protocols, without revealing extra information to the sender. This yields a tighter security bound against a malicious receiver. For practical scenarios with a fixed security target, this approach reduces the amount of required quantum communication by one to two orders of magnitude, depending on the specific parameters.
items.author: Alex Bredariol Grilo, Lucas Hanouz, Anne Marin

items.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
items.summary: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients.
items.author: Zhi-Rong Deng, Jie Yang

items.title: Magnetometry and slow light in PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics
items.summary: The generation of optical higher-order sidebands, which produces new frequencies with regular spectral separation, holds significant promise for applications in optical communication and quantum metrology. We investigate second-order sideband generation and tunable slow-fast light effects in a parity-time (PT)-symmetric cavity optomechanics and propose an enhanced magnetometer scheme. We demonstrate that the PT-symmetric structure, an external magnetic field, and the photon tunneling strength provide powerful and flexible control over both the second-order sideband efficiency, as well as the broadening and switching of slow-fast light propagation. Operating in the PT-symmetry-protected phases, our magnetometer based on the second-order sideband achieves a theoretical sensitivity at the picotesla level, surpassing the performance of previous optomechanical approaches.
items.author: Yuguo Su, Tianshun Tan, Yiying Yan et al.

items.title: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
items.summary: Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion hinder Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. Here we propose a laser-driven route toward transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering that combines photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning. Classical relaxation and zero-temperature fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo trap benchmarks show that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T to sub-Tesla fields, defining ultrafast preparation targets.
items.author: Yiming Pan, Jiapeng Yang, Hao Geng

items.title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV II: D series models
items.summary: Three-state Potts gravity and tetracritical Ising gravity have the same central charge and the same conformal spectral curve. What distinguishes their amplitudes once a handle or a boundary is added? We answer this question by extending Johnson's differential-equation approach, in the reconstruction form developed in Part I for the reduced KP hierarchies, to D-series minimal strings. Their spatial operator is a pseudo-differential pencil with a nonlocal Pfaffian term, and the classical energy acquires a second pole at zero momentum. Regularity at both poles fixes the quantum corrections uniquely, ordinary string equations supply them, and the ordinary D flows add boundaries in a way that matches the tau function.
items.author: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar

items.title: Emission regimes and characteristic energy scales in reverse-biased 4H-SiC Schottky barriers: unified field-emission formulas and energy-dependent tunneling effective mass
items.summary: Reverse leakage in 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes is analyzed using a current integral with Fermi-Dirac supply and WKB transmission. The ratio of the interface field to a critical field $F_c$ sets the depth of the thermionic-field-emission (TFE) saddle point. The Airy energy distinguishes the thermionic-tunneling crossover, the validity of the TFE formula, and the TFE/field-emission (FE) boundary, which generalizes to $c_1 k_B T \approx 1$ for arbitrary barrier shapes. Closed-form FE and TFE expressions are given for triangular and quadratic barriers; for the latter, the Padovani-Stratton formulas give 1.4-7.9 times (FE, $10^{19}$ cm$^{-3}$) and 2.5-3.6 times (TFE, low-doped layers, 300-433 K) the WKB current, whereas the present expressions agree within 15% and 2%.
items.author: Tetsuo Hatakeyama

items.title: Tweezing microparticles by tightly focused optical skyrmionic fields
items.summary: The concept of skyrmions, once translated to the optical domain, provides a topological framework to investigate structured light-matter interactions. However, their practical use for the manipulation of material systems remains barely explored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate trapping and tunable orbital motion of dielectric microparticles in tightly focused skyrmionic polarization textures prepared using a compact spin-orbit optical element. We explore the tweezing capabilities at fixed topology either by varying the relative weights of the orthogonally polarized components or by switching between skyrmion and bimeron polarization textures. Vectorial focusing and optical-force calculations qualitatively reproduce the experimental observations. These results motivate extending skyrmionic light to the manipulation of micro-objects, including birefringent and chiral samples.
items.author: Liuhao Zhu, Hao Zhang, Xi Xie et al.

items.title: Competing Symmetry Breakings and Spontaneous Parity Restoration in Desynchronously Pumped Kerr Resonators
items.summary: Symmetry breaking is a cornerstone of nonlinear science, where stronger driving typically compounds parity loss across coupled degrees of freedom. Here, we uncover a counterintuitive symmetry-restoring transition driven by the competition between internal spontaneous polarization symmetry breaking (PSB) and external explicit temporal symmetry breaking (TSB) in desynchronously pumped Kerr resonators. Tuning pump-cavity desynchronization steers dissipative cavity solitons from pure PSB, through a robust hybrid symmetry-breaking (HSB) regime where both asymmetries coexist, into a pure TSB state accompanied by the abrupt, spontaneous restoration of polarization parity. Using collective-coordinate perturbation theory, we map the effective Ginzburg-Landau potential landscape and show that kinematic drift weakens local driving until a saddle-node bifurcation eliminates the temporal confining barrier.
items.author: Jun Ji, Zhibin Ren, Benli Yu et al.

items.title: Entanglement structure in conformal Y-junctions
items.summary: We study how entanglement constrains energy transmission in conformal Y-junctions using holographic and free-field models. We define pairwise effective central charges from mutual information as a natural extension of the interface entanglement coefficient. For holographic junctions, we formulate a branched RT prescription and show that the resulting entropies satisfy monogamy of mutual information. We find that the pairwise effective central charge does not always bound the corresponding energy transmission, but a correction involving finite tripartite information restores the bound, with a sharp coefficient determined by limiting saturation. Free-boson and Dirac-fermion junctions also violate the pairwise bound, but the tripartite correction fails because the tripartite information is positive or vanishing, respectively.
items.author: Yan Liu, You-Jie Zeng

items.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
items.summary: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential.
items.author: Ji Wang

items.title: M5-branes wrapped on topological disks from maximal 7D gauged supergravity
items.summary: We study new supersymmetric $AdS_5 \times Σ$ solutions for $Σ$ being a topological disk from the maximal gauged supergravity in seven dimensions with $CSO(p,q,5-p-q)$ gauge groups. These gauged supergravities can be obtained from consistent truncations of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $H^{p,q} \circ T^{5-p-q}$. We find a number of solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ and $SO(3,2)$ gauge groups as well as $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetric solutions from $SO(5)$ and $SO(4,1)$ gauge groups. Solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry preserve $16$ supercharges while the other solutions preserve only $8$ supercharges. Although some of the solutions give a holographic description of the dual $N=1$ SCFTs in four dimensions with finite central charges, most of the solutions describe codimension-2 defects within $N=(2,0)$ theories in six dimensions.
items.author: Patharadanai Nuchino, Parinya Karndumri

items.title: NS5-branes and the black hole/string transition
items.summary: Near to the onset of BTZ black hole formation in string theory is a large ensemble of 6d BPS supergravity solutions sourced by slightly separated fundamental strings and Neveu-Schwarz fivebranes. We extend the construction of these geometries to include gauge excitations of the fivebranes, and then study the energetics of D-string solitons in relation to the deconfinement transition of little strings, which are the natural non-abelian degrees of freedom that deconfine in the transition to the black hole phase.
items.author: Asad Fayiz, Emil J. Martinec

items.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
items.summary: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pmλ_{1},\pmλ_{2}$ satisfying $0<λ_{1} < λ_{2} < 2λ_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium.
items.author: Sajjad Bakrani

items.title: M 4.5 - 9 km NNW of La Tronosa, Panama
items.summary: A magnitude 4.5 earthquake was recorded 9 km NNW of La Tronosa, Panama. The event happened on 24 November 2026 at 01:55 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 16 km. About 2 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Temporal Soliton Waves in Modern Fiber Laser Systems
items.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of temporal soliton-wave in modern fiber systems. Temporal soliton waves constitute a broad class of nonlinear localized structures in modern fiber laser systems, arising from different balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, spectral filtering, and various forms of cavity coupling. We review the underlying theory, basic experimental findings, and practical methods for the generation, real-time characterization, and active control of soliton families, with a particular focus on recent progress reported for mode-locked fiber-laser platforms. The families covered in the chapter include dissipative solitons, soliton molecules (bound states), and dispersion-managed solitons. For each species, we focus on the pulse energy, duration, stationary and breathing states, and emerging intelligent (machine-learning-assisted) control strategies.
items.author: Shilong Liu, Boris Malomed

items.title: M 5.3 - 67 km WNW of Mangan, India
items.summary: A magnitude 5.3 earthquake was recorded 67 km WNW of Mangan, India. The event happened on 24 November 2026 at 01:32 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. About 54 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
items.summary: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension.
items.author: Mari Carmen Bañuls, Krzysztof Cichy, C. -J. David Lin et al.

items.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
items.summary: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum.
