The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution.
items.author: Juan Hormaza, Wenyang Qian

items.title: Mechanisms of turnkey soliton generation in self-injection-locked photonic-crystal ring resonators
items.summary: Turnkey generation of dissipative Kerr solitons in photonic-crystal ring resonators relies on the interplay between engineered mode splitting, self-injection locking, and modulation instability, yet the mechanism governing soliton initiation and number selection remains incompletely understood. We investigate this interplay using coupled Lugiato-Lefever equations with a self-consistent nonlinear self-injection-locking condition. Analysis of continuous-wave steady states and their locking stability reveals operating points accessible through feedback-induced transitions between split resonances. Evaluating modulation-instability gain at these points identifies conditions for comb initiation and links the dominant unstable sideband modes to soliton-number selectivity. Direct time-domain simulations corroborate the analysis, showing that appropriately chosen mode splitting enables highly repeatable single-soliton generation without external laser-frequency scans.
items.author: Naoya Kuse

items.title: Concurrent Clinical Experiential Learning and Health Systems Science Education for Undergraduate Pre-Professional Students.
items.summary: Pre-professional undergraduates often have limited opportunities for meaningful clinical participation or structured instruction linking their experiences to the broader organization and delivery of healthcare. We describe the design and formative evaluation of an undergraduate course pairing supervised clinical experiential learning with health systems science instruction.
items.author: Crick JP, Alain GN, Southerland L, Thomas E, Quatman C, Quatman-Yates CC.

items.title: Letting Residents Teach Us: Lessons from a Resident-as-Teacher Elective.
items.summary: Even without formal training, residents are educators-of medical students, peers, patients, even faculty. Yet teaching-identity development is often implicit, not intentional. We describe a qualitative thematic review of end-of-rotation reflections from a Resident-as-Teacher elective to examine how our rotators internalized educational theory and to identify gaps for curricular improvement.
items.author: Geringer JL, Lindholm DA, Ford MB.

items.title: Developing an Applied Medical Spanish Elective for Students With Prior Spanish Proficiency: Evaluation of a Preclinical Curriculum.
items.summary: A medical Spanish elective was developed for students with prior Spanish proficiency to improve communication with Spanish-speaking patients. The elective included didactic lectures, role-play, and standardized patient encounters. Students showed increased confidence in interacting with Spanish-speaking patients, particularly among advanced learners.

items.summary: After years of mentoring medical students and young physicians, I have become wary of how easily a record of performance turns into a verdict about a person. Examinations matter, especially in a profession that owes patients demonstrable competence. Yet grades cannot tell us the whole story.
items.author: Andrade BB.

items.title: Multimorbidity Guidelines in Low- and Lower-Middle-Income Countries: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: Introduction Multimorbidity is an increasing global health concern that is growing in prevalence in low- and lower-middle income countries (LMICs). It is therefore important to understand the current policies and guidelines that are used to inform multimorbidity care in low-resource settings.
items.author: Smith TM, Ayinmode EO, Olabisi EO, Adesokan MM, Kolawole IO, Olufunmilola O M, Gibbs KD, Estill J, Wang Z, Burgers J, Babatunde OO.

items.summary: Osteoporosis poses a substantial health and financial burden. Although secondary causes are more common in men, they are screened less for osteoporosis than their female counterparts. We present the case of a 70-year-old man with a history of an adrenal incidentaloma with a recent diagnosis of 2 vertebral fractures.
items.author: Dahi I, Van Dorpe J, Verly E.

items.title: Induced ubiquitination drives ER protein degradation through a VCP-dependent pathway.
items.summary: Heterobifunctional proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable degradation of disease-relevant proteins but have largely been limited to cytosolic targets. Using reporter cell lines and the dTAG system to recruit cytosolic E3 ligases, we found that luminal substrates are resistant to degradation, whereas ER membrane proteins are efficiently degraded across multiple topologies.
items.author: Tomlinson SJ, Johnson SL, Kroskrity AH, Hu Y, Deol KK, Zhang CY, Harris CA, Nomura DK, Olzmann JA.

items.title: Deep cervical lymphatic-venous anastomosis attenuates neuroinflammation in experimental ischemic stroke.
items.summary: Impaired cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) lymphatic outflow may contribute to neuroinflammation and secondary brain injury after ischemic stroke, yet whether therapeutic augmentation of CSF lymphatic outflow improves stroke outcomes remains unknown. Here, we evaluated deep cervical lymphatic-venous anastomosis (dcLVA) in a rat model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO).

items.title: Temporal Evolution and Prognostic Value of Strong Ion Difference and Standard Base Excess in Critically Ill Children.
items.summary: Importance Acid-base disturbances are common in critically ill children and may provide important prognostic information. However, the relative and complementary prognostic value of the physicochemical strong ion difference (SID) and traditional standard base excess (SBE) frameworks, particularly when assessed longitudinally, remains incompletely understood.
items.author: Totapally BR, Jones J, Sendi P, Kobaitri K, Meyer K.

items.title: Economic Security as the New Anchor of Critical Minerals Governance and Global Energy Transition.
items.summary: The race for critical minerals has become inseparable from geopolitical tension and the clean energy transition. This study argues that an emerging doctrine of economic security has become the organising principle of critical minerals governance among major economies, reconfiguring the market-led multilateral arrangements that previously governed mineral supply chains.
items.author: Nem Singh JT, Zhang H.

items.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Diabetic Complications Among Type 2 Diabetes Patients in Addis Ababa Hospitals, Ethiopia: Cross-Sectional Study.
items.summary: Background and aims Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a growing public health concern globally and in Ethiopia. Its prevalence is rapidly increasing in urban settings like Addis Ababa, driven by rapid urbanization, changing lifestyles, and dietary habits, which in turn escalates the burden of its complications.

items.summary: Background and aims Patients with cirrhosis are at risk of death not only from complications of liver disease but also from infection and comorbid conditions. We aimed to describe how the interplay between COVID-19 pandemic and reasons for terminal hospitalization in patients with cirrhosis.

items.summary: The objective of this study was to evaluate whether toxicity-weighted pesticide exposure improves county-level cancer models, whether endpoint-matched metrics provide different model performance, and whether observed associations persist after accounting for spatial dependence and geographic validation. Data were collected for 3,107 U.S.

This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of physician-diagnosed kidney stone history and examine its demographic, socioeconomic, behavioral, anthropometric, metabolic, and clinical correlates among adults participating in the Tabari Cohort Study (TCS) in northern Iran.

Vitamins, including B6, B12, and D, support sleep regulation via neurotransmitter synthesis and circadian pathways. However, empirical data evaluating student literacy and dietary practices regarding these micronutrients remain scarce in low-resource African settings.

If chromosomal breakage testing is unavailable, phenotype with marrow morphology and exome sequencing can establish Fanconi anemia. A genetic diagnosis achieves little without structured follow-up: this child returned 9 months later with hemoglobin 2.2 g/dL.

Methods We conducted a retrospective multicenter case series of eight pediatric patients with RRP who failed conventional surgical and local adjuvant therapies and were subsequently treated with systemic bevacizumab.

items.summary: Fibrosis is a maladaptive repair process marked by fibroblast activation, myofibroblast accumulation, and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, which can compromise tissue architecture and organ function. Its causes, cellular niches, reversibility, and therapeutic windows vary across the lung, liver, kidney, and heart.

We report, to our knowledge, the first airborne recordings of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) and buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum), with gas exchange and chlorophyll fluorescence on the same plants.
items.author: Saha, B., Haque, M. I., Strozecki, M. et al.

items.title: Differential DNA methylation and transcriptome revealed enhanced photosynthetic recovery and ROS modulation to promote cold tolerance in Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica.
items.summary: Indica rice, being a tropical crop, is highly sensitive to cold temperatures. Cold stress affects vegetative growth, photosynthetic efficiency and reproductive features. Screening diverse landraces to identify novel alleles associated with cold tolerance can be an approach to develop cold resilient indica rice.
items.author: Roy, V., Parveen, R., Dasgupta, P. et al.

items.title: Two copy-number forms of the Kala4/OsB2 upstream duplication in purple rice revealed by a telomere-to-telomere genome of landrace ZN65
items.summary: Background: Black and purple pericarp in rice requires activation of the regulator Kala4/OsB2. The canonical black-rice allele is a promoter rearrangement that was described from DNA gel blots and amplified fragments, and its sequence is unavailable. Whether pigmented landraces carry one upstream structure or several is therefore unknown.
items.author: Zhao, F., Zhao, J., Zhao, F. et al.

items.title: Individual neurons in monkey sensory and prefrontal cortices contribute to both working memory maintenance and readout
items.summary: Despite extensive research, the neural implementation of working memory, from information maintenance to readout that guides behavior, remains elusive. We provide direct evidence that neurons in auditory and prefrontal cortices of monkeys maintain tone-specific information via persistent changes in spiking during the memory delay.
items.author: Huang, Y., Brosch, M.

items.title: Connexin43 drives mitochondrial biogenesis and organelle stress in BRAF-mutant melanoma cells
items.summary: Metabolic flexibility helps cancer cells survive targeted therapy, and BRAF-mutant melanoma rewires mitochondrial metabolism in response to BRAF/MEK inhibitors (BRAF/MEKi). We previously showed that connexin43 (Cx43) acts as a tumour suppressor in BRAF-mutant melanoma and enhances the response to BRAF/MEKi.
items.author: Guitian-Caamano, A., Fernandez-Bejarano, E., De Jesus-Sen, C. et al.

items.title: Population-scale immunoglobulin genomics links inherited variation to antibody repertoire organization
items.summary: Human antibody repertoires emerge from inherited immunoglobulin variation interacting with V(D)J recombination and selection, yet how population-level germline diversity contributes to repertoire organization remains incompletely understood. We integrated long-read genomic data across the IGH, IGK, and IGL loci from 871 individuals, including 172 individuals with matched antibody repertoire sequencing.
items.author: Peres, A., Jana, U., Rodriguez, O. et al.

items.title: Identifying a cooperative catalytic network for efficient esterase catalysis
items.summary: Efficient catalysis is hard to engineer because sequence comparisons reveal only a handful of conserved catalytic residues, and single substitutions rarely speed up catalysis. We hypothesize that efficient catalysis requires a cooperative catalytic network of residues enabling the physical and chemical steps that together determine kcat.
items.author: Sarak, S., Yang, H., Pierce, C. et al.

items.title: The use of cultured symbionts enhances the survival of reef-deployed coral recruits
items.summary: Introduction: Symbiodiniaceae dinoflagellates are essential for coral juvenile development and survival, yet early-life symbiont provisioning remains underused in coral restoration. Objectives: We tested whether inoculating sexually propagated Acropora spathulata recruits with cultured symbionts before reef deployment improves survival and shapes symbiont community composition.
items.author: Pfeffer, E., Nitschke, M., Ferguson, S. et al.

items.title: Apple floral attractants function across the 24-hour cycle to support potential diurnal and nocturnal pollinators
items.summary: Pollination in apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) is typically attributed to diurnal bees, yet nocturnal insects also contribute to fruit set. To assess whether apple flowers recruit potential pollinators throughout the 24-hour cycle, we quantified diel patterns in floral attractants and insect visitation in an orchard in Northwest Arkansas, United States.
items.author: Potdar, S., Kutcherov, D., Jennings, M. et al.

items.title: No evidence of evolution of male fitness components in response to yeast deprivation: Putative female specific nutrient dependent reproductive adaptation
items.summary: Intersexual genetic correlation (IGC) is pervasive in sexually reproducing organisms and can constrain sex-specific adaptive evolution. Nevertheless, sexes frequently undergo adaptive divergence in response to novel ecological challenges. Here, we investigated whether adaptation to nutritional stress is sex-limited or constrained by shared genetic architecture.
items.author: Adhikary, S., Pal, R. S., Halder, S. et al.

items.title: Brazil requests dispute panel regarding additional duties imposed by the United States
items.summary: At a meeting of the Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) on 24 November, members considered a request from Brazil for the establishment of a dispute panel to review additional US duties on products originating in Brazil as a result of two investigations by the United States under Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974.

items.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
items.summary: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface.
items.author: Md Saklain Morshed, John Cobbinah, Ijaas Mohamed et al.

items.title: Compact Slow-Wave Hybrid Magnonics on Ultrahigh-Permittivity Substrates
items.summary: Hybrid magnonics based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) enables strong, broadband magnon-photon coupling, but the centimeter-scale device footprints required at low gigahertz frequencies hinder integration. Here, we demonstrate miniaturized slow-wave hybrid magnonic devices using an ultrahigh-permittivity ceramic substrate ($\varepsilon = 140$).
items.author: Yu Jiang, Haiyang Yun, Zixin Yan et al.

items.title: Thermodynamic constraints on warm inflation with the Standard Model
items.summary: In warm inflation with the Standard Model (SM), an axion-like inflaton dissipates energy into the plasma through QCD sphaleron transitions. Current predictions assume a friction linear in the bias, defined as the free energy released per transition in units of the temperature. The friction, however, has only been simulated at moderate biases in pure SU(2) gauge theory. We show that, during slow roll, energy conservation, the axial anomaly and thermodynamics relate the bias to the quark chemical potentials generated by the transitions, independently of the form of the friction and of the reaction network in the plasma. A bias within the simulated range requires chemical potentials a few times the temperature, which typically lead to Higgs condensation.
items.author: Martin A. Mojahed

items.title: All the Positive Energy Correlators
items.summary: We develop a framework to systematically obtain the full set of positivity bounds on multi-point energy correlators for sources of arbitrary spin. The constraints are organized in a family of positive operators $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, with $k=0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor$. Our approach provides outer bounds, which exclude correlators that violate the positivity of $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, and inner bounds, obtained by constructing ensembles of consistent collider events via linear programming. Both methods converge to each other as numerical precision increases. This approach, in particular, characterizes the allowed higher-point correlators once lower-point correlators are determined. We illustrate this through several examples, including bounds on multipoles of the three-point energy correlator in QCD derived from measurements of one- and two-point correlators at LEP.
items.author: Lorenzo Ricci, Marc Riembau, Minho Son

items.title: M 4.6 - 130 km SSW of Merizo Village, Guam
items.summary: A magnitude 4.6 earthquake was recorded 130 km SSW of Merizo Village, Guam. The event happened on 23 November 2026 at 21:25 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 35 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Ultra-Wideband Stacked Patch Antenna for D-Band Applications
items.summary: This article proposes a wideband stacked dual-patch antenna designed for D-band applications. The antenna is demonstrated with both wireless and dielectric waveguide (DWG) channels. The patch dimensions and spacings are chosen to ensure that the $10~dB$ return loss (RL) bandwidth covers the entire D-band ($110$--$170~GHz$).
items.author: Mohamed Elsawaf, Neelam Prabhu Gaunkar, Georgios C. Dogiamis et al.

items.title: Dijet photoproduction in ep and eA collision in POWHEG
items.summary: We present the implementation of dijet photoproduction in electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions in the POWHEG BOX V2 Monte Carlo event generator. The process is computed at next-to-leading order in QCD including both direct and resolved photon contributions and is consistently matched to parton showers using the POWHEG method. The implementation is validated by using POWHEG BOX V2 internal consistency checks as well as by comparing fixed-order results with SHERPA. We compare our predictions to dijet photoproduction data from DESY HERA I and II, finding good agreement within theoretical uncertainties, and provide predictions for both electron-proton and electron-gold collisions at the upcoming BNL EIC, illustrating its potential to further constrain both photon and nuclear parton distribution functions.
items.author: Alexander Feike, Tomáš Ježo, Michael Klasen

items.title: Gluon GPDs from hard-exclusive electroproduction of heavy quarkonium at NLO
items.summary: Gluon tomography of the nucleon through hard-exclusive electroproduction of $J/ψ$ has been one of the key motivations for Electron-Ion Collider. However, the next-to-leading order (NLO) perturbative QCD calculations available in the literature were performed either in the collinear factorization limit where the heavy-quark mass is neglected, or in heavy-quark limit where the heavy quarkonia are approximately point-like. We present a full next-to-leading order collinear factorization for the hard exclusive production of heavy mesons that retains the meson mass as well as full light-cone distribution amplitude. We compare the full NLO result with the special limits and estimate the errors due to potentially-large corrections from $α_s(M)$ and $M^2/Q^2$ at this order.
items.author: Yuxun Guo, Xiangdong Ji, Yao Ji et al.

items.title: Quarkonium Energy Correlators in Proton-Proton Collisions: Analytic Calculation and Angular-Momentum Hierarchy
items.summary: We present the first complete leading-order (LO) analytic calculation of the quarkonium energy correlator (QEC) in $pp$ collisions, for the color-singlet ${}^3S_1^{[1]}$ and the color-octet ${}^1S_0^{[8]}$, ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$, and ${}^3P_J^{[8]}$ channels of $J/ψ$ production. Instead of the high-$p_T$ fragmentation approximation, the calculation retains the full kinematics of the recoil parton, inverts the map from transverse momentum to the rest-frame angle in closed form, and is validated by \textsc{HELAC-onia} in shape and absolute normalization. We also give the analytic counterpart of the $p_T$-weighted variant of the correlator. The LO shape of each channel is organized by the total angular momentum $J$ of the $c\bar c$ pair, as a consequence of the tree-level selection rule that forbids two on-shell gluons from forming a $J=1$ state.
items.author: June-Haak Ee, Christopher Lee, Bianka Meçaj et al.

items.title: Exotic Portals for Hadronic Processes: The Gluon-Gluon and Gluon-Quark Portals
items.summary: In this work we explore all possible light exotic (LEX) particles which are accessible through the gluon-gluon ($g$-$g$) and gluon-quark ($g$-$q$) phenomenological portals up to effective dimension six. We present effective models for these new states, which are directly accessible through gluon and quark fusion processes, and which are guaranteed decays involving Standard Model (SM) quarks and gluons. We note many accessible states in particularly unusual SU(3)$_\text{c}$ representations, which contain large Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. We also include some interesting dimension seven operators with highly unusual features. We also consider all potential spin values for our LEX states, looking at Lorentz representations and color selection rules.
items.author: Katherine Schwind, Linda M. Carpenter

items.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
items.summary: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models for autonomous driving use chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to guide action generation, but incur substantial memory and computational costs. We study structured pruning for these models, focusing on preserving both scene understanding and trajectory prediction. Our analysis of Taylor importance in Alpamayo-1.5-10B shows that reasoning and trajectory objectives assign different importance to the same vision-language model (VLM) structures. In the action expert, MLP channels exhibit more stable importance rankings across denoising steps than query heads, and a small fraction of channels accounts for most of the measured importance. Based on these findings, we propose MoOP, which combines importance ranks from both objectives for VLM pruning and aggregates stepwise importance to select a fixed subset of expert MLP channels.
items.author: Seongchan Kim, Soowon Son, Sangoh Kim et al.

items.title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
items.summary: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To address this challenge, we introduce Integral, which converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across the two capabilities. Integral implements this design through two complementary components.
items.author: JB Kim, Byungwoo Jeon, Kyungmin Lee et al.

items.title: Two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems
items.summary: Quantum interactive proof systems can be parallelized to three messages, as shown by Kitaev and Watrous (STOC 2000), perhaps their most striking distinction from classical counterparts. In this work, we establish that any quantum interactive proof system can further be parallelized to two messages, with the verifier sending halves of EPR pairs (``quantum public coins'') and, after the prover's response, using only stoquastic verification. Technically, we strengthen ${\sf QIP}(3) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}$ of Jain, Ji, Upadhyay, and Watrous (JACM, 2011) and fully characterize two-message quantum interactive proof systems by proving \[ {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf StoqAM} = {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf QAM} = {\sf QIP}(2) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}.
items.author: Yupan Liu

items.title: The Simons Observatory: Analysis of methods for polarization calibration of multiple instruments
items.summary: Cosmic birefringence, the rotation of the CMB linear polarization plane across the Universe, is a powerful test of parity-violating physics beyond the Standard Model. Static isotropic rotation, however, is limited by an instrument's absolute polarization-angle calibration. We present a method for transferring absolute calibration between Simons Observatory (SO) instruments, validated on map-level simulations of the Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) and Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) with lensed CMB polarization, polarized Galactic foregrounds, correlated instrumental noise, and polarization-angle miscalibration. We develop two pipelines: a joint LAT+SAT likelihood transferring calibration through their overlap, and the Minami-Komatsu foreground-based method, which separates cosmic birefringence from instrumental miscalibration using Galactic dust polarization without an external angle prior.
items.author: The Simons Observatory Collaboration, Anto I. Lonappan, Patricia Diego-Palazuelos et al.

items.title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: CLIP-style dual encoders map images and text through two separate towers into a shared embedding space, where the two modalities occupy distinct regions separated by a modality gap. Retrieval fails when wrong matches, or hard negatives, outrank the correct one, and the gap is the usual suspect. Yet removing it post hoc degrades retrieval on every CLIP checkpoint we test. We introduce a paired statistic that identifies directions where the two towers agree more on hard negatives than on matched pairs. Mildly attenuating these directions improves retrieval while largely preserving the gap. We arrive at this correction through weight-space programming: guided by the statistic, an LLM agent inspects both towers and writes closed-form weight edits without backpropagation.
items.author: Hani Alomari, Md Atabuzzaman, Chris Thomas

items.title: Nonabelianization map for the $W_{3,c=2}$ conformal blocks. Part I
items.summary: This work is inspired by the nonabelianization construction of Virasoro conformal blocks. We start the process of defining the nonabelianization map which expresses $c=2$ $W_3$-algebra conformal blocks on a Riemann surface $C$ from Heisenberg blocks on a branched triple cover $\tilde{C}$ of $C$. This generalized nonabelianization map uses the datum of a $\mathfrak{gl}_3$ spectral network on $C$ and we find that this map also depends on the soliton degeneracies corresponding to the spectral network even though the soliton data didn't show up explicitly in the Virasoro case. This nonabelianization construction defines new formulas for $W_3$-algebra conformal blocks on $C$ in terms of fermion correlation functions determined by the Heisenberg blocks on $\tilde{C}$.
items.author: Qianyu Hao

items.title: Simple design of adaptive protocols for quantum metrology with limited data
items.summary: Recent sensing experiments have used a Bayesian notion of precision gain to adapt control parameters for fixed measurements. Here, we advocate a simple design principle based on Personick's minimum mean square loss formalism to extend this procedure in order to include measurement optimisation, determining the optimal measurement for each probe and providing a prior-dependent precision gain to optimise the probe itself. This offers a Bayesian counterpart to protocol design based on the Fisher information, with a similar algebraic structure but incorporating the full prior. We apply this principle to adaptive phase estimation with single-mode Gaussian probes, showing that joint optimisation outperforms both adaptive homodyne detection and a fixed-probe strategy optimised for the initial prior, with a maximum reduction of 32% in mean posterior variance relative to homodyne detection.
items.author: Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Jesús Rubio

items.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
items.summary: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-4, 14.7B) across 15,200 math benchmark attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors within each model's capability frontier. Applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations across these failure points, we demonstrate a consistent decoupling between monitoring and control. On monitoring, all four models fail to detect their own errors.
items.author: Daniel Theron

items.title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling
items.summary: Understanding how genetic perturbations affect cellular behaviour is essential for studying gene function and regulatory mechanisms. Large-scale CRISPR screens measure these effects across thousands of genes, but cover relatively few cellular contexts. Predicting perturbation responses in unseen cell types and identifying perturbed genes from their transcriptional effects therefore remain challenging. Here, we show that both tasks can be addressed through a common linear decomposition of transcriptional responses into shared and perturbation-specific components. Building on this principle, we introduce BiPert, a simple linear framework for both forward perturbation prediction and inverse identification. For forward prediction, BiPert outperforms existing methods that use no external biological knowledge when predicting gene expression changes in unseen cell lines.
items.author: Abhishek Sharma, Aleksej Zelezniak

items.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
items.summary: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image.
items.author: Mohammad Hossein Moslemi, Mahdi Beitollahi, Zhimin Mei et al.

items.title: Small-World Networks Yield Tunable Quantum Codes at Short Circuit Depth
items.summary: Random Clifford circuits implemented on Watts-Strogatz small-world networks generate quantum error-correcting codes with tunable properties. By adjusting nonlocal graph rewiring, measurement rate, and circuit depth, researchers can create codes that form at logarithmic depths and exhibit low failure probabilities compared to local circuit designs.
items.author: Samuel Bevins, Gregory Bentsen
items.original_title: Small-world networks yield tunable quantum codes at short circuit depth
items.original_summary: Monitored random quantum circuits naturally generate quantum error-correcting codes. We generate quantum codes with tunable properties by implementing random Clifford circuits on Watts--Strogatz `small-world' networks and tailor code properties via three knobs: nonlocal graph rewiring, measurement rate, and circuit depth. On fully rewired networks, circuits of logarithmic depth produce codes with a finite rate and an extensive mean contiguous distance with failure probability substantially lower than codes produced from local circuits. These small-world codes form at a circuit depth growing as $\ln n$ compared to polynomial depths required for codes produced from local networks. Rewiring also moves the purification transition to higher measurement rates and changes its critical exponents.
items.ai_title: Small-World Networks Yield Tunable Quantum Codes at Short Circuit Depth
items.ai_summary: Random Clifford circuits implemented on Watts-Strogatz small-world networks generate quantum error-correcting codes with tunable properties. By adjusting nonlocal graph rewiring, measurement rate, and circuit depth, researchers can create codes that form at logarithmic depths and exhibit low failure probabilities compared to local circuit designs.

items.title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automation will help future mobile networks translate high-level network intents into concrete network optimization or control actions. However, existing approaches often focus on intent management and orchestration, leaving the adaptation of underlying network optimization and control functions largely unaddressed. This article proposes a triadic agentic AI framework that co-designs intent management and intent fulfillment through three agents: an interpreter, powered by a language model, that translates and refines intents into machine-readable optimization templates; an optimizer that adapts controller policies to intent specifications; and a controller that performs fast decision-making. We discuss the design space of each agent and how the workflow can be embedded across network architectural domains.
items.author: Burak Demirel, Yu Wang, Pablo Soldati

items.title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
items.summary: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each finding segmented. On the 200 ReXGroundingCT validation scans, CTLink achieved a hit rate of 0.816, an instance F1 score of 0.456, and a mean Dice score of 0.400, compared with 0.533, 0.175, and 0.234 for VoxTell, a publicly available text-prompted segmentation model (P < .001 for all).
items.author: Mohammed Baharoon, Sung Eun Kim, Mahmoud Hussain Alabbad et al.

items.title: LeJEPA Features Are Not Isotropic, and Should Not Be
items.summary: The SIGReg term in LeJEPA regularizes features to have an isotropic Gaussian distribution. Our first result is to show that this regularizer, in practice, cannot achieve its goal. We design a modified regularizer to enforce the objective better. This leads to slightly improved performance. For example, on ImageNet-100, our modified regularizer reaches the final accuracy of SIGReg in 1.3$\times$ fewer epochs. Our second result argues that self-supervised encoders should not have isotropic Gaussian features. We show that the alignment term in LeJEPA conflicts with SIGReg, because it couples the magnitude of the features with their directions. In contrast, isotropic Gaussian features would entail independent magnitude and directions.
items.author: Richeek Das, Pratik Chaudhari

items.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning.
items.author: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xuhui Li et al.

items.title: Massive de Sitter correlators at one loop
items.summary: Fermions and massive fields charged under an unbroken symmetry couple to the inflaton only in pairs, so their signals in primordial correlators begin at one loop. Templates for these signals are mostly late-time estimates. Starting from a representation of massive de Sitter correlators as finite Mellin-Barnes integrals, we compute the exact squeezed coefficients of these signals and their corrections away from the squeezed limit. The leading coefficient factorizes into a hard part and a soft vertex. Late-time estimates treat the hard part exactly but approximate the soft vertex by its late-time limit, whereas we compute both exactly. Without a chemical potential, the exact coefficient differs from the late-time one by a universal factor that depends only on the masses in the loop and the coupling at the soft vertex.
items.author: Amara McCune

items.title: Flood forecasting using a physics-guided conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model
items.summary: High-resolution flood forecasting with full two-dimensional shallow water equation (SWE) solvers remains computationally expensive, even on GPUs. We develop a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) that forecasts the evolution of 30 m water-depth fields over a four-day horizon for the Des Plaines River watershed, Illinois. The model is trained on SynxFlow SWE simulations of 113 historical storms observed across twelve Midwestern states (2003-2024), each under three antecedent-wetness scenarios, and can optionally be conditioned on coarse 100 m or 150 m hydrodynamic simulations. Because reverse diffusion is stochastic, every forecast is a 20-member ensemble drawn from the same trained model.
items.author: Omar Sallam, David Coe, Jeremy Feinstein et al.

items.title: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
items.summary: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.
items.author: Bikun Li, Guo Zheng, Liang Jiang

items.title: Solute-Aware Stochastic Korhonen Model of Electromigration in Wide vs Near-Bamboo Al-Cu Lines
items.summary: We couple an evolving Cu field to the one-dimensional Korhonen stress equation on random grain maps for wide (10 $μ$m), narrow (3 $μ$m) and near-bamboo Al-Cu lines. Earlier random-microstructure simulations fixed the Cu effect, and most continuum solute models used prescribed structures with all Cu mobile; we join the two and let only dissolved Cu move, the excess staying as immobile precipitate. With $10^3$ maps per condition at 200 $^\circ$C, we report nucleation times and sites, immortal fractions and Black's-law parameters. In cathode-limited lines Cu depletion shortens the median nucleation time 1.15- to 1.20-fold relative to immobile Cu for the cited Cu diffusivity; treating all Cu as mobile overstates this a further 2.24- to 2.36-fold at 2 wt%; the exponent stays near 2.
items.author: Narahara Chari Dingari, David R. Heskett

items.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
items.summary: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents.
items.author: Zexin He, Rui Li, Yushi Lan et al.

items.title: JAISP: A Joint Rubin-Euclid Foundation Model for Cross-Instrument Source Detection and Astrometry
items.summary: Joint pixel-level processing of Rubin and Euclid imaging promises deeper source detection and the cross-survey consistency that precision cosmology requires. We introduce JAISP (Joint AI Survey Processing), a foundation model that learns a single representation of ten-band imaging: Rubin ugrizy and Euclid VIS, Y, J, and H, from the first public releases over $\approx 0.2$ deg$^2$ of the ECDFS deep field. Trained without labels by predicting each band from the other nine, its frozen encoder drives small task-specific networks for source detection and astrometry. The detection network recovers nearly all VIS-selected Euclid Q1 catalog sources on held-out sky, and source injection shows that combining all ten bands extends the point-source detection limit by $\approx 0.3$ mag beyond VIS alone.
items.author: Shoubaneh Hemmati, George Helou, Yu-Heng Lin et al.

items.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
items.summary: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement.
items.author: Xiao-Ming Wu, Kang Liao, Yuexiao Ma et al.

items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.summary: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol.
items.author: Rui Sun, Junhua Huang, Luca Zancato et al.

items.title: VITA-WAM: Manifold-Aligned World-Action Modeling for Real-Time Robot Control
items.summary: World action model (WAM) is a promising paradigm for visuomotor control by jointly modeling world dynamics and actions. Notably, existing WAMs often rely on large generative models and iterative sampling which incur substantial latency for action generation, limiting real-time deployment. In particular, there are two root causes of inefficiency in conventional flow matching or diffusion based action models in WAMs: 1) transporting uninformative Gaussian noise into precise actions necessitating multiple ODE steps, and 2) repeatedly injecting task context through expensive cross-attention modules. Our key insight is that jointly learning and aligning the source and action manifolds streamlines the transport between them, substantially accelerating action generation.
items.author: Boqi Zhao, Dechen Gao, Hanchu Zhou et al.

items.title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations for fMRI generation. We first train a separate EEG encoder to predict each fMRI signal, learning target-specific temporal and spectral features from the same EEG window. After training, we freeze the encoders and project their concatenated hidden features into a shared neurovascular code. Conditioned on this code, stochastic interpolant transforms Gaussian noise into a vector of fMRI signals, allowing different responses to be sampled for the same EEG window. We evaluate our approach on eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets, including four resting-state and four task-based datasets with 61,646 volume-level pairs.
items.author: Yiming Sun, Yifan Wang, Aosong Feng et al.

items.title: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems often return queries that execute successfully but answer the wrong question. Detecting these errors at deployment is hard because execution correctness is defined against a gold query, which exists only in labeled data. We formulate confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation under a latent correctness variable that is observable at calibration time through gold-SQL execution and latent at deployment. Our estimator separates generation from validation. A generator LLM writes and executes the query, and a different critic LLM judges the query and its execution result. The critic's validation and execution-grounded alignment scores are fused with the generator's verbalized confidence, token-level uncertainty, and SQL-structural features in a Random Forest, using two sequential LLM calls.
items.author: Avinash Kumar Singh, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

items.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
items.summary: We perform the complete light-cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $κ$-symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which in its turn is required to be nonvanaishing and nontrivial in this limit. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar.
items.author: Igor Bandos

items.title: Self-guided estimation of the stabilizer fidelity with single-copy Pauli measurements
items.summary: The stabilizer fidelity quantifies the non-stabilizerness of pure states, but it is hard to estimate because it requires optimizing over $2^{O(n^2)}$ stabilizer states for $n$ qubits. Here, we propose a self-guided estimation protocol for the stabilizer fidelity of an unknown state, pure or mixed, which requires only Pauli measurements on single copies. The protocol moves through the graph of neighboring stabilizer states, obtains the fidelities of a whole stabilizer basis from a single direct fidelity estimation, and reuses previous outcomes, which also provide a restart point that mitigates the barren plateau of a random start. In addition, it certifies the global optimum when the lower confidence bound of the estimated fidelity exceeds $\cos^2(π/8)$.
items.author: M. Torres, J. Gidi, L. Pereira

items.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. We introduce CO-GRAFT, a reward-agnostic interventional attribution framework in which an RL-trained agent and its pre-RL initialization jointly generate a single trajectory under closed-loop execution with live retrieval. Each policy controls a mutually exclusive subset of four functional roles: intermediate reasoning, search-or-answer decision, search query generation, and final answer extraction. Evaluating all 2^4=16 role assignments without modifying weights or retraining defines a cooperative game whose Shapley values decompose the total RL gain across roles, while M"obius interaction terms distinguish standalone role improvements from multi-role coupling.
items.author: Ramraj Chandradevan, Sayontan Ghosh, Vinoth Selvendran

items.title: Four consistent estimates of $H_0$ from a $Λ$CDM inference network given CMB data
items.summary: We organize inferences from cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, of the current rate of expansion, $H_0$, into a network whose structure is informed by a scaling symmetry of the Einstein-Boltzmann evolution equations. There are four distinct routes through this network from a calibrating anchor to $H_0$. Given key assumptions of the $Λ$CDM model, they are mutually consistent. This consistency is a significant feature of the $Λ$CDM model's compatibility with CMB data. The redundancy in $H_0$ determinations illuminates a hurdle to resolving the $H_0$ tension with alternative cosmological models.
items.author: Gabriel P. Lynch, Lloyd Knox

items.title: Floquet spectra and parameter sensitivity of entanglement in the quantum kicked top
items.summary: We investigate the relationship between the Floquet spectrum and the sensitivity of the entanglement landscape to parameter and initial condition change in the quantum kicked top. We focus on the case of four qubits and on locating degeneracies in its Floquet eigenphases using the resultant of its characteristic polynomial $p$ and its derivative $\partial_λp$ and quantitatively map the sensitivity of the entanglement landscape to changes in kicking strength over the sphere of spin coherent initial states. We find that prominent sensitivity maxima coincide with either Floquet eigenphase degeneracies or kick strengths exhibiting short-period quantum revivals, with some points satisfying both conditions.
items.author: Dyari Jarvis, Peter A. Rose, Arjendu K. Pattanayak

items.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions
items.summary: Conversational recommenders must rank items against needs that catalogs record only in part, while users add, withdraw and reverse needs and switch between requests. LLM rankers re-read the dialogue at every turn: they are slow, and their ordering does not show which needs an item meets. We show that a conversational recommender can be built from typed decisions instead: named questions over fixed options, answered with option probabilities rather than generated text. On each turn, one typed request maps the message onto the catalog's fields, keeps what no field expresses in the user's words, and decides how the turn changes each earlier need.
items.author: Sungchul Kim, Weixiao Huang, Mekala Raja Sekhar Reddy et al.

items.title: EmboEagle: An Efficient Agentic Embodied Framework for Long-horizon Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Long-horizon robotic manipulation demands reliable execution across interdependent stages, yet standalone World-Action Models (WAMs) suffer from compounding physical errors, while stateless Vision-Language Model (VLM) supervision incurs prohibitive chunkwise latency and lacks 3D spatial persistence. We present EmboEagle, a closed-loop agentic framework that unifies subtask-conditioned WAM control, latent-space adaptive supervision, and memory-guided geometric recovery. First, we adapt sequential WAMs via decoupled two-stage flow matching that preserves cross-stage visual history while calibrating truncated action supervision at subtask boundaries. Second, without an auxiliary vision encoder, we distill teacher intervention decisions into a lightweight routing gate driven solely by the WAM Action Expert's pre- and post-chunk latent transitions and subtask embeddings.
items.author: Fan Xu, Zhongtao Wang, Hao Wu et al.

items.title: New analytic constraints for the soft anomalous dimension bootstrap at three loops
items.summary: The soft anomalous dimension governs the universal long-distance singularities of gauge theory amplitudes. It exhibits a highly constrained analytic structure and has been shown to be amenable to bootstrap methods. In this paper we revisit the relation between unitarity cuts and sequential discontinuities of Feynman integrals and use it to derive new constraints on the soft anomalous dimension. At three loops, we show that certain sequential discontinuities in non-overlapping two-particle channels vanish for every web contributing to the quadrupole function that correlates four coloured partons. These constraints hold for arbitrary parton masses, and we explicitly verify them for the known massless and one-mass cases.
items.author: Einan Gardi, Luke Lippstreu, Andrew J. McLeod et al.

items.title: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
items.summary: Modular exponentiation dominates the logical cost of factoring 2048-bit RSA integers (RSA-2048) with Shor's algorithm. Recent approaches based on approximate residue number systems (RNS) sharply reduce the required logical qubits, yet still demand billions of Toffoli gates. Optimizing these circuits is difficult because shared ancilla qubits and measurement-based uncomputation tightly couple the arithmetic stages, while rare overflows in compressed registers occur too infrequently for random simulation to detect. Here we use large language model (LLM)-driven search to redesign the RNS pipeline across stages and build a deterministic compiler that produces a Pareto frontier of RSA-2048 circuits. We bound rare overflow probabilities analytically and verify the resulting elementary gate sequences across all constituent RNS primes on representative circuits.
items.author: Xiaodi Li, Yuqing Wang, Xue Chen et al.

items.title: Protected Charge Readout Scheme Utilizing Nonlinear Resonators
items.summary: Charge detection of nanoscale quantum devices commonly relies on dissipative sensors, where signal absorption causes measurement backaction. Recently, nonlinear resonators showed a near-unity readout signal through an induced frequency shift. We show that this frequency shift protects the sensor, as it detunes the resonator from the measurement signal. The resonator excitation reduces while an enhanced readout signal is maintained. Our results, supported by numerical modeling, show that nonlinear resonators can combine strong readout contrast with reduced measurement-induced backaction.
items.author: Andrea Cicovic, Harald Havir, Pierre Glidic et al.

items.title: A proposal for an LHC search for baryon number violation in complementarity with trilepton nucleon decay searches
items.summary: We investigate the compatibility of existing limits on trilepton nucleon decay by the Super-Kamiokande (Super-K) experiment with Baryon Number Violation (BNV) at the TeV scale and motivate a dedicated search using existing data at the LHC. Working within an effective field theory framework, we derive model-independent constraints on higher-dimensional operators associated with $B - L/3$ conserving texture of BNV. We demonstrate that existing Super-K limits on loop-level trilepton nucleon decay provide significantly stronger constraints compared to tree-level charm-baryon decays induced by these operators. These constraints translate into bounds of $O(1-30)$ TeV on the BNV scale, leaving open the possibility of an LHC search for $B - L/3$ type BNV.
items.author: Amit Bhoonah, Francis M. Burk, Da Liu et al.

items.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
items.summary: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count.
items.author: Ilumi Chavez, Aditya Ghosh, Chris Kelso et al.

items.title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. To address this challenge, we introduce \textbf{WeaveVLA}, a framework that enhances VLA action generation by explicitly modeling task-relevant relative 3D relations and maintaining relational context across observations. WeaveVLA employs a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network to encode relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references. Pair-specific recurrent edge states integrate geometric evidence across observations to maintain evolving spatial context. A learned-query readout summarizes the updated graph representations into compact relational tokens, which condition the action expert alongside the original vision-language context.
items.author: Zien Wang, Yuhao Pan, Yunfeng Fan et al.

items.title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
items.summary: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five suites spanning world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation. We further develop RUIKit, a unified framework that crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. In simulation, changing only the RUI shifts a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%, and that of a fine-tuned 4B model from 13% to 47%.
items.author: Yanzhe Chen, Zhijun Cao, Zechen Bai et al.

items.title: Electromagnetic Memory as a Collider Observable
items.summary: Electromagnetic memory and charge correlators are measured by different detectors, sensitive to soft radiation and to hard charged tracks. We show that the Ward identity of large gauge symmetry relates these quantities as inclusive observables. For lepton pairs produced by an electromagnetic current, we compute all massless multipoint memory correlators and the massive two-point function, whose coincident limit gives the soft photon number. The correlators admit a celestial free-boson representation and remain finite at first radiative order, where recoil generates back-to-back Sudakov logarithms.
items.author: Felipe Diaz, Hernán A. González, Oriana Labrin et al.

items.title: Near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--Krylov response in noncommutative-inspired BTZ spacetime
items.summary: We compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a Lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired BTZ black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--Krylov complexity. In the BTZ limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{K}_0 = X(\coshτ- 1)$. With smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $F'_α(X)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $F'_α(x_+)/2$. The two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled BTZ curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. For a distant release point the early response approaches BTZ, whereas the late-time rate does not.
items.author: F. A. Brito, F. G. Costa, J. A. V. Campos

items.title: NoveltyGate: Novelty, Not Error, Decides Which VLA Prefix Tokens to Compute Exactly
items.summary: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ re-encode the camera images and the instruction with a 2B-parameter backbone at every control step, and the feed-forward layers of this prefix account for most of its compute. A natural way to save this compute is to send most tokens through a low-rank MLP and compute exactly only the tokens whose approximation error is large. We find that this intuition is wrong. Even a verifier that knows every token's exact error picks the wrong tokens, producing 1.3--1.7$\times$ larger action deviation than a simple test of whether a token's input is novel, that is, whether it falls outside the subspace seen during calibration.
items.author: Lemeng Qi

items.title: Localized Strain Tuning of Second-Harmonic Generation in MoS2 Monolayers and Bilayers
items.summary: We investigate the modulation of second-harmonic generation (SHG) in CVD-grown MoS2 monolayers and few-layer flakes through localized mechanical deformation applied by an atomic force microscope (AFM) tip. MoS2 membranes suspended over microstructured Si3N4 substrates allow simultaneous measurements of force and SHG intensity during controlled approach and retraction cycles. Suspended regions exhibit enhanced SHG relative to substrate-supported regions, with pronounced suppression near the clamping boundaries. While the SHG response during compressive loading varies among individual membranes, adhesion-mediated pulling during retraction consistently reduces the SHG intensity until tip detachment, when the signal recovers. By correlating the optical modulation with the measured pull-off force and a phenomenological estimate of effective strain, we obtain a characteristic sensitivity of approximately 12% SHG modulation per 1% effective strain, with comparable behavior in monolayers and bilayers.
items.author: Martín Aversa, Florencia Cammarata, Camila Borrazás et al.

items.title: Kaon-pair production with NNLO effects
items.summary: The Monte Carlo framework McMule has been extended to support the processes $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ and $e^+\,e^-\to K^0\,\bar{K}^0$. Our results include NNLO initial-state QED corrections together with NLO mixed corrections. The latter are evaluated in the FsQED approach, using disperon QED. The implementation is fully differential and can be used with any kaon form factor. We present the total cross section for energies relevant to the CMD-3 experiment and observe very large corrections. For $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ we also present selected differential observables for energies around the $φ(1020)$ resonance.
items.author: Yizhou Fang, Sophie Kollatzsch, Adrian Signer

items.title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
items.summary: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant.
items.author: Marten Reehorst

items.title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
items.summary: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations.
items.author: Randall H. V. Pradinett, Theo F. Motta, Gastão Krein

items.title: Terahertz detection of magnon chirality in polycrystalline CsCuCl$_3$
items.summary: In antiferromagnets, the handedness of magnon precession is usually measured on single crystals. In a pressed pellet of the chiral helimagnet CsCuCl$_3$, whose grains carry both structural handednesses and all orientations, we found that, from 5 to 7 T, the sub-terahertz magnon absorbs one circular polarization more than 20 times as strongly as the other, which rules out precession about each grain's own axis. Spin-wave theory attributes this to the Zeeman frequency, here two to four times the exchange-enhanced gap, which locks the precession axis to the field in every grain. Magnon chirality in antiferromagnets is thus accessible without a single crystal.
items.author: Juan S. Rodríguez-Hernández, Gabriel F. Freitas, Nicolas M. Kawahala et al.

items.title: Interface-Engineered Piezoelectricity and Electromechanical Coupling in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructures
items.summary: Interfaces between dissimilar two-dimensional (2D) materials provide a route to engineer electromechanical responses that are not intrinsic to the individual constituent layers. Here, we use high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate 461 van der Waals heterostructures constructed from 57 2D monolayers and establish a materials-design framework linking work-function mismatch, interfacial charge redistribution, dipole formation, and strain-dependent electromechanical response. We find that heterostructure formation generates out-of-plane interfacial dipoles via charge redistribution between the constituent layers, while biaxial in-plane strain systematically modulates them. The resulting heterostructures exhibit two distinct regimes: metallic interfaces with strain-tunable interfacial dipoles and semiconducting heterostructures with well-defined piezoelectric responses.
items.author: Shivanand Yadav, Raihan Ahammed, Umer Ali et al.

items.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
items.summary: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials.
items.author: Alexey Tal, Fabien Tran, Wei Chen et al.

items.title: ProTechnology Innovation Showcase: From the surface of the sun to the depths of the ocean" – Use Cases in the Display and Communication of Complex NOAA Scientific Data
items.summary: ProTechnology Innovation Showcase: From the surface of the sun to the depths of the ocean" – Use Cases in the Display and Communication of Complex NOAA Scientific Data November 23, 2026 A very successful ProTechnology Innovation Showcase was held on November 18, 2026, featuring “Use Cases in the Display and Communication of Complex NOAA Scientific Data”. We had over 200 attendees and featured presentations from six different ProTech Prime vendors and their teams. Please find a copy of their presentations here offsite link . We plan to hold future ProTechnology Innovation Showcases regularly, covering a variety of topics. For the latest updates, please visit our news and events page: news and events page .
items.author: sabrina.wallace

items.title: Molecular Pawns on a Surface Chessboard: Computational Investigation of Nanographenes with Atomistic Methods
items.summary: Atomically precise nanographenes combine tunable electronic topology with localized, coherent spin states, making them candidate platforms for molecular quantum technologies. This review examines the multiscale theoretical framework governing these systems: the hierarchy of computational methods for describing magnetic properties, the substrate-molecule interface, on-surface synthetic kinetics, and supramolecular self-assembly. We highlight how density functional theory, automated reaction-path discovery, and spin-aware machine-learned interatomic potentials connect static electronic structure to mesoscale dynamics, and how magnetic exchange, optical excitations, and spin transport can be predicted before synthesis.
items.author: Antonio Lorenzo Mariano, Jacopo Lupi, Emilio Lorini et al.

items.title: Optimal fidelity over zero-capacity erasure channels
items.summary: Antidegradable quantum channels have zero capacity for reliable quantum communication. However, they can nevertheless transmit quantum information with nontrivial fidelity. This raises the question: how well can quantum information be preserved through such channels? In this work, we exactly characterize the optimal asymptotic entanglement fidelity of quantum erasure channels throughout the antidegradable regime. Specifically, we show that it equals $γ+\frac{1-γ}{d}$ for transmission probabilities $0<γ\le \frac{1}{2}$ and logical dimension $d$. We use fractional extendibility to establish an upper bound on the entanglement fidelity achievable by arbitrary error-correcting protocols. Furthermore, we construct a family of permutation-invariant codes that asymptotically saturates this bound.
items.author: Camilo Castro-Landolt, Rabsan Galib Ahmed, Graeme Smith

items.title: Coherent Recovery of Nested Codes over the Quantum Erasure Channel Using Erasure Decoding and Quantization
items.summary: Motivated by quantum capacity results, we revisit nested binary linear codes for the quantum erasure channel through a packing-covering viewpoint: the outer code supports erasure reconstruction, while the inner code performs erasure quantization. We turn this perspective into two explicit decoder architectures. Architecture I requires no stabilizer-syndrome measurements and combines a classical peeling decoder and erasure quantizer with corresponding coherent quantum reconstruction and cleanup operations that disentangle the logical state from inaccessible erasure-environment branches. Architecture II goes one step further and implements erasure belief propagation directly through reversible ternary quantum gates, providing quantum state healing that reconstructs erased symbols while leaving unerased code states unperturbed.
items.author: Aditya Guhagarkar, S. Sandeep Pradhan, Achilleas Anastasopoulos

items.title: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
items.summary: While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time.
items.author: Zhenyu Du, Xiongfeng Ma, Vlatko Vedral et al.

items.title: Altermagnetism of MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 in a wurtzite-based crystal structure
items.summary: Based on symmetry analysis, the Pna2_1 wurtzite-based crystal structure with Mn as a magnetic group-II element, MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 belong to the class of altermagnets because spin-up and spin-down Mn in the unit cell are related by rotation or mirror plane type operations rather than inversion or translation. Spin polarized density functional theory calculations and quasiparticle self-consistent (QS) GW calculations support the symmetry analysis and identify the lowest-energy spin configuration as Pna'2_1' in agreement with neutron diffraction data. The altermagnetic band splittings allowed for the three different antiferromagnetic ordering patterns are reported and symmetry analyzed. Additionally, spin wave dispersions, chiral magnon spltting, and Neel temperature estimates from the mean-field and random-phase approximations are provided, as well as calculations of the optical dielectric function using the Bethe-Salpeter Equation method.
items.author: Ilteris K. Turan, Jonathan Agrinya, Walter R. L. Lambrecht

items.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
items.summary: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$.
items.author: V. K. Oikonomou

items.title: M 4.7 - South Sandwich Islands region
items.summary: A magnitude 4.7 earthquake was recorded South Sandwich Islands region. The event happened on 23 November 2026 at 15:10 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 103 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Programmable Broadband Polarization-Preserving Optical Delay Line with Faraday Mirrors
items.summary: We report a broadband optical delay line programmable for delays up to 1 μs with nanosecond resolution, while preserving an arbitrary and unknown polarization state of the original light. The delay line comprises bidirectional pass in cascaded segments of standard single-mode fibers, along with terminal reflection from Faraday mirrors (FMs) at both ends. Each segment contains either a short path or a long path, selected by an optical switch. The FMs auto-compensate for random polarization fluctuations introduced by the optical fibers, thereby restoring the initial polarization state. Broadband operation of the delay line was assessed by investigating dispersion of both the fiber and the FMs.
items.author: Salem F. Hegazy, Salah S. A. Obayya, Bahaa E. A. Saleh

items.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
items.summary: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.
