items.author: Hanieh Najafzadeh, Radmehr Jafari, Abdollah Langari

items.title: Gallium at germanium surfaces: links to superconducting films and correlated adatom lattices
items.summary: Epitaxial films grown on Ge(001) show that germanium hyperdoped with substitutional Ga is superconducting. In earlier implanted films, Ga-rich precipitates obscured the origin of the superconductivity. This review examines the sites Ga occupies on Ge(001) and Ge(111) and how it enters the growing film. The Ga fraction expected from the growth fluxes is 17.9\%, yet the distribution of Ga among lattice sites is unknown. Comparisons include Ga on Si(001) and Si(111),In, Sn, Pb, Sb and P on Ge(001), and elemental and two-dimensional Ga. Where its surface coordination has been established, Ga has three bonds, whereas substitutional Ga in the films is fourfold coordinated and acts as an acceptor.
items.author: Peter Jacobson

items.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
items.summary: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches. For example, we show that it can further delay the production of tripartite entanglement. We build the quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap, and prove that it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement for crystal quenches.
items.author: Paul Gaudin, Clément Berthière

items.title: Pulse-to-pulse Power Fluctuations in Ultra-Fast Fiber Amplifiers with Gain-Managed Nonlinearity
items.summary: We present a theoretical framework for predicting pulse-to-pulse power fluctuations caused by pump and seed power noise and by amplified spontaneous emission in ultrafast fiber amplifiers operating in the gain-managed nonlinear regime. The numerical model evaluates statistically averaged quantities directly, without Monte Carlo simulations with stochastic sources, and reduces to a semi-analytical monochromatic model in the limit of vanishing signal bandwidth and negligible ASE. We show that nonlinear spectral broadening of the signal and of its perturbations, combined with the frequency-dependent gain, significantly alters the technical relative intensity noise in both the high-power, high-repetition-rate and the low-power, low-repetition-rate regimes, and that in the latter regime the contributions related to amplified spontaneous emission become comparable to those induced by pump and seed fluctuations.
items.author: Maksim Kozlov, Colin J. McKinstrie, Nitzan Haviv et al.

items.title: Quantum resources constrain function approximation
items.summary: Universal function approximation is central to machine learning. Quantum learning models are universal as well, but this does not specify the resources needed to approximate a given function. We study how coherence, imaginarity, entanglement and magic constrain function approximation for a fixed encoding and readout, using the cumulative resource power of the trainable gates. In a one-qubit model with phase encoding, coherence bounds the oscillation of the model function, while imaginarity bounds its odd part. In a two-qubit model, entanglement bounds the distance from product functions. These bounds hold at any encoding depth. For magic, the phase encoding itself supplies non-Clifford operations.
items.author: Oxana Shaya, Lirandë Pira

items.title: Janus Asymmetry Unlocks Rashba Spintronics and Chiral Phononics in Two-Dimensional Carbo-Chalcogenides
items.summary: Spintronics and chiral phononics offer complementary routes for nanoscale control, yet realizing both functionalities within a common two-dimensional platform remains challenging. Here, using extensive first-principles calculations, we show that Janus asymmetry simultaneously drives both effects in transition-metal carbo-chalcogenides (JTMCCs) along two chemically distinct routes, through either chalcogen or transition-metal substitution. Remarkably, both Janus routes yield giant Rashba responses, with $α_\mathrm{R}\approx2$ eV Å in Ta$_2$CSSe and NbTaCS$_2$, exceeding those reported for Mo/W-based Janus transition-metal dichalcogenides. Furthermore, Janus asymmetry lifts the degeneracy of opposite-chirality phonons, producing splittings as large as $\approx28$ cm$^{-1}$. More strikingly, asymmetry generates chiral carbon vibrations that were achiral in the centrosymmetric parent compounds, with splittings reaching $\approx8$ cm$^{-1}$.
items.author: Valentina Barreca, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Giovanni Cantele et al.

items.title: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots
items.summary: We investigate electronic transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer with two quantum dots in the presence of finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. With the help of a diagrammatic technique, we derive, within linear perturbation theory in the tunnelling-coupling strength, analytic expressions for the occupations, current, and interferometric visibility in terms of a coherence measure that involves the sum of four off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix. The latter are calculated numerically from a master equation for arbitrary settings of the system parameters. For some symmetric setups, we obtain closed-form expressions for the linear conductance. We systematically analyse the impact of a finite Coulomb interaction on the interferometric visibility, and reveal a rapid suppression of destructive interference upon breaking of system symmetries.
items.author: Oliver Oing, Alexander Hahn, Jürgen König et al.

items.title: Statistical analysis of residue contact energies reveals folding determinants of ion channels
items.summary: Tetrameric and pseudo-tetrameric cationic channels, which are targeted by many drugs and toxins, play key roles in the cell physiology and pathophysiology. This diverse superfamily of P-loop channels includes but is not limited to voltage-gated potassium, sodium and calcium channels, TRP channels, and ionotropic glutamate receptors.
items.author: Svetlana I. Tarnovskaya, Boris S. Zhorov, Denis B. Tikhonov

items.title: Large-scale analysis of AlphaFold structures reveals organism-specific physicochemical signatures
items.summary: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures.
items.author: Michael J. Stam, Diego A. Oyarzún, Nadanai Laohakunakorn et al.

items.title: High-multiplexity imaging reveals distinct modes of translating time into space during embryonic patterning
items.summary: Classical models of embryonic patterning explain how cells acquire positional identities by responding to different concentration thresholds along morphogen gradients. Yet many developmental systems generate spatial patterns through temporal programs of gene expression, raising the question of how these programs translate into spatial organization.
items.author: Jimena Garcia-Guillen, Mahla Ahmadi, Theophilus Frimpong et al.

items.title: Translation of a four-codon ORF in the 3′UTR of MAP3K10 regulates its expression
items.summary: Several eukaryotic mRNAs are polycistronic because of translatable open reading frames (ORFs) embedded in different regions, including untranslated regions (UTRs), in addition to the primary ORF (i.e., the coding sequence). While 5′UTR upstream ORFs (uORFs) are mechanistically and functionally well studied, 3′UTR downstream ORFs (dORFs) remain poorly understood.
items.author: Kirtana Vasu, Swati Ghosh, Sarthak Sahoo et al.

items.title: Fungal secreted leucine-rich repeat proteins suppress plant immunity to enhance colonisation
items.summary: Plant pathogens secrete proteins (effectors) to alter the molecular environment of their host, manipulating general physiology and defence processes to enhance virulence. Here we describe a previously uncharacterised group of plant-like, secreted, leucine-rich repeat (sLRR) proteins produced by fungal pathogens, which contribute to this process.
items.author: Haider Ali, Elisha Thynne, Toby Ellis et al.

items.title: Trichinella spiralis infection in pregnant mice alleviates TNBS-induced colitis in their offspring by reshaping the gut microbiota–metabolite axis
items.summary: Epidemiological surveys have shown that in regions with a high prevalence of Trichinella spiralis ( T. spiralis ) infection, the risk of neonates developing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is reduced. The hygiene hypothesis links the incidence of IBD to helminth infections.
items.author: Xuanrui Liu, Tongxuan Zhang, Yuxin Wang et al.

items.title: Noncanonical P gene mRNA editing in Cedar virus generates a U protein that is required for efficient virion production
items.summary: Highly pathogenic Hendra and Nipah viruses encode accessory P gene products (C, V and W) that antagonize innate immunity and contribute to pathogenicity. Cedar virus (CedV), an apathogenic bat-borne henipavirus, is presumed to lack P gene mRNA editing and therefore is unable to express V and W proteins.
items.author: Henriette Schwotzer, Patricia Schupp, Richard Küchler et al.

items.title: When should adaptation arise from a polygenic response versus few large-effect changes?
items.summary: by William R. Milligan, Laura K. Hayward, Guy Sella When will adaptation involve a few genetic changes of large effect versus a polygenic response? There are compelling reasons to expect polygenic adaptation to be common, yet direct evidence is lacking. Conversely, there are hundreds of examples of large-effect adaptations across species, but it is unclear whether they occur frequently within any given species. These different lines of evidence are hard to synthesize, in part due to the lack of theory that relates them. To address this gap, we frame the question in terms of the properties of an adaptive trait.
items.author: William R. Milligan, Laura K. Hayward, Guy Sella

items.title: Multi-model forecasting of respiratory disease activity in Germany during the 2024–2025 season
items.summary: by Johannes Bracher, Daniel Wolffram, Rodrigo Amaral Lind, Nils Bardeck, Micha Böhm, Seba Contreras, Philipp Dönges, Felix Günther, Rolf Kaiser, Jan van de Kassteele, Alexander Kuhlmann, Berit Lange, Barbora Němcová, Viola Priesemann, Ulrich Reinacher, Isti Rodiah, Frank Sandmann, the RESPINOW Study Group , Melanie Schienle Respiratory diseases cause considerable morbidity in autumn and winter and are a priority in public health monitoring. In Germany, they are subject to a number of surveillance systems, including both pathogen-specific and syndromic indicators. In this paper we present a collaborative multi-target and multi-model real-time forecasting system rolled out during the 2024/25 season, and discuss differences to earlier efforts carried out during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.author: Johannes Bracher, Daniel Wolffram, Rodrigo Amaral Lind et al.

items.title: AlphaFold models of host-pathogen interactions elucidate the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry
items.summary: by Delora Baptista, Lidia Gomez-Lucas, Jürgen Jänes, Nevan J. Krogan, Maria João Amorim, Ylva Ivarsson, Pedro Beltrao Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall low performance.
items.author: Delora Baptista, Lidia Gomez-Lucas, Jürgen Jänes et al.

items.title: Cognate antigen recognition induces HIV-1 outgrowth from proviruses in repressive chromatin contexts
items.summary: by Angelica Camilo-Contreras, Filippo Dragoni, Hao Zhang, Junlin Zhuo, Daniel Smith, Arturo Casadevall, Jun Lai, Pablo Tebas, Janet D. Siliciano, Robert F. Siliciano, Stuart Ray, Luis J. Montaner, Joel N. Blankson, Francesco Roberto Simonetti During long-term antiretroviral therapy (ART) and in elite controllers, intact HIV-1 proviruses become enriched in genomic regions associated with transcriptional repression, raising questions about whether they can be reactivated in vivo. We developed an antigen-specific quantitative viral outgrowth assay to test whether cognate antigen stimulation can induce replication-competent virus from such proviruses. We studied cells from two people with HIV: one receiving long-term ART and one elite controller.
items.author: Angelica Camilo-Contreras, Filippo Dragoni, Hao Zhang et al.

items.title: The Chlamydia trachomatis secreted effector CebN targets nucleoporins and Rae1 to antagonize STAT1 nuclear localization
items.summary: by Brianna P. Steiert, Paige N. McCaslin, Cherilyn A. Elwell, Julia Kevil-Yeager, Parker Smith, Xavier Tijerina, Madison A. Elliott, Steven Huang, Yennifer Delgado, Jocelyn Ni, Robert Faris, Shelby E. Andersen, Quinn Eldridge, Brian S. Imai, Justine V. Arrington, Peter M. Yau, Kathleen M. Mirrashidi, Jeffrey R. Johnson, Erik Verschueren, John Von Dollen, Gwendolyn M. Jang, Nevan J. Krogan, Mehdi Bouhaddou, Christine Suetterlin, Joanne N. Engel, Mary M. Weber To usurp host defenses and establish a replicative niche, obligate intracellular pathogens are tasked with remodeling the host cell using a discrete repertoire of effector proteins. For Chlamydia trachomatis ( C.t. ), the identification of secreted proteins and their host targets, as well as the elucidation of their functions, has been particularly challenging given the inherent obstacles in applying genetics to an obligate intravacuolar pathogen.
items.author: Brianna P. Steiert, Paige N. McCaslin, Cherilyn A. Elwell et al.

items.title: DDX58 modulates epithelial cell survival and mumps virus persistence after infection
items.summary: by Xinyu Zhu, Nicholas S. Heaton Paramyxoviruses, including mumps virus (MuV), primarily cause acute infections, but the duration of viral replication and associated diseases can vary. A molecular understanding of the basis for differential viral clearance timelines, however, remains incompletely understood. Using a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in human lung epithelial A549 cells, we identified DDX58, a cytosolic viral RNA sensor, as a key regulator of MuV-induced cell death. DDX58 deficiency limited cell death independently of interferon (IFN) signaling and allowed the establishment of apparently persistent MuV infection in cells. This long-term infection in DDX58 deficient cells was characterized by low rates of viral replication and small viral replication factories.
items.author: Xinyu Zhu, Nicholas S. Heaton

items.title: Estimation of annual exposures and antibody kinetics against norovirus GII.4 variants from English serology data, 2007–2012
items.summary: by Kathleen M. O’Reilly, James A. Hay, Lisa C. Lindesmith, David Allen, Stephane Hue, Kari Debbink, Adam Kucharski, Ralph S. Baric, Judy Breuer, W. John Edmunds Norovirus in humans is highly contagious, causing diarrhoea and vomiting, and is especially common in young children. Winter incidence varies annually, and previous research indicates that the change of dominant norovirus variant is followed by high incidence, but having a clear mechanism to explain this observation could support better prediction of epidemics. Here we analyse unique norovirus GII.4 serology blockade data from 656 children in England collected via opportunistic sampling between 2007–2012 using a mathematical model of multi-variant antibody kinetics to infer metrics such as annual attack rates and age-specific infection rates.
items.author: Kathleen M. O’Reilly, James A. Hay, Lisa C. Lindesmith et al.

items.title: Toxin-triggered activation of regulated exocytosis enhances bacterial egress from the intestinal layer
items.summary: by Christopher Margraf, Lilo Greune, Paweena Wessel, Samriti Sharma, Sandra Heissler, Christian Rüter, Petra Dersch Bacterial exit from host cells is essential for dissemination yet remains poorly understood. Here, we define a non-lytic egress pathway exploited by the enteric pathogen Yersinia pseudotuberculosis that co-opts the host exocytosis machinery in intestinal epithelial cells. The bacteria secrete a CNF-family toxin that activates the Cdc42-PLCγ1-IP 3 -IP 3 R signaling cascade, triggering SNARE-dependent fusion of the Yersinia -containing vacuoles with the cell membrane via VAMP7, Stx4, and SNAP23. This controlled exocytic release preserves epithelial barrier integrity and occurs infrequently, representing a key rate-limiting step in systemic spread.
items.author: Christopher Margraf, Lilo Greune, Paweena Wessel et al.

items.title: Enhancing multi-level reading comprehension through Content-Based Language Teaching: A quasi-experimental study
items.summary: by Yohannes Joressa Wordofa, Bedilu Teka Geleto This study examined the effects of Content-Based Language Teaching (CBLT) on EFL students’ multi-level reading comprehension, focusing on literal, inferential, and critical dimensions. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 60 first-year university students at Mattu University, Ethiopia, divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group received over an eight-week CBLT intervention using content-based thematic reading materials, while the control group was taught through conventional reading instruction. Data were collected using researcher-developed parallel reading comprehension tests and analyzed using MANOVA, MANCOVA, ANCOVA, and paired-samples t-tests. Results indicated no statistically significant differences between the groups at pretest, confirming baseline equivalence.
items.author: Yohannes Joressa Wordofa, Bedilu Teka Geleto

items.title: The state of genetic literacy among high school students in Czechia
items.summary: by Marek Procházka, Markéta Klimešová, Vanda Janštová To investigate high school students’ understanding of modern genetics and to characterize the obstacles that impede deeper understanding of this subject, we translated the Learning Progression‑Based Assessment of Modern Genetics diagnostic instrument into Czech and validated it with 282 Czech high school students. We present the Czech version of this instrument which spans Mendelian genetics; molecular biology (proteins, nucleic acids, gene expression); mutation; cell division; genetics–evolution connections; environmental influences on phenotype; intra‑individual and inter‑individual genetic variation; and interspecific differences. Czech high school students frequently fail to connect proteins to phenotypic traits, rarely attain molecular‑level reasoning, and underappreciate the evolutionary significance of genetic mechanisms.
items.author: Marek Procházka, Markéta Klimešová, Vanda Janštová

items.title: Associations of physical exercise and sedentary behavior with problematic smartphone use and interaction anxiety in a predominantly first-year convenience sample of Chinese college students: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Qi Han Problematic smartphone use and interaction anxiety are common concerns in university settings, but their joint relationships with exercise and sedentary behavior remain unclear. We examined these associations in a predominantly first-year convenience sample recruited through 36 universities in four Chinese provinces. The analytical sample included 1,025 students aged 18 years or older, of whom 902 (88.0%) were first-year students. Physical exercise was represented by an adapted self-reported exercise-volume index derived from exercise intensity, duration, and frequency. Sedentary behavior was assessed with a single item whose response categories used inconsistent daily and weekly time frames; it was therefore analyzed as an exploratory categorical indicator.
items.author: Qi Han

items.title: Ten-year clinical outcomes after successful percutaneous coronary intervention compared with medical treatment in patients with chronic total occlusion and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction
items.summary: by Hye Yon Yu, Jihun Ahn, Seung-Woon Rha, Byoung Geol Choi, Se Yeon Choi, Jae Kyeong Byun, Youjin Lee, Abiseka Panji Baskoro, Aditya Reza Pratama, Melly Susanti, Manda Satria Chesario, Soohyung Park, Cheol Ung Choi Background The long-term clinical benefit of revascularization in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≥50%) remains uncertain. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the clinical impact of CTO revascularization in patients with preserved LVEF compared with those receiving optimal medical treatment (OMT) up to 10 years. Methods A total of 939 patients with CTO and preserved LVEF were analyzed, including those treated with OMT (OMT group; n = 492) or successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI group; n = 447).
items.author: Hye Yon Yu, Jihun Ahn, Seung-Woon Rha et al.

items.title: Effects of long-term exposure to four widely used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice
items.summary: by Mingming Pan, Yanhua Shen, Zhihao Wu, Guiping Wang, Jing Wang, Zhengyu Zhou Gut microbiota plays a vital role in regulating host physiological status and is susceptible to environmental factors, including different drinking water regimens. This study aimed to explore the effects of long-term exposure to four commonly used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice. A total of 32 male mice were randomly divided into four groups and continuously administered reverse osmosis water (ROW), hydrochloric acid-acidified water (HCl-AW), sulfuric acid-acidified water (H 2 SO 4 -AW), and chlorinated water (CW) for 12 weeks, respectively.
items.author: Mingming Pan, Yanhua Shen, Zhihao Wu et al.

items.title: Effects of virtual reality-based rehabilitation on upper-limb motor function and functional independence after subacute stroke: A systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
items.summary: by Joaquín Pérez-Cárcamo, Edgar Vásquez-Carrasco, Pablo Valdés-Badilla, Cristian Sandoval-Vásquez, Cristian Núñez-Espinosa, Jordan Hernandez-Martínez Background Virtual reality (VR)-based rehabilitation has emerged as a promising approach to enhance recovery after stroke; however, its effectiveness during the subacute phase remains unclear. This systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis evaluated the effects of VR-based rehabilitation on upper-limb motor function, manual dexterity, and functional independence in individuals with subacute stroke. Methods PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL Complete, and Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection were searched through May 2026. Randomized controlled trials involving adults with subacute stroke receiving immersive or non-immersive VR-based rehabilitation were included. Comparators consisted of active or inactive control interventions.
items.author: Joaquín Pérez-Cárcamo, Edgar Vásquez-Carrasco, Pablo Valdés-Badilla et al.

items.title: Environmental enrichment enhances hepatic oxidative stress and antioxidant defenses without modulating immunometabolic gene expression in adult male mice
items.summary: by Matheus Santos de Sousa Fernandes, Tiago Lacerda Ramos, Débora Eduarda da Silva Fidélis, Fatma Hilal Yagin, Allifer Rosendo Pereira, Thyago Oliveira Rodrigues, Claudia Jacques Lagranha, Mariana Pinheiro Fernandes, Lúcia Helena de Oliveira Cordeiro, Abedelmalek Kalefh Tabnjh, Sameer Badri Al-Mhanna, Fabrício Oliveira Souto Background Environmental enrichment (EE) is a non-pharmacological intervention based on modifications of the housing environment that increase sensory, cognitive, and motor stimulation, and it has been proposed to modulate immunometabolic responses. Aim To investigate the effects of EE on hepatic redox status, oxidative balance, and immunometabolic gene expression in healthy mice. Methodology Male C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned at 45 days of age to a standard environment (SE; n = 7) or an enriched environment (EE; n = 7) for six weeks.
items.author: Matheus Santos de Sousa Fernandes, Tiago Lacerda Ramos, Débora Eduarda da Silva Fidélis et al.

items.title: A standardized XRCT protocol for quantitative 3D shape preferred orientation analysis in rocks
items.summary: by Puqing Li, Vasileios Chatzaras, Matthew Foley, Sinan Özaydın, Patrice Rey Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) mineral shape-preferred orientation (SPO) is important for interpreting deformation, magma flow, sediment transport, and anisotropic rock properties. X-ray computed tomography (XRCT) enables non-destructive measurement of mineral SPO in three dimensions, but few openly documented workflows link data acquisition, image processing, object extraction, and fabric quantification. This Lab Protocol presents an end-to-end XRCT workflow covering data acquisition, volume reconstruction, phase segmentation, grain-parameter extraction, fabric quantification, and projection of the calculated fabric onto the physical sample for oriented sectioning. An expert-calibrated machine-learning procedure returns reproducible, sample-specific loose and strict candidate minimum grain-volume thresholds (Vmin) for review before an operating threshold is adopted.
items.author: Puqing Li, Vasileios Chatzaras, Matthew Foley et al.

items.title: Trends in low back pain burden attributable to high BMI and occupational ergonomic factors among women in four selected Asia–Pacific Subregions, 1990–2023
items.summary: by Xiang Xiao, Yuxue Xiao, Ruizhe Li, Zebiao Zheng, Yipu Xiao, Hang Ren Background Low back pain (LBP) is a major cause of disability worldwide. We investigated the burden of female LBP attributable to high body mass index (BMI) and occupational ergonomic factors across four Asia–Pacific subregions. Methods Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data, we assessed disability–adjusted life years (DALYs) and DALY rates in East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Oceania from 1990 to 2023. Joinpoint regression, socioeconomic inequality, decomposition, and frontier analyses were performed, and Bayesian age–period–cohort models projected burden through 2040. Results High–BMI–attributable LBP burden increased across all four subregions, with South Asia showing the most pronounced increase.
items.author: Xiang Xiao, Yuxue Xiao, Ruizhe Li et al.

items.title: Terminal shoot maturity orchestrates Carbon–Nitrogen balance and hormonal signaling to regulate floral induction in litchi ( Litchi chinensis Sonn.)
items.summary: by Qiusheng Xiao, Yuqing Niu, Xingjie Li, Fayong Li Floral induction in litchi ( Litchi chinensis Sonn.) is triggered by chilling but strictly contingent upon terminal shoot maturity; however, the regulatory mechanism linking shoot status to floral fate remains elusive. This study investigated the physiological and molecular determinants of flowering in ‘Feizixiao’ litchi shoots of varying maturity under natural winter chilling. We found that shoot maturity is a prerequisite for flowering competency. Mature shoots accumulated significantly higher carbohydrate reserves (soluble sugars and starch), resulting in a high carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio compared to immature shoots. Hormonal profiling revealed that maturation remodeled the hormonal landscape by upregulating abscisic acid (ABA) and suppressing gibberellin A 3 (GA 3 ).
items.author: Qiusheng Xiao, Yuqing Niu, Xingjie Li et al.

items.title: Healing and secondary displacement after palmar open-wedge osteotomy for distal radial malunion without bone graft
items.summary: by Robin Benjamin Kim Hansson, Miled Dhaouadi, Therese Collin, Emir Ouahrani, Hans Erik Berg, Yan Li This retrospective cohort study assessed whether the presence or absence of cortical contact influenced healing and secondary displacement after palmar open-wedge osteotomy without bone grafting in extra-articular distal radial malunion. Seventy-nine patients treated at a single tertiary center between 1999 and 2024 were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the presence or absence of cortical contact on intraoperative fluoroscopic images. Secondary displacement and bone healing were the primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes included group analysis of cortical contact, complications and re-operations. The median radiographic follow-up duration was 28 weeks (IQR 14–60).
items.author: Robin Benjamin Kim Hansson, Miled Dhaouadi, Therese Collin et al.

items.title: Biological age acceleration and urinary incontinence: A combined analysis from two national cohorts in the United States and China
items.summary: by Ping Kong, Zhangxiang Chen, Zhiqi Liu, Haibing Wang, Zhiqiang Zhang Background To explore the relationship between the GOLD biological age difference (GOLD BioAgeDiff)—a quantitative measure of aging—and urinary incontinence using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Materials and methods In NHANES, weighted multinomial logistic regression assessed UI subtypes, ordinal logistic regression assessed severity; additional analyses included propensity score matching (PSM), restricted cubic splines (RCSs), subgroup analyses, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). In CHARLS, Cox models and Kaplan-Meier curves evaluated incident UI. Results GOLD BioAgeDiff was associated with urge (OR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01–1.04) and mixed UI (OR 1.02, 95% CI: 1.00–1.03), but not stress UI.
items.author: Ping Kong, Zhangxiang Chen, Zhiqi Liu et al.

items.title: Electronic trap monitoring systems reduce operator response time during live trapping for harvest in Germany
items.summary: by Franziska Sommer, Kathrin Büttner, Johannes Lang, Michael Lierz Live trapping of mammals is practiced worldwide for purposes including pest control, wildlife harvest, species conservation, and research, with increasing emphasis on animal welfare. Electronic trap monitoring systems (ETMS) aim to reduce confinement time of captured animals by enabling faster trap checks. We conducted a field study to evaluate whether commercially available ETMS reduce operator response time and work reliably under practical trapping conditions. Between 2022 and 2024, volunteer trappers from Germany tested 91 devices from 4 commercial ETMS. During the first phase, trappers could not access the ETMS notifications (simulating non-electronically monitored traps), whereas in the second phase they received notifications.
items.author: Franziska Sommer, Kathrin Büttner, Johannes Lang et al.

items.title: Evidence of the implementation of a professional practice model and absenteeism and engagement indicators among the nursing team: A scoping review protocol
items.summary: by Wania Regina Mollo Baia, Isabela Gomes Musa dos Santos, Ricardo Toshio Yamassake, Vivian Aline Mininel, Renata Santos Tito, Patricia Campos Pavan Baptista Objective To map the evidence regarding the relationship between management and professional practice models and absenteeism and engagement indicators among nursing teams in healthcare services. Introduction The nursing workforce is the largest global workforce in healthcare; however, unequal distribution, high turnover, and absenteeism exist, directly impacting quality of care and patient safety. Professional practice models grounded in shared governance and participatory leadership have emerged as promising strategies to promote engagement and retention of these professionals. Nevertheless, the absence of systematic mapping as to how these models influence absenteeism and engagement justifies the development of this scoping review.
items.author: Wania Regina Mollo Baia, Isabela Gomes Musa dos Santos, Ricardo Toshio Yamassake et al.

items.title: Magnetic control of waveguide modes with an anisotropic all-dielectric spacer
items.summary: by Illia Fedorin We study how magnetic bias and passive dielectric anisotropy control the mode spectrum of a parallel-plate waveguide with a ferrite–semiconductor effective core. A subwavelength dielectric laminate supplies distinct normal and tangential spacer permittivities. The core follows a published diagonal Bloch model, and regular characteristic determinants enforce the perfect electric conductor and material-interface conditions for transverse-magnetic (TM) and transverse-electric (TE) fields. A matched scalar spacer isolates the normal-permittivity contribution: TE spectra coincide, while the TM propagation constant changes. At a plate separation of 0.4 mm, angular frequency 10 11 rad/s, core fill fraction f = 0.5, compositions δ = ρ = 0.5, and bias 2500 Oe, the normalized TM constants are 3.563 and 7.944 for the laminate and scalar control.
items.author: Illia Fedorin

items.title: Safety collaborative prevention and control technology for coal mining beneath oil pipelines
items.summary: by Tuanjie Liu, Gui Liu, Xiangnan Li, Aiguo Guo, Yaokun Fu, Haoyu Hu Coal mining beneath oil pipelines requires a balance between resource recovery and the control of mining-induced pipeline deformation. Using coal seam at Haichatan Coal Mine and the Jingbian-Yulin refined-oil pipeline as a case study, a coupled analysis framework was developed to link ground movement, relative pipe-soil displacement, and pipeline equivalent stress. The probability integral method was used to predict ground subsidence, tilt, horizontal strain, and curvature. The three-dimensional ground-displacement field was then applied to a nonlinear Winkler foundation model implemented in ANSYS. Sixteen scenarios were defined by combining two pipeline branches, two mining scales, and four mining-thickness levels.
items.author: Tuanjie Liu, Gui Liu, Xiangnan Li et al.

items.title: Efficacy of erector spinae plane block for patients with inflammatory bowel disease undergoing major abdominal surgery: A double-blind randomized controlled trial
items.summary: by Yasmin Alhamdah, Yehoshua Gleicher, Hermann dos Santos Fernandes, Sharon Peacock, Xiang Y. Ye, Christopher Brown, Anthony de Buck van Overstraeten, Zeev Friedman, Naveed Siddiqui Objectives Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) undergoing abdominal surgery face challenges in postoperative recovery due to high opioid needs and limited analgesic alternatives. The erector spinae plane (ESP) block has been shown to improve recovery in abdominal procedures, but its efficacy in the IBD population remains unknown. We investigated whether bilateral ESP blocks improve postoperative quality of recovery in this population. Methods In this prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial, adults with IBD scheduled for elective laparoscopic-assisted abdominal surgery were randomized to receive bilateral ESP blocks with either 0.5% ropivacaine or normal saline before induction of anesthesia.
items.author: Yasmin Alhamdah, Yehoshua Gleicher, Hermann dos Santos Fernandes et al.

items.title: Patient acceptance of continuous wearable vital-sign monitoring on surgical wards: A prospective mixed-methods survey study
items.summary: by Ephrahim E. Jerry, Daphne L. J. Nabben, Ashley J. R. De Bie Dekker, Igor W. F. Paulussen, R. Arthur Bouwman, Simon W. Nienhuijs Background Continuous wearable monitoring of vital signs is increasingly implemented on hospital wards to enable early detection of clinical deterioration and to reduce the burden of intermittent vital-sign measurements. While feasibility of wearable monitoring and its acceptance among healthcare professionals have been demonstrated, patient perspectives remain underexplored. Objective To evaluate patient experiences with wearable monitoring devices during hospitalization. Methods This prospective, single-center mixed-methods study included adult surgical ward patients monitored with a wearable device (Healthdot or viQtor) for ≥ 24 hours.
items.author: Ephrahim E. Jerry, Daphne L. J. Nabben, Ashley J. R. De Bie Dekker et al.

items.title: Comparative efficacy of modern antithrombotic regimens for saphenous vein graft patency after coronary artery bypass grafting: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
items.summary: by Ayesha Irshad Ansari, Muhammad Faraz Tariq, Muhammad Usman Khan Background Saphenous vein graft (SVG) occlusion remains common after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) despite aspirin. We compared contemporary postoperative antithrombotic regimens for preserving SVG patency. Methods We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 2026. The primary outcome was graft-level SVG occlusion. Aspirin was the reference treatment. Inconsistency was assessed using design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting. Because multiple SVGs could arise from the same patient, we added a post-hoc variance-inflation sensitivity analysis using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.15, 0.20, and 0.25.
items.author: Ayesha Irshad Ansari, Muhammad Faraz Tariq, Muhammad Usman Khan

items.title: Maternal epilepsy, prenatal antiseizure medication exposure, and risk of special education needs: A population-based cohort study in Wales
items.summary: by Alexia Karain, Jill P. Pell, Daniel F. Mackay, Scott Nelson, Sarjit Singh, Neha Rao, Michael Fleming Background Prenatal exposure to antiseizure medications (ASM) has been associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in children, although the contribution of maternal epilepsy itself remains unclear. This study aims to investigate associations between maternal epilepsy, prenatal ASM exposure and subsequent neurodevelopmental and educational outcomes. Methods A Welsh cohort was constructed of children born in 2009–2016 using linkage of routinely collected data in SAIL. Healthcare records identified children with prenatal exposure to at least one ASM and/or maternal epilepsy, with subgroup analyses by British National Formulary (BNF) ASM category and by individual ASM.
items.author: Alexia Karain, Jill P. Pell, Daniel F. Mackay et al.

items.title: The association between epilepsy and inflammatory bowel disease in adults: Findings from the 2023 National Health Interview Survey
items.summary: by Xianming Su, Yueying Lin, Shuyan Shen, Liya An, Ting Yang, Yuxing Qi, Xingzong Huang, Yinlong Deng, Jian Hu, Haiyu He, Dali Sun Background Evidence suggests a bidirectional association between nervous system diseases and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), but the association between epilepsy and IBD in adults remains unexplored. This study examined the adult epilepsy–IBD association using data from the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Methods Adult participants from the 2023 NHIS were selected based on inclusion and exclusion criteria. Baseline characteristics were compared using weighted analyses. Weighted multivariable logistic regression models with progressive covariate adjustment were performed to evaluate the association between epilepsy and IBD.
items.author: Xianming Su, Yueying Lin, Shuyan Shen et al.

items.title: BoolFunc-EA: A Boolean–evolutionary approach for accurate inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series gene expression data
items.summary: by Shohag Barman, Rudra Pratap Deb Nath Network inference is the process of discovering genetic information from time-series data. The inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series data represents a significant challenge in bioinformatics. Despite the development of many Boolean network inference methods, most struggle with scalability as they impose restrictions on regulatory genes for each target gene. Other methods suffer from local optimum issues or are unable to compute the exact mutual information between a regulatory gene and its target gene. To resolve these issues, we present a novel method referred to as BoolFunc-EA, which employs Boolean functions and a genetic algorithm to infer gene regulatory networks from time-series gene expression data.
items.author: Shohag Barman, Rudra Pratap Deb Nath

items.title: A multicentre comparative study of health sciences students' preferences for instructors' nonverbal communication skills across participating universities in Saudi Arabia and Malaysia
items.summary: by Raju Suresh Kumar, Shinu Pottathil, M.Ganesh Kamath, Muhammad Anwar Khan, Ahmaed Baashar, Abdulaziz Saleh Almulhim, Krutika Darbar Shaikh, Anroop B. Nair, Rekha Prabhu, Afzal Haq Asif, Hussien Yahya Almutawa, Abdullah Abdulhamid Ahmed Altaweel Nonverbal communication (NVC) is an important component of instructor–student interaction, yet evidence regarding health professions students’ perceptions across different educational and cultural settings remains limited. This multicentre cross-sectional study examined students’ perceptions of instructors’ NVC and explored the psychometric properties of a researcher-developed questionnaire across three universities in Saudi Arabia and Malaysia. Undergraduate health professions students completed a 21-item, five-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Psychometric evaluation included exploratory factor analysis, parallel analysis, internal consistency assessment, and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA).

items.title: The role of percutaneous trans-hepatic and trans-splenic variceal obliteration in uncontrolled gastric variceal bleeding
items.summary: by Kiyoun Yi, Young Joo Park, Hojun Lee, Hoon Kwon, Hyun Young Woo, Jeong Heo, Chang Won Kim Background/Aims Gastric variceal bleeding (GVB) is a serious complication of portal hypertension, with limited therapeutic options when conventional endoscopic and radiologic interventions are not feasible. Percutaneous trans-hepatic and trans-splenic variceal obliteration (PTVO) has been described as a salvage therapy; however, clinical evidence regarding its efficacy and safety remains scarce. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 23 cirrhotic patients (median age, 58 years; 18 men) who underwent PTVO for uncontrolled GVB between October 2017 to July 2024 at a tertiary hospital. Primary endpoints were technical success and postprocedural changes in liver function.
items.author: Kiyoun Yi, Young Joo Park, Hojun Lee et al.

items.title: A randomized controlled study of daily aspirin to reduce liver stiffness and noninvasive fibrosis markers in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)
items.summary: by Khanisorn Meesri, Akarawich Boondamnoen, Kittithat Tantitanawat, Anuchit Suksamai, Sakkarin Chirapongsathorn Objective To evaluate the effect of low-dose aspirin on liver stiffness and noninvasive fibrosis markers in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in a randomized controlled study. Methods Participants with MASLD were randomly assigned to receive either aspirin or a placebo. The primary outcome was the change in liver stiffness at 6 months measured using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE). Secondary outcomes included changes in liver enzyme levels and noninvasive fibrosis scores (FIB-4, APRI, and NAFLD fibrosis score). Results At the 6-month follow-up, the aspirin group showed a statistically significant reduction in liver stiffness compared to placebo [−0.64 kPa (95% CI, −0.88 to −0.41) vs.

items.title: Development of the decisional balance scale for health behaviors after transarterial chemoembolization in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A Modified Delphi Study
items.summary: by Yujun Jiang, Wenxi Guo, Wang Feng, Xiaolin Wang Objective Based on the decisional balance construct within the Transtheoretical Model, a preliminary instrument for evaluating health behavior decision-making among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma following transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) was developed. The Delphi expert consultation method was then used to assess item appropriateness, the degree of expert consensus, and content validity. This process provides an empirical foundation for subsequent refinement of the scale and its further psychometric validation in clinical practice. Method A modified Delphi method was employed. Between 10/12/2025 and 27/01/2026, 24 experts specializing in liver cancer patient care, interventional nursing, and psychological nursing from 16 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities) across China were invited to rate the importance and feasibility of each item.

items.title: A Highly Tunable (Ti,Zr)N$_x$-Based MIM Plasmonic Sensor for Multidomain Biological, Chemical, and Physical Sensing
items.summary: Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) plasmonic refractive index (RI) sensors have attracted considerable attention for label-free, real-time analyte detection; however, their reliance on noble metals such as gold and silver imposes fundamental constraints on tunability, thermal stability, and CMOS process compatibility. In this work, we propose a novel MIM plasmonic RI sensor based on a square ring resonator with embedded circular nanorods, employing the ternary nitride (Ti,Zr)N$_x$ as the plasmonic material, marking its first application in a MIM sensing platform. Compared to binary nitrides and other alternative plasmonic materials reported in the literature, (Ti,Zr)N$_x$ offers broader compositional tunability and greater flexibility in tailoring the optical response while remaining fully CMOS-compatible.
items.author: Mohammad Abrar Kabir, Aosaf Jarif Siddiquee, Abdullah Taharat et al.

items.title: Motion of dissipative solitons in quasi-one-dimensional potentials
items.summary: We consider the motion of two-dimensional (2D) dissipative solitons and soliton pairs in the framework of the cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation with quasi-1D potentials, spatially periodic or radial-lattice ones. The equation is solved numerically for inputs representing one or two fundamental solitons, which are set in motion by a kick. For the quasi-1D potential, the kick parallel to the potential axis naturally initiates free motion of the 2D solitons, as the model remains Galilean-invariant in this direction. Motion in the transverse direction, which may entail pulse multiplication, commences if the kick is strong enough. Oblique kicks lead to a straightforward superposition of the longitudinal and transverse motions.
items.author: Valentin Besse, Herv{é} Leblond, Dumitru Mihalache et al.

items.title: Geometry-conditioned differentiable surrogate with adjoint Monte Carlo sampling for scintillator detector co-design
items.summary: Optimizing light-guide geometries for scintillator-based imaging detectors requires repeated photon-transport evaluations, making direct Monte Carlo simulation computationally costly. Differentiable surrogates can accelerate these evaluations and support detector readout co-design aimed at improving information extraction from particle interactions. In this work we describe a surrogate model for photon transport. We develop it starting from a modular, event-driven Monte Carlo model for the generation and transport of scintillation photons, and a reciprocal Monte Carlo construction (an adjoint model) of a spatially and temporally resolved optical response field. The latter evaluates the collectible light output and its temporal structure from a scintillator volume by launching weighted photon trajectories from the light-guide readout face.
items.author: Lorenzo Pepa, Mohammad Ali Marashli, Nicolas Babio Elguero et al.

items.title: Femtosecond laser-controlled production of functional titanium niobate layers from TiO$_{2}$/Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders
items.summary: Conventional synthesis methods of titanium niobates (TNO) require prolongated high-temperature treatments. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we have developed a confined powder-bed femtosecond (fs) laser-based technique to sinter TNO films starting from a mixture of TiO$_{2}$ and Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders, avoiding furnace-based approaches. The influence of laser-processing conditions on film formation, phase composition, and microstructure is systematically investigated, demonstrating that different TNO phases and morphologies can be obtained by controlling the laser pulse energy. A comprehensive characterization of the processed films has been performed, providing insights into the mechanisms governing their formation, which appear to share key features with laser-induced backward transfer (LIBT) processes.
items.author: Gonzalo Gomez-Munoz, Aarón Calvo-Villoslada, Inmaculada Álvarez-Serrano et al.

items.title: 1.2 dB Insertion Loss in a Monolithically Integrated Silicon Mach-Zehnder Optical Isolator Using Stoichiometric Ce:YIG
items.summary: Integrated optical isolators play a crucial role in photonic integrated circuits (PICs) by effectively stabilizing optical signals, making them indispensable components for advanced photonic systems. However, integrated magneto-optical (MO) isolators suffer from their high insertion loss, which is mainly caused by the relatively low FoM of Ce:YIG MO thin films deposited on silicon. Here, we show that film stoichiometry plays a key role in controlling the FoM of Ce:YIG. We observed garnet phase Fe-rich and Ce-rich nano-clusters in non-stoichiometric Ce:YIG. By using an iron-deficient target, we demonstrated that nearly stoichiometric Ce:YIG films on Si(100) could be fabricated, eliminating the nano-cluster defects.

items.title: Apparent thermal conductivity governed by interface-injected phonon spectra
items.summary: Thermoreflectance techniques such as time- and frequency-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR and FDTR) are widely used to measure the thermal conductivity of bulk materials, thin films, and interfaces. When phonon mean free paths $Λ_ω$ become comparable to the thermal penetration depth, a Fourier analysis yields an apparent thermal conductivity $κ_{\rm app}$ that deviates from the bulk value $κ_{\rm bulk}$. Recent studies have highlighted the role of the phonon spectrum injected through the transducer interface, which is generally out of equilibrium owing to frequency-dependent transmission, and have shown that accounting for this nonequilibrium distribution can yield $κ_{\rm app}>κ_{\rm bulk}$, unlike conventional suppression-function analyses that predict only $κ_{\rm app}\leqκ_{\rm bulk}$.

items.title: Designing Incoherent Multispectral Diffractive Optical Networks for Satellite Image Classification
items.summary: Optical neural networks and diffractive optical computing provide a promising route for performing task-specific inference with high parallelism and lightweight electronic post-processing. These advantages are especially attractive for multispectral satellite imaging, where conventional workflows rely on transmitting high-dimensional image cubes to the ground for downstream electronic analysis. Here, we introduce a computationally efficient surrogate model-guided framework for designing incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks that directly output class probabilities onboard, eliminating the need to capture and transfer the full multispectral data cube for ground-side inference. We first train a physically compatible surrogate model, represented by a non-negative fully connected model that accommodates a generalized detector readout, yielding a task-specific non-negative multispectral intensity transformation that can be transferred to an optical processor.

items.title: Pyroelectric Harvesting from Steady Heat Sources via Active Piezoelectric Thermal Switching
items.summary: This study demonstrates pyroelectric energy harvesting from a steady heat source using active piezoelectric thermal switching in a PZT/Si bimorph cantilever. The same PZT layer serves as both the mechanical actuator and the pyroelectric energy-conversion element. Dual output electrodes enable separation of the pyroelectric and piezoelectric signals. Pyroelectric energy harvesting is experimentally demonstrated at frequencies up to 110 Hz and temperature differences as small as 5 K. Comparison with the response predicted from the independently measured pyroelectric coefficient, together with transient thermal simulations, identifies dynamic interfacial heat transfer as a key limitation to high-frequency operation. This work demonstrates a compact MEMS approach for higher-frequency pyroelectric energy harvesting from low-grade steady heat sources.

items.summary: Purpose This systematic scoping review evaluates contemporary advancements in the design and clinical application of lab-on-a-chip (LOC) microdevices specialised for measuring breast cancer cell motility parameters. It tracks the engineering frontiers of biomimetic systems and addresses their predictive potential in oncology research.

items.title: Recurrent Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension With Bilateral Abducens Nerve Palsy in a Prepubertal Child: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.summary: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is rare in prepubertal children and may present atypically. We report a recurrent case in a 7-year-old boy with bilateral abducens nerve palsy and papilledema. Refractory symptoms necessitated lumboperitoneal shunting, resulting in complete clinical recovery and sustained remission.
items.author: Rehman AU, Khan A, Shah SW, Ali A, Zafar MA, Ullah S, Kamil KA.

items.title: The Myasthenic Masquerade: A Case Report of Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 Mimicking Seronegative Myasthenia Gravis.
items.summary: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) can rarely mimic myasthenia gravis, presenting with fluctuating ptosis and fatigability. We describe a 20-year-old male initially suspected of seronegative myasthenia gravis whose diagnosis was established by electromyographic myotonic discharges and supportive family history. This case emphasizes the importance of careful phenotypic evaluation, family history.
items.author: Ayon MAAH, Ahmmed F, Roy S, Chowdhury II, Tamim SMT, Sagor SH.

items.title: Effect of Cysteamine on 90-Day Mortality in Patients With Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: Cysteamine has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and antibiotic-potentiating effects. We evaluated IV cysteamine in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia within REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) trial, an international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple interventions across several therapeutic domains.
items.author: Shankar-Hari M, Ryan EG, Pogson D, Golden D, Puxty K, Walden A, Craven TH, Derde L, Gordon AC.

items.title: Trade-facilitating measures help offset rise in new G20 trade restrictions
items.summary: The number of tariff increases and other non-facilitating trade measures introduced by G20 economies rose sharply in the first half of 2026, and the stockpile of such measures reached a record level, according to the WTO's latest report on G20 trade measures.

items.title: Assessing Guidance and Counseling Needs of Iranian Dental Students: A Cross-Sectional Study in Kerman University of Medical Sciences.
items.summary: Background Upon admission to the university, students encounter a range of personal, emotional, academic, and occupational challenges that impact their mental health and overall efficiency. This study aimed to evaluate the guidance and counseling needs of dental students at Kerman University of Medical Sciences.
items.author: Sajadi FS, Balvardi M, Akbari-Hooye H, Mollaali M.

items.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Towards Monkeypox Among Dental Professionals: Implications for Outbreak Preparedness-An Analytical Cross-Sectional Study.
items.summary: Background and aims Understanding healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices towards monkeypox is essential for timely recognition and prevention. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of dental professionals in Pakistan regarding the outbreak of monkeypox virus.
items.author: Nisar A, Abbasi MS, Ahmed B, Nadeem R, Shah R, Ahmed N, Jouhar R, Heboyan A.

items.title: vartracker: an end-to-end tool for pathogen longitudinal variant analysis and visualization.
items.summary: Longitudinal sequencing can reveal fine-grained pathogen evolution during acute and chronic infections and inform public health responses. However, integrating ordered pathogen genomic data into a coherent evolutionary and clinical framework can be tedious and error-prone. We present vartracker, an open-source tool for longitudinal pathogen variant analysis and visualization.
items.author: Foster CSP, Rawlinson WD.

items.title: mapfx.norm: a method for removing unwanted variation from massively parallel cytometry data.
items.summary: Massively parallel cytometry (MPC) experiments allow cost-effective quantification of >200 surface proteins at single-cell resolution. The Infinity Flow protocol was developed to measure highly informative protein 'Backbone' markers on all cells in wells distributed across plates, along with well-specific exploratory protein 'Infinity' markers.
items.author: Liao HC, Speed TP, McCarthy DJ, Salim A.

items.title: Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered ILC2s for targeted immune regulation.
items.summary: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering has transformed cellular immunotherapies, yet whether CAR signaling can direct innate lymphoid cell functions for therapeutic applications has not been established. IL-10-producing ILC2s (ILC2 10 ) suppress pathogenic T cell responses in preclinical transplant models, making them attractive candidates for engineered regulatory cell therapies.
items.author: Mashhouri S, Jegatheeswaran S, Colpitts SJ, Mathews JA, Reid KT, Levings MK, Crome SQ.

items.title: A TNF-producing neutrophil subset drives age-dependent hepatotoxicity in mice.
items.summary: The mechanisms by which aging contributes to the detrimental effect of cancer therapy are unclear. Here we show that while a synthetic double-stranded RNA (poly-inosinic:cytidylic acid (polyIC)) suppresses liver tumors in young mice, it induces lethal liver damage in aged mice.
items.author: Lee J, Gao Y, Zhang Y, Yang D, Havas A, Adams P, Shadel GS, Kaech SM, Feng GS.

items.title: Clinical analysis of patients with refractory status epilepticus in a tertiary hospital in northern Ceará, Brazil: a case series.
items.summary: Background Refractory status epilepticus (RSE) is a neurological emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality. Despite its clinical significance, data from regional tertiary centers in Brazil remain limited. Objective To characterize the clinical profile of RSE patients and to identify predictors associated with in-hospital mortality.
items.author: Afonso AJA, Carvalho FCP, Melo GBJ, Ribeiro EML.

items.title: Prolonged exposure for PTSD related to intimate partner violence during ongoing threat: a case study.
items.summary: Background: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is associated with the development of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and may adversely affect family functioning. Although prolonged exposure (PE) is an effective treatment for PTSD, its use in the context of ongoing IPV remains debated.
items.author: van Osch M, Kullberg ML, de Kleine RA, Schoorl M.

items.title: From being instructed and supported experiences to enacting educational roles: associations between past supervised experiences and educational role enactment among clinical teachers.
items.summary: Purpose Clinical teachers enact educational roles differently, yet relatively little is known about the antecedents of this variation. Drawing on social cognitive theory, this study examined whether physicians' past supervised experiences were associated with subsequent educational role enactment among attending physicians serving as clinical teachers.
items.author: Lin YC, Ou LC.

items.title: FGF23 in chronic kidney disease progression: biomarker or mediator?
items.summary: Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) is an important regulator of phosphate balance that rises early in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Evidence suggests that elevated FGF23 is associated with adverse renal outcomes. However, whether FGF23 is merely a biomarker or a direct mediator of CKD progression remains unresolved.
items.author: Chandrakar K, Shet Shirodkar SN, Nagaraju SP, Maradi R, Rao IR.

items.title: AI-derived retinal vascular metrics and MoCA-B-defined mild cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes: a community-based cross-sectional study.
items.summary: Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major risk factor for mild cognitive impairment (MCI). As an embryological extension of the brain, the retina offers a unique window into cerebral microvascular health; artificial intelligence (AI) now enables objective, large-scale quantification of retinal vascular parameters to investigate this association.
items.author: Sun R, Ying H, Zhao S, Wang J, Xu L, Jiang S, Luo Y, Yan C, Ran M, Yang K, Hu Y.

items.title: Melatonin ameliorates calcification in senescent vascular smooth muscle cells under phosphate conditions via the PI3K/AKT pathway.
items.summary: In patients with chronic kidney disease, vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) senescence and osteogenic transdifferentiation induced by factors such as hyperphosphatemia are key pathological mechanisms underlying vascular calcification. Recent studies have shown that melatonin exerts protective effects by modulating this process.
items.author: Chen L, Chen Z, Li H, Yao L, Xu T, Qu W, Zheng X, Du W, Zheng H, Ji Z.

items.title: Innovations in intradialytic hypotension management: pathophysiology, precision monitoring, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
items.summary: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is one of the most frequent and consequential complications of maintenance hemodialysis, affecting up to 40% of treatments depending on the definition used. IDH is independently associated with myocardial stunning, cerebral hypoperfusion, loss of residual kidney function, vascular access failure, and increased mortality.
items.author: Bizer B, Thongprayoon C, Kashani K.

items.title: Chronic evoked seizures differentially worsen cognitive function and long-term neuropsychiatric comorbidities in Alzheimer's disease-related genotypes
items.summary: Variants in one of three deterministic risk genes - amyloid precursor protein (APP), presenilin 1 (PSEN1), or presenilin 2 (PSEN2) - lead to early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD), which also carries a high risk of spontaneous seizures. Seizures may worsen AD-related behavioral comorbidities, including depression, anxiety, and cognitive impairment.
items.author: Knox, K., Fang, J., Davidson, S. et al.

items.title: Identification of a human Anxa1-associated dopaminergic population linked to Parkinson's disease vulnerability and sensorimotor putaminal networks
items.summary: The selective loss of dopaminergic (DA) neurons drives motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD). In mice, Anxa1+ SNc DA neurons are highly vulnerable in PD models, project to the dorsolateral striatum, and display movement-correlated activity, yet they lack clearly defined human counterparts.
items.author: Schonfeld, E., Baliki, M. N., Monje, M. H. G. et al.

items.title: The language network responds stronger to connected than to unconnected sentences
items.summary: Purpose: Reliable functional mapping of the language network and preoperative assessment of language lateralization are essential for safe and effective craniotomy in patients with lesions in language-eloquent brain regions, yet existing fMRI language paradigms are often time-consuming and place substantial cognitive and economic demands on patients and diagnostic services.
items.author: Paliga, F., Javed, Z., Unnerstall, M. et al.

items.title: Dynamic T-cell receptor repertoire remodeling is associated with murine and human lung allograft dysfunction
items.summary: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is a major cause of late graft failure after lung transplantation. Acute cellular rejection is an established risk factor for CLAD. However, its diagnosis by biopsy may incompletely capture dynamic and spatially heterogeneous immune remodeling within the allograft.
items.author: Wang, Y., Palchevskiy, V., Lari, S. et al.

items.title: A Conserved Interface Between COG4 and Syntaxin 5 Is Essential for Intra-Golgi Membrane Trafficking
items.summary: The conserved oligomeric Golgi (COG) complex tethers retrograde intra-Golgi transport vesicles, but how it engages the SNARE machinery to support vesicle fusion remains unclear. Here, we identify a functional interface between the COG subunit COG4 and the Qa-SNARE Syntaxin 5 (STX5).
items.author: Neetole, S. T., Pokrovskaya, I., Shank, B. et al.

items.title: Physical constraints on the social-genetic dynamics of mtDNA inside plant mitochondria
items.summary: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes essential cellular machinery and is contained within mitochondria. This physical containment shapes the genetic dynamics of mtDNA populations in the cell. In plants (and other non-bilaterians), mtDNA colocalisation is essential for recombination, while other cellular priorities may favour mtDNA spacing through the cell.
items.author: Chustecki, J. M., Summers, A. J., Wang, J. et al.

items.title: Genomics of the diversification of Heliconius cydno (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in northern South America: geographic and phenotypic patterns
items.summary: The interplay between natural selection, gene flow, and geography is a key driver of population differentiation. This study investigates their influence on the recent adaptive radiation of Heliconius cydno, a mimetic and aposematic butterfly with striking variation in wing color pattern across its distribution in Central and northern South America.
items.author: Arias Cardenas, A., Rueda-M, N., Arias, C. F. et al.

items.title: Paint-Lac: A photoactivatable integrator for L-lactate
items.summary: Genetically encoded integrators, which convert transient signals into persistent optical signals, can provide unique insights into cell signaling, but the range of target species remains very limited. This work introduces the first photoactivatable integrator for L-lactate, Paint-Lac1, which operates through a ligand-modulated, irreversible {beta}-elimination reaction.
items.author: Peng, J., Takahashi-Yamashiro, K., Terai, T. et al.

items.title: The Impact of Germ Layer Origin on the Ageing Transcriptome
items.summary: Ageing is accompanied by widespread changes in gene expression, yet whether these changes share any common organisation across groups of tissues remains unclear. Adult tissues arise from three embryonic germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm), so shared developmental lineage could influence how tissues age.
items.author: Ederies, T., de Magalhaes, J. P.

items.title: Predicted templates improve the prediction of antibody-antigen structures by AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2
items.summary: Motivation: In spite of the much improved protein structure prediction methods, the success rate remains low for antibody-antigen complexes. While this can be improved by computationally demanding massive sampling, results are still much poorer than for most other types of protein-protein interactions.
items.author: Ziaee, O., Lazou, M., Joseph-McCarthy, D. et al.

items.title: Functional hot-spots and communication networks of the cellular prion protein from information-theoretical measures
items.summary: The cellular prion protein (PrPC) is a ~33 kDa molecule featuring a disordered region and a globular part, mostly expressed in the brain and in the central nervous system. The biological role of this protein is still unclear, but its pathogenic behavior in specific conditions has been ascertained.
items.author: Guadagnin Pattaro, A., Gasparotto, D., Biasini, E. et al.

items.title: Avibactam dose-escalation augments aztreonam-avibactam activity against extensively drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae persisters
items.summary: Objectives: Strategies to address persistence during {beta}-lactam/{beta}-lactamase inhibitor (BL/BLI) therapy remain undefined. To address this clinical gap, we explored increasing AVI exposure throughout aztreonam/avibactam (ATM-AVI) administration to enhance combination activity and suppress extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae persisters. Methods: 24h time courses were profiled against three XDR K.
items.author: Klem, J. F., Kaur, J. N., Liu, Y. et al.

items.title: Hydrogen sulfide modulation of intrinsic excitability in rat hippocampal CA1 pyramidal cells
items.summary: Although traditionally known as a toxic gas, hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is now recognized as a biologically active molecule with modulatory effects on many physiological targets, including the central nervous system. In this context, pyramidal cells of the hippocampus express the H2S-generating enzymes required for its synthesis and local release.
items.author: Martinez-Rojas, V. A., Perez-Barragan, A., Rojas-Hernandez, L. et al.

items.title: Rescue of KATP channel nonsense mutations using anticodon-edited transfer RNAs
items.summary: KATP channels composed of sulfonylurea receptor 1 (SUR1) and Kir6.2 encoded by ABCC8 and KCNJ11, respectively, play a crucial role in regulating insulin secretion. Nonsense mutations that introduce premature termination codons (PTCs) in ABCC8 and KCNJ11 disrupt KATP channel expression, resulting in congenital hyperinsulinism (HI).
items.author: Kuo, Y.-Y., Yang, Z., Porter, J. J. et al.

items.title: Serum albumin restrains obesity by coordinating brown adipose thermogenic capacity with beta3-adrenergic responsiveness
items.summary: Obesity reflects chronic imbalance between energy storage and expenditure, yet how abundant circulating carrier proteins contribute remains poorly understood. Using constitutive and inducible albumin-deficient mice, we show that reduced circulating albumin promotes diet-induced adiposity and hepatic lipid accumulation while impairing energy expenditure, cold tolerance and stimulus-induced lipid mobilization.
items.author: Luo, Z., Jiang, Y., Liu, H. et al.

items.title: Agriculture group meeting weighs trends in global food market trade
items.summary: Current conditions in global agricultural commodities were the focus of a meeting of the Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS) Global Food Market Information Group, held at WTO headquarters in Geneva on 23-24 November. The AMIS, launched by the G20 group of major economies in 2011, seeks to improve market transparency and strengthen food security by bringing together the principal economies involved in agricultural commodities trade and helping to coordinate policy action in times of market uncertainty.

items.title: A Theoretical Investigation of Magnetic Susceptibility Measurement of Diamagnetic Liquids Using a Michelson Interferometer
items.summary: We examine the theoretical use of a Michelson interferometer to infer the magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic liquid from a magnetically induced surface deformation. A ring magnet changes the liquid thickness along the sample beam, producing a signed phase shift relative to a fixed optical reference. For a double traversal of the sample, the fringe displacement is $m = 2(n_{\ell} - n_a)Δz/λ$. We derive the susceptibility inversion both in a local gravity approximation and with surface tension included through the linearized Young-Laplace equation. The treatment distinguishes a finite reference field from a zero-field reference, specifies the displacement sign and susceptibility contrast, and identifies calibration and uncertainty requirements.
