items.title: Polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
items.summary: High-refractive-index dielectric metasurfaces supporting optical modes are ideal candidates for achieving strong coupling with transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) materials. However, optical illumination with a specific polarization is always required to estimate the maximal coupling strength in such coupled systems due to the polarization-dependent optical modes. Here, we propose a self-hybridized strong coupling between Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBICs) mode and A excitons in the same bulk WS2 metasurface. By changing the thickness of the bulk WS2 metasurfaces, a typical anticrossing behavior with Rabi splitting of 165.9 meV is observed. Such Rabi splitting is unchanged when changing the polarization of the incident light from linearly to circularly polarizations, demonstrating the polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling.
items.author: Xiongwei Guo, Fu Liu, Jinhai Si et al.

items.title: Analysis of Geometric Eigenmode Splitting in Planar Microwave Resonators
items.summary: A traditional challenge in planar microwave resonator design is to find geometric mechanisms that can control individual resonant frequencies - or tune coupling between specific eigenmodes - without affecting other system parameters, such as the center frequency. Achieving this capability can be transformative for the design of microwave sensors, filters, antennas and resonant networks. Starting from first principles, we outline the development of an analytical method that guides practical design by suggesting specific perturbation shapes capable of achieving resonant mode-splitting while keeping the center frequency nearly stationary. This approach opens the door to novel designs that were previously difficult to discover or optimize.
items.author: Hagen Papenburg, Jason Corn, Romain Speciel et al.

items.title: Exploring the Potential of Ag Nanoparticles Embedded Activated Carbon as an Efficient Dispersive Solid-Phase Micro Extractor for Batch and Mini-Column Remediation and Detection of Eosin Yellow Textile Dye in Water: Performance, Mechanistic Insights, Sensing and Reusability Study.
items.summary: A simple, superhydrophobic, superoleophilic and low-cost Ag nanoparticles (Ag NPs) embedded activated carbon (AC) (Ag NPs/AC) has been established as efficient and promising dispersive solid-phase micro extractor (d-μ SPME) for remediation, recovery and sensing of eosin yellow (EY) textile dye in water bodies.
items.author: Abduljabbar TN, Alblawi KS, Alwael H, Bashammakh AS, Alnajjar HR, Nasef HA, El-Shahawi MS.

items.title: Serial Tracheal Changes in Possible Relapsing Polychondritis.
items.summary: Serial CT may reveal evolving airway cartilage abnormalities in possible airway-predominant relapsing polychondritis. In patients with steroid-responsive cough, systemic inflammation, and normal lung parenchyma, careful assessment of the cartilaginous tracheal wall and comparison with prior CT images may facilitate recognition.
items.author: Kurimoto R, Nishiyama A, Motoori K, Suda A.

items.title: Fish Bone in the Esophagus.
items.summary: Emergency endoscopy within 2 h is standard for esophageal foreign body impaction; retention beyond 24 h increases serious complication risk by 14.1-fold. This awake cap-assisted technique with patient cooperation appears safe and effective in selected patients intolerant of general anesthesia or standard sedation.
items.author: Su D, Tan Y, Tang X, Yang Q.

items.title: Non-Intestinal Adenocarcinoma Centered in the Middle Ear With Focal Mucinous Differentiation: A Rare Case Managed With Surgery and Adjuvant Radiotherapy.
items.summary: A 68-year-old man with longstanding unilateral hearing loss and persistent otorrhoea was found to have a rare non-intestinal adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous differentiation centered in the middle ear. He underwent mastoidectomy and tympanomastoid surgery followed by adjuvant radiotherapy. More than 5 years later, he remains disease-free with persistent hearing loss.
items.author: Saife S, Al Kiswani S, Al-Qaisi MZ, Eid S, Ajlouni FAH, Nofal A, Al Saraireh O.

items.title: The ordinary in the extraordinary: stories, relationships, and the role of general practitioners in times of disaster.
items.summary: Background International research on disaster response highlights general practitioners' (GPs') practical roles and contributions. They act as frontline health care providers, delivering first-contact care, maintaining continuity for chronic and mental health conditions, buffering hospital demand, and supporting community resilience across all phases of a disaster.
items.author: Rønneberg M, Mjølstad BP, Hvas L, Getz LO.

items.title: Melatonin as a multi-target modulator of chemoresistance in colorectal cancer: mechanistic insights and clinical perspectives.
items.summary: Chemoresistance in colorectal cancer (CRC) occurs for several major reasons, such as the enhancement of chemotherapy drug efflux and the attenuation of apoptosis. Enhanced efflux of chemotherapy drugs occurs due to increased expression and activity of ABC family transporters, especially ABCB1 (P-gp).
items.author: Vaghari-Tabari M, Mahrooz A, Yousefi B, Molavand M.

items.title: Associations between urate‑lowering strategies and kidney function trajectories: a real‑world comparative study.
items.summary: Hyperuricemia contributes to chronic kidney disease progression, yet whether different urate-lowering agents are associated with distinct kidney function trajectories remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the associations between dotinurad, a selective urate transporter 1 (URAT1) inhibitor, and kidney function trajectories compared with benzbromarone and allopurinol.
items.author: Ikenouchi K, Suzukawa R, Inaba S, Takahashi D, Mori T, Iimori S, Sohara E, Uchida S, Mandai S.

items.title: Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.
items.summary: Ischemic stroke and ischemic acute kidney injury are both clinical challenges. Danhong injection (DHI) has been reported to exert protective effects against cerebral and renal ischemic injury. However, the shared therapeutic targets and mechanisms underlying its effects in these two organs remain unclear.
items.author: Hu F, Sun Y, Shi Y, Zhang Z, Shi S, Zhou H, Jin B, Wan H, Guo Y.

items.title: Xist deletion in T cells protects against influenza-induced lung injury
items.summary: Sex differences in antiviral immunity are well established, yet the contribution of X-Chromosome Inactivation (XCI) to T cell responses during infection is unknown. Here, we identify an unexpected role for Xist RNA in shaping T cell immunity and pulmonary injury following influenza infection.
items.author: Valero-Pacheco, N., Forsyth, K. S., Toothacre, N. et al.

items.title: EPIC2: integrating single-cell chromatin accessibility with human genetics to identify trait-relevant cell types
items.summary: Summary: EPIC2 is a computational and statistical framework for prioritizing trait-relevant cellular contexts by integrating genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics with single-cell chromatin accessibility data. It accounts for linkage disequilibrium when testing for association between GWAS association strength and cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility at both SNP and regulatory-peak resolutions.
items.author: Zhu, L., Jiang, Y.

items.title: Bryostatin-1 exploits a developmental signaling vulnerability in MEF2D-rearranged B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia
items.summary: MEF2D-rearranged (MEF2D-r) B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) is a rare molecular subtype associated with high-risk clinical features and frequent relapse and characterized by a distinctive pre-B-cell developmental state and dependence on pre-B-cell receptor (pre-BCR) signaling. Despite these distinctive biological features, MEF2D-r BCP-ALL lacks subtype-directed therapy.
items.author: Glaziou, Q., Qi, X., Aswad, L. et al.

items.title: Syngeneic human iPSC Macrophages and Microglia possess distinct neuroinflammatory profiles, responses to HIV infection, and ART treatment
items.summary: Macrophages are innate immune cells that primarily function as professional phagocytes, playing essential roles throughout the body in host defense and maintaining homeostasis. The CNS is populated by two anatomically distinct macrophage populations; parenchymal microglia and border-resident CNS-associated macrophages (CAMs).
items.author: Oteju, O., Daniali, M., Kist, T. et al.

items.title: Media matters: A resource for understanding the determinants of migratory potential of malignant and non-malignant cells
items.summary: Cell mobility is critical for homeostatic processes such as wound repair and diseases like cancer metastasis. While the advent of migrastatic and antimetastatic therapies has promise, the identification and translation of pathways important for migratory plasticity into druggable targets approved in clinical trials are considerably lacking.
items.author: Kim, B., Lopez, A., Osuna, M. F. et al.

items.title: YAP activity sustains mitochondrial adaptation to NAMPT inhibition in triple-negative breast cancer
items.summary: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is an essential metabolic cofactor, and maintenance of NAD+ homeostasis is critical for cancer cell survival. Pharmacological inhibition of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), the rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway, induces NAD+ depletion and energetic stress, although the development of resistance limits its therapeutic potential.
items.author: Buongiorno, A., Franceschi, E., Cerri, E. et al.

items.title: Smyd1 regulates H3K4me3 to support adaptive fatty acid oxidation in the adult heart during lipid overload
items.summary: Obesity and metabolic syndrome are major risk factors for heart failure, and impaired fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a key contributor to metabolic dysfunction in obesity-related cardiomyopathy. However, how the heart maintains FAO and adapts to chronic lipid overload remains poorly understood.
items.author: Mukai, R., Oka, S., Sung, E.-A. et al.

items.title: Single-molecule in situ detection and quantification of mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy
items.summary: The mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is a multi-copy genome present in most eukaryotic cells and essential for life. The presence of different mtDNA variants within a cell, or heteroplasmy, may cause pathology when the level of deleterious variants exceeds a critical threshold.
items.author: Gottardo, S., Chowdhury, S. R., Wilson, B. A. et al.

items.title: Variation of anti-oomycete activity in Pseudomonas spp.: phenotypic characterization and comparative genomics
items.summary: Pathogenic aquatic oomycetes Aphanomyces astaci and Saprolegnia parasitica represent a major threat to biodiversity and aquaculture production, but their interactions with host-associated microbes remain poorly understood. From a collection of bacterial isolates (n = 328) obtained from fish and crayfish hosts, we focused on Pseudomonas spp.
items.author: Saric, E., Miljanovic, A., Struski, P. et al.

items.title: MASH-in-a-dish reveals fatty acid-driven itaconate crosstalk between Kupffer cells and hepatocytes
items.summary: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is driven by interactions between metabolically stressed hepatocytes and non-parenchymal liver cells, leading to hepatocyte injury, inflammation, and fibrosis. Metabolites can mediate intercellular communication, yet their contribution to MASH pathogenesis remains poorly understood, partly because tissue dissociation disrupts the local metabolic environment.
items.author: Chang, J.-C., Sullock Enzlin, A., Haaker, M. W. et al.

items.title: Layer-Weighted Source-Anchored Transfer Learning for Multi-Omics Survival Prediction and Risk Stratification in Younger Breast Cancer Patients
items.summary: Background- Younger breast cancer patients (<50 years) often present with more aggressive disease and distinct molecular characteristics, yet predictive models for this group are underpowered due to small sample sizes. Most existing models are built on older populations and may not translate directly, particularly across multiple omics data types.
items.author: Guo, W., Wang, B., Tatsuoka, C.

items.title: Myhre syndrome variants form long-lived SMAD heterotrimers through a rewired polar interface at the variant site
items.summary: TGF-{beta} signaling through SMAD transcription factors governs development and tissue homeostasis. Most disease-associated SMAD4 mutations cause loss of function, but five germline variants at only two positions in the MH2 domain, Arg496 and Ile500, instead cause Myhre syndrome, a rare condition inducing pathway dysregulation.
items.author: Torner, C., Pluta, R., Condeminas, M. et al.

items.title: From prophylaxis to precision immunotherapy via engineering vaccine platforms.
items.summary: Vaccines are evolving from antigen-delivery products into modular technologies designed to elicit specific immune functions. Although prophylactic vaccination aims to establish protective memory before exposure, therapeutic vaccination must redirect immunity in the presence of persistent antigen, immune suppression or pathological tissue remodeling.
items.author: Cabral-Miranda G, Silva JDQ, Hamaguchi B, Giugni FR, Durães-Carvalho R, Cabral-Marques O, Câmara NOS, Sabino EC, Krieger JE.

items.title: Remarkable Biosynthetic Diversity in the Bionectriaceae: Uncovering the genomic basis of antipathogen bioactivity of cacao fungal endophytes Clonostachys rosea and Waltergamsia zeylanica.
items.summary: Cacao (Theobroma cacao) production in tropical countries is threatened by fungal diseases caused by Moniliophthora roreri and M. perniciosa. Two cacao pod endophytes from Bionectriaceae, Clonostachys rosea TCF417 and Waltergamsia zeylanica TCF400, exhibit growth antagonism towards M. roreri; however, the genetic basis underlying the bioactivity of these strains has not been addressed. Here, we aimed to identify biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) potentially associated with the antifungal bioactivity of these two strains and performed a comparative analysis with 30 publicly available Bionectriaceae genomes using BiG-SCAPE. Whole-genome sequencing using Oxford Nanopore and Illumina technologies, resulted in assemblies of 52.9 Mb (C. rosea TCF417) and 31 Mb (W.
items.author: Atencio, L. A., Castillo, H. E., Barrios-Jaen, M. et al.

items.title: High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Millimeter-Scale Malignant Territories and Immune Exclusion patterns in Human Salivary Gland Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma
items.summary: Background/Objectives: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the salivary gland (SGACC) is a rare malignancy with frequent late recurrence and limited response to systemic and immune therapies. Bulk and single-cell sequencing do not preserve tissue architecture, so the spatial organization of its MYB-driven myoepithelial and luminal tumor cells, stroma, and immune cells remains poorly defined. This study aimed to map the SGACC tumor microenvironment at near-cellular resolution. Methods: Visium HD based spatial transcriptomics was performed on four SGACC tissue sections from three patients with tubulo-cribriform tumor form in stage III - IV. Bins of 10 x 10 {micro}m were annotated and deconvolved with cell2location using an integrated single-cell reference of 119,189 cells from 20 donors.
items.author: Bijukumar, G., Hoff, K., Brayer, K. J. et al.

items.title: High GPX4 Expression Marks an Oxidative-Metabolic, PD-L1/CD47-Low and Stroma-Poor Tumor State in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
items.summary: Background: Glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) protects cancer cells from ferroptosis and is a candidate therapeutic target in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). How GPX4 expression relates to the immune and metabolic features of patient tumors is not well characterized. Methods: We analyzed RNA-sequencing data from 366 primary tumors of the TCGA-LIHC PanCancer Atlas cohort (365 with survival data). Associations between GPX4 and ten immune and stress-response markers were tested by Spearman correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, then re-estimated after adjustment for consensus tumor purity, CTNNB1 and TP53 mutation, age and sex. A T-cell-inflamed profile, a CD8 T-cell score and an NRF2 target-gene score, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) of GPX4-high versus GPX4-low tumors, and Cox models were added as further tests.
items.author: Govindaraj, P. R., Akaye, M. P.

items.title: Metabolic priming recruits tumour cells across a mitochondrial vulnerability threshold and sensitizes them to chemotherapy
items.summary: Intratumour heterogeneity allows a fraction of cancer cells to escape otherwise effective treatment. Here we ask whether metabolic priming can recruit heterogeneous tumour cells into a transient mitochondrial state that is selectively vulnerable to photodynamic damage. Tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester (TMRM) has previously been shown to act as a mitochondria targeted photosensitizer; we exploit its voltage-dependent accumulation and dynamic fluorescence during pulsed illumination to quantify vulnerability in single cells. The response is a reproducible fluorescence excursion, a rise to a maximum followed by a decay, accompanied by reactive oxygen species production. Comparing seventeen descriptors of this excursion against subsequent fate in 195 cells across four arms shows that quantities referenced to each cell's own resting value outperform static intensity.
items.author: Iborra, F. J.

items.title: A latent tau amplifier in the neuronal proteome lowers the seeding threshold for Alzheimers disease pathology
items.summary: The stereotyped spread of tau pathology through connected brain regions is accompanied by striking differences in the vulnerability of individual neuronal populations, pointing to cell-intrinsic determinants of susceptibility. Using a combination of computational APR analysis, in vitro and cellular aggregation assays, and quantitative proteomics of human postmortem brain, we identify the splicing factor TRA2B as an endogenous modifier of this susceptibility. TRA2B enhances the activity of patient-derived tau seeds, promotes tau pathology in vivo, and progressively redistributes from the nucleus into insoluble tau-associated material in Alzheimers disease brain. Mechanistically, TRA2B contains two aggregation-prone regions (APRs) homologous to tau nucleation sites that are required for tau interaction and seeding enhancement.
items.author: Tsaka, G., Kolla, R., Wiedmer, A. E. et al.

items.title: Read&Tag enables antibody-independent combinatorial and multifactorial chromatin profiling
items.summary: Genome-wide chromatin profiling methods based on in situ tagmentation have expanded access to epigenomic information but generally rely on antibodies, thereby limiting their multifactorial capacity and the direct measurement of combinatorial chromatin states. Here, we introduce Read&Tag, in which engineered chromatin reader domains or intrabodies are fused directly to the Tn5 transposase to target specific chromatin features in situ. Read&Tag profiles active and repressive histone modifications, DNA methylation, and elongating RNA polymerase II, with signal amplitude increasing with target abundance and remaining robust in frozen tissue and low-input samples. Because the targeting module is a protein of defined structure and affinity, two specificities can be combined within a single complex.
items.author: Schneider, M., Kopp, L. C., Schwarzlose, C. et al.

items.title: Bayesian nonparametric identification of spectrally distinct neural states
items.summary: Identifying neural oscillations is essential for linking fast brain dynamics to underlying cognitive processes. However, this is challenging because oscillatory events can be brief, embedded in 1/f-like background activity, and may comprise an unknown number of spectrally distinct states. Conventional approaches often apply narrowband band-pass filters to one or a few predefined frequency bands and then use amplitude thresholding to identify oscillatory events, but detection outcomes can be highly sensitive to these choices. Although recent unsupervised alternatives based on hidden Markov models (HMMs) address these limitations, they still require the number of states to be specified in advance and can underfit or overfit when this number is misspecified.
items.author: Yamada, S., Nagel, S. E., Kobeleva, X. et al.

items.title: Relationships between the isotopic signatures of dissolved inorganic carbon and environmental variability in Northern Ireland coastal waters
items.summary: The isotopic signatures of dissolved inorganic carbon ({delta}13C-DIC) can provide a sensitive tracer of biological and biogeochemical processes in aquatic environments. However, isotopic measurements remain uncommon within routine coastal monitoring programmes. This pilot study investigated spatial variability in {delta}13C-DIC in surface waters across twelve Northern Ireland coastal monitoring stations sampled during July 2020. We tested the relationships between {delta}13C-DIC, dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) concentration, nutrients, chlorophyll-a, temperature and salinity. {delta}13C-DIC exhibited substantial spatial variability, ranging from 1.25 to 2.53{per thousand}. Significant positive relationships were observed between {delta}13C-DIC and temperature (R2 = 0.55, p = 0.009), chlorophyll-a concentration (R2 = 0.38, p = 0.045) and DIC concentration (R2 = 0.52, p = 0.012), while significant negative relationships occurred with dissolved inorganic nitrogen (R2 = 0.53, p = 0.011) and phosphate (R2 = 0.44, p = 0.026).
items.author: Hunter, W. R., Smyth, C.

items.title: LRCP: identifying functionally related SNPs and genes from phenome-wide genetic-effect correlations using GWAS summary statistics
items.summary: Genetic correlation describes which traits share genetic causes. The transposed question, which variants act alike across the phenome, has no comparable estimator, although it points directly to shared genes, pathways and regulators. Correlations of GWAS Z scores between variants across many traits are easy to compute, but they are confounded by linkage disequilibrium (LD) and, for any pair of variants, by sample overlap and genetic correlation among the GWAS. We show that in 452 Pan-UK Biobank GWAS the effective number of independent traits is only 58, and that naive tests reject 51-70% of null pairs of distal variants. We introduce LRCP (likelihood and regression on cross-products of Z scores), which estimates the phenome-wide genetic-effect correlation{rho} between SNPs by regressing Z-score cross-products on LD cross components, using per-SNP heritability enrichment from the companion method LRCQ and LDSC-derived plug-ins.
items.author: Chen, L. G., Thach, T. Q., Sham, P. C.

items.title: LRCQ: phenome-wide heritability enrichment of genomic loci from GWAS summary statistics
items.summary: Some genetic variants are associated with many traits, but a variant's GWAS statistics are also inflated by the effects of variants in LD with it and by confounding shared by all variants in a study. Existing measures of per-variant pleiotropy, such as counts of significant associations or multi-trait association tests, do not separate these sources. Stratified LD score regression separates them for one trait at a time and only through predefined annotations. We present LRCQ (LD score regression on {chi}2 across many GWAS), which estimates for each locus its phenome-wide heritability enrichment: the variance of its causal effects across a set of traits, relative to an average locus.
items.author: Chen, L. G., Thach, T. Q., Sham, P. C.

items.title: CortexDecoder: Efficient fMRI-to-Image Reconstruction from Cortical Flatmaps
items.summary: Recent brain decoding work has shown the potential of Vision Transformers (ViTs) to learn mappings from neural representations to visual features. Here we present CortexDecoder, a framework that reconstructs viewed images from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) flatmaps, which are neural responses projected onto the cortical surface and unfolded into 2D images. We show that a frozen, pretrained cortical foundation model is sufficient for competitive reconstruction. A frozen CortexMAE encoder turns flatmap patches into brain tokens, and two lightweight cross-attention bridges map these tokens to semantic CLIP embeddings and low-level image features. The final image is generated using a frozen SDXL-unCLIP model which takes a low-level image reconstruction as an initial image and a predicted CLIP embedding used to condition the image generation.
items.author: Imoto-Tar, T., Fung, M., Gurha, A.

items.title: Decoding the molecular cues regulating the transition of Influenza virus polymerase from transcriptase to replicase.
items.summary: Influenza virus polymerase (FluPol) dynamically transitions between distinct conformational states to coordinate viral gene transcription and genome replication. While vRNP-associated monomeric FluPol supports transcription, ANP32-dependent asymmetric and ANP32-independent symmetric polymerase dimers mediate genome and antigenome (vRNA/cRNA) replication. How FluPol coordinates these distinct functional states to maintain the transcription-replication balance remains poorly understood. Here, we identify and characterize interdomain interactions within PB2 that govern the stability of the replication-competent conformation of FluPol. Specifically, a highly conserved salt bridge between PB2 Mid-E282 and NLS-K752 stabilizes the replicase conformation, while the charge state of residue 627 (E or K) dictates ANP32 engagement, together coordinating polymerase dimerization and replication activity.
items.author: De, A., Roy, A., Mondal, A.

items.title: Cell-state conditioning predicts the expression response to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects
items.summary: Background: Second-generation sequence models can be conditioned on a cell state supplied as a single-cell snapshot rather than selected from a fixed catalogue, but whether that conditioning carries an experimentally applied perturbation has not been tested. Results: We conditioned such a model on interferon-{beta}-stimulated and unstimulated monocytes from a published experiment, using cells disjoint from those providing the measurement, and asked whether the predicted expression response tracks the measured one and whether the same conditioning identifies expression QTL specific to the stimulated state. Predicted and measured responses agree at Spearman {rho} = 0.616 across 119 genes (95% CI 0.486 to 0.716), and at 0.607 after all 119 target genes are deleted from the conditioning input; across fifteen conditions the model's response scales with how much each condition's biology genuinely overlaps the target response (slope 0.73, Pearson 0.92), and a near-neighbour monocyte subset receives 0.295 against a measured overlap of 0.336.
items.author: He, H., Sun, J., Xu, J. et al.

items.title: Reproducing squat kinematics after total knee replacement with bi-level inverse optimal control
items.summary: Total knee replacement restores mobility in patients with advanced osteoarthritis, yet many individuals still experience limited ability to perform high-flexion tasks such as squatting. Current preoperative planning relies on static imaging and does not evaluate postoperative high-flexion kinematics. In this study, we developed a simulation framework that uses bi-level inverse optimal control to reproduce postoperative squat kinematics from subject-specific models. Musculoskeletal models were built for six total knee replacement patients from experimental squat recordings. Cost-function weights were identified in an individualised setting and in a group-level setting. The former gives a subject-specific reconstruction when postoperative motion is available. The latter yields one shared cost function that does not need each patient's postoperative trajectory.
items.author: Song, H.

items.title: GENECraft: A Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System for Controllable Regulatory DNA Design
items.summary: Designing regulatory DNA requires reconciling two complementary modeling paradigms: genomic language models (gLMs) capture evolutionary syntax without guaranteeing targeted regulatory activity, whereas sequence-to-function predictors provide explicit functional supervision without enforcing native-like sequence plausibility. We introduce GENECraft, a training-free Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System (FP-DDS) that couples a genomic language model (Carbon) and a functional oracle (AlphaGenome) during inference-time optimization to balance predicted regulatory activity and consistency with genomic sequence priors. GENECraft evolves continuous latent nucleotide logits while evaluating strictly decoded discrete DNA sequences under a time-dependent composite vector field that fuses normalized functional utility, bidirectional contextual prior guidance, and compositional quality penalties, followed by feasibility-first trajectory readout.
items.author: Wang, J., Xu, T., Tan, C. et al.

items.title: A structural grammar of truncation across the human homodimer landscape
items.summary: Alternative splicing and proteolytic truncation generate tens of thousands of protein isoforms in the human proteome. Their consequences for quaternary state, the level at which most protein function operates, have been examined largely one molecule at a time. Using the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database expansion to predicted human homodimers, we compared 5,168 canonical-versus-truncated pairs on four interface metrics distributed with that release. Truncation partitions high-confidence canonical homodimers into structural conservation (56.4% of pairs), complete interface ablation (26.1%) and partial destabilization (17.5%). The partition holds on predicted interface size and not only on interface confidence. Conservation events retain a median 0.938 of the canonical interface residues, destabilization events 0.622, and ablation events 0.000.
items.author: Karagöl, T., Karagöl, A.

items.title: Bounded by compartment, composition and time: efferocytic transcriptional readouts after ischaemic stroke
items.summary: After ischaemic stroke, efferocytosis is usually inferred from a single bulk-tissue transcript score. Such a score cannot distinguish more phagocytes from more active ones, nor separate clearance from the inflammatory output that follows. We scored apoptotic demand (DEMAND), clearance machinery (CAPACITY), immunogenic output (OUTCOME) and an inhibitory brake separately across 38 datasets (30 numeric) spanning brain, blood and sorted human parenchyma, rating a program only where 75% of its genes were detected. Each difference was compared with expression-matched random gene sets, checked against leukocyte composition, and reported against the smallest difference its design could resolve. Energy supply and demand were scored on the same scale.
items.author: Ding, S., Liu, Y., Zeng, Y. et al.

items.title: How brain operation emerges from its nested recurrent circuitry extending into the body
items.summary: Behavior and thoughts are dynamic processes driven by activity in a multitude of internal and external nested neuronal circuitry loops. This causes an unexplained complexity in neuron population dynamics. Pursuing an atomic principle of how brain operation emerges from these nested closed loops, here we show that the activity state space travel of a neuron population can be understood as a consequence of a vector field with an attractor point, which emerges from the intrinsic neuronal properties and the synaptic connections between them. Neuronal activity in the brain in vivo, however, indicates that attractor point continually moves along trajectories, which we show requires dynamic input from sensors and input-independent activity generation in neurons.
items.author: Szeier, S., Jorntell, H.

items.title: Antibiotic effects on gut-derived short chain fatty acid pools in healthy volunteers.
items.summary: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are vital microbial metabolites that maintain gut health and immune function. Despite the established deleterious effect of antibiotics on anaerobic bacteria in the gut, the longitudinal effects of antibiotics on SCFA pool dynamics remain poorly characterized in humans.
items.author: Shremo Msdi A, Ayele H, Begum K, Hu C, Jo J, Alam MJ, Eubank T, Lu X, Haidacher SJ, Horvath TD, Hanson BM, Garey KW.

items.title: A two-dimensional party-position panel from text and expert data.
items.summary: This Data Descriptor releases an election-year panel of economic left-right and cultural cosmopolitan-traditionalist party positions for 708 parties in 65 countries from 1944 to 2025. The panel supports comparative analyses connecting party-level ideological supply to elections, regions, voters, institutions, or political economy over long periods.
items.author: Seimel A.

items.title: Current Challenges and Opportunities in Contemporary Urology Residency Program Coordination.
items.summary: Purpose of review Urology program coordinators manage all administrative aspects of their training programs and have become essential members of the education leadership team. This review aims to evaluate the current literature regarding the opportunities and challenges encountered by program coordinators today.
items.author: Mussehl DA, Couzo TA, DeSaulniers C, Hamilton L, Jung K, Knight W, Neimann N, Serrano M.

items.title: Research progress and clinical prospects of sonodynamic therapy in cancer treatment.
items.summary: Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) uses ultrasound and a sensitizer to generate cytotoxic chemistry at depths inaccessible to most light-based treatments. Nanomaterial studies have broadened this idea from local reactive oxygen species (ROS) production to delivery, microenvironment remodeling, and immune priming, while published human studies remain small.
items.author: Zhang W, Gao H, Sun S, Gao Y, Zhou Y, Zhang D, Zhang C.

items.title: Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design.
items.summary: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy for eliminating disease-associated proteins, including targets that remain challenging to modulate using conventional occupancy-driven inhibitors. Among TPD approaches, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) exploit the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) to induce selective and event-driven degradation of proteins of interest (POIs).
items.author: Pandiyan S, Bhol CS, Wang L, Sethi G.

items.title: From isolated component failure to coupled degradation networks in proton exchange membrane fuel cells.
items.summary: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are among the most promising energy conversion technologies for achieving sustainable and carbon-neutral energy systems. Despite remarkable advances in catalyst and membrane materials, the limited durability of membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) remains a major barrier to large-scale commercialization.
items.author: Habib MA, Park J, Kim H, Jung J, Kim S, Cha DC, Yeo YS, Jeong J, Kim TH, Choi MC, Leem G, Lee JH, Yang WS, Lee S.

items.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals the Macroscale Signatures of Cortical Cell Types on Anatomic Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
items.summary: ​Esta​blishing how intensity in magnetic resonance images (MRIs) covaries with molecular factors can help to derive quasi-mechanistic biological insights from neuroimaging. Gray/white matter contrast (GWC) of [Formula: see text]-weighted MRI is an abundantly available phenotype often used to investigate aging and cognition.
items.author: Chowdhury NF, Jafar T, Irimia A.

items.title: Immunoblot analysis as a helpful adjunct to determine the time of a CMV infection in pregnancy.
items.summary: Aim To evaluate the utility of immunoblot analysis for determining the timing of maternal CMV infection in pregnancy. Methods Retrospective study including 151 pregnant women referred for suspected primary CMV infection or unclear serological results at the University Hospital Tübingen between July 2023 and November 2025.
items.author: Bissinger AL, Schmid L, Hoopmann M, Enders M, Kagan KO.

items.title: Treatment Simplification for People with HIV and Limited Treatment Options: Oral and Long-Acting Approaches.
items.summary: Purpose of review To examine clinical complexities and emerging therapeutic strategies for people with HIV on complex multi-tablet regimens or with limited treatment options. Recent findings While single-tablet regimens standardise modern care, 3-10% of individuals face multi-class resistance and complex regimens and have increased risk of potential complications.
items.author: Mercer O, Orkin C, Ring K.

items.title: Marine Streptomyces biomass as a novel functional feed additive for improving the health and growth of European seabass.
items.summary: This study investigated the production of marine-derived Streptomyces griseus and Streptomyces mutabilis using seawater-based media and evaluated their efficacy as functional feed additives for European seabass (Dicentrarchus labrax). Under optimized starch nitrate seawater conditions, S. griseus and S. mutabilis produced high biomass yields (24.8 g/L and 23.9 g/L, respectively).
items.author: Ehab MM, Hegazy GE, El-Sayed HS, Saleh NE, Hamed MM, Youssif AM, Ghozlan HA.

items.title: Efficacy and mechanisms of supplementary motor area rTMS for freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease: a randomized sham-controlled trial.
items.summary: Objectives To evaluate the efficacy and neural mechanisms of 10‑Hz repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the supplementary motor area (SMA) for freezing of gait (FOG) in Parkinson's disease (PD) assessed OFF medication. Methods In this randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial, 52 PD patients with FOG were randomized (1:1) to receive 12 sessions of 10-Hz SMA-rTMS (n = 26) or sham (n = 26) over 4 weeks. A total of 50 patients (26 rTMS, 24 sham) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The primary outcome was the change in the New Freezing of Gait Questionnaire (NFOG-Q) score from baseline to post-intervention (T1).
items.author: Liu C, Li G, Hou M, Song L, Wan Y, Wu N, Zhang Y, Qi C, Zhao J, Li J, Liu Z, Gan J.

items.title: Surveillance strategies for the early detection of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors in neurofibromatosis type 1: a systematic review.
items.summary: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) is the leading cause of cancer-related death in neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), with a lifetime risk of 8-15% and five-year survival below 50% in most series. Imaging surveillance, most often whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI), is offered on the premise that earlier detection of premalignant or early malignant lesions permits curative resection, but the supporting evidence has not been formally synthesized. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, trial registries, and conference proceedings from 2000 to July 2026 for studies of structured surveillance or lesion characterization in people with NF1.
items.author: Damodharan S, Tonsgard J.

items.title: Women's experiences of gynaecological surveillance in Lynch syndrome.
items.summary: Gynaecological surveillance is offered in Lynch syndrome despite limited evidence for its clinical effectiveness. Invasive gynaecological investigations often cause pain and distress, but experiences vary and little is known about the psychological burden of repeated testing. We evaluated the lived experiences of annual gynaecological surveillance in women with and at risk of Lynch syndrome. Recruitment occurred via hospital clinics, social media, and Lynch Syndrome UK. Participants completed a semi-structured questionnaire by telephone. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively. Free-text responses were recorded verbatim, coded inductively and grouped thematically, with outputs reviewed by a second researcher. Overall, 104 women participated: 93 had confirmed Lynch syndrome and 11 had a strong family history of Lynch syndrome cancers (median age: 41 years).
items.author: Johnson JE, Dore M, Saso S, Balega J, Duncan T, Smith T, Monahan KJ, Davidson EJ.

items.title: Beyond survival: early effects of meningioma resection on health-related quality of life and neurofunctional recovery.
items.summary: Background WHO grade I meningiomas rank among the most common primary intracranial tumor entities. Although surgery often achieves favorable tumor control, postoperative recovery may involve impairments in everyday functioning, cognition, functional independence and patient-reported Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL). This study evaluated short-term outcomes after WHO grade I meningioma resection across global functioning status, neuropsychology and cognitive performance, motor function, and HRQoL within three months after surgery. Methods This prospective exploratory longitudinal single-center cohort study included 23 patients undergoing WHO grade I meningioma resection at the Department of Neurosurgery, Bayreuth Hospital, Bayreuth, Germany. Patients were assessed preoperatively, shortly before postoperative discharge, and at three-month follow-up using a standardized multidimensional test battery.
items.author: Maier N, Kleemann B, Schneider KI, Stark F, Khafaji F, Reyes-Medina B, Saffour S, Monfroy N, Linsler S, Sippl C.

items.title: A qualitative exploration of the psychosocial and financial outcomes for cancer survivors with ostomies.
items.summary: Purpose Rural cancer survivors with ostomies face multiple healthcare utilization issues including cost. The purpose of this study was to identify ostomy-related modifiable factors that are expected to impact the total cost of care. Methods Cancer survivors with ostomies were identified in three geographically diverse areas (Southern California, North Dakota, Pennsylvania). Individual open-ended, semi-structured interviews were conducted to elicit participant descriptions of the explicit and implicit costs of ostomy management. Results Eleven of 24 participants described explicit financial burden from their ostomy. Additional costs that were inferred included unreimbursed ostomy supplies, waste due to trial and error, new clothing due to ostomy placement, travel for treatment, and co-pays.
items.author: Barg FK, Sun V, Sticca R, Hoffman RL, Maeng D, Bilger A, Grant M, Krouse RS.

items.title: Competing routes back to firing shape population hyperexcitability and its selective suppression
items.summary: Even within the same neuron, successive spikes can follow distinct trajectories, with afterdepolarization permitting early return to firing and depolarization block prolonging inactivity. Therefore, we propose that hyperexcitability involves changes in the opportunities to fire again from different points across the spike cycle, and not just from quiescence. The hazard of firing - the instantaneous propensity to fire again with time elapsed after a spike - isolates these opportunities. In bursting dopamine neurons, the hazard rises early due to burst-sustaining spikes, falls, then rises again due to burst-initiating spikes. Within a renewal framework, we represent each rise as a competing pathway back to firing and show that recruitment from quiescence and firing again before full recovery provide independent control over population activity.
items.author: Kamaraj, A. K., Szuromi, M. P.

items.title: Super-resolved mass photometry reveals the dissociation pathways of individual protein complexes
items.summary: Mass photometry (MP) measures the mass of single unlabelled molecules as they adsorb to a glass surface, but conventional analysis captures each molecule only momentarily, as it binds, and neglects its subsequent fate. Here we correct for coverslip drift and use mass-dependent localisation precision to link successive events at one site to a single molecule and enables two workflows for studying protein assemblies. In tandem MP, matching each binding event with its outcomes yields a two-dimensional precursor-product spectrum that separates dissociation from unbinding, providing structural insights into the protein assemblies and the kinetics of subunit loss. By comparing citrate synthase homologues, we reveal distinct fingerprints and disassembly pathways among complexes of the same oligomeric state.
items.author: O'Shea, A. R., Bishop, J. L., Sendker, F. L. et al.

items.title: IL-15 superagonist induces robust STAT5 phosphorylation to support the differentiation and survival of tumor-relevant memory precursor effector-like CD8 T cells, enhancing long-term antitumor protection
items.summary: The tumor-draining lymph node (tdLN) serves as a critical reservoir of tumor-reactive T cells, yet its contribution to preventing metastatic recurrence remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate CD8 T cell clonal dynamics and memory responses induced by neoadjuvant anti PD-1 therapy. We demonstrate that PD-1 blockade promotes the emergence of protective CD8 T cell memory, enriched with tumor-relevant clones that persist in the lymph nodes of long-term survivors. Furthermore, we show that combination of a neoadjuvant IL-15 superagonist with PD-1 blockade significantly increases clonal diversity, cytotoxicity, and clonal persistence in non-draining lymph nodes. These changes result in enhanced systemic antitumor immunity and durable memory that prevents tumor relapse.
items.author: Cruz, T. D., Honigsberg, R., Markowitz, G. J. et al.

items.title: Revisiting Hydractiniidae (Hydrozoa): Mitogenomic Insights into the Diversity, Systematics and Life-Cycle Evolution of North Atlantic and Arctic Species
items.summary: Hydractiniidae is a diverse family of colonial hydrozoans exhibiting substantial morphological variation and a wide range of life-cycle strategies, including species with and without a medusa stage. Several species are established model organisms, yet fundamental gaps in current knowledge on hydractiniid biosystematics hinder comparative studies of reproductive and developmental traits and our understanding of their true distributions. Here, we employ an integrative approach combining detailed morphological assessments with DNA barcoding and complete mitochondrial genomes to reassess species diversity and distribution, phylogenetic relationships, and life-cycle variation in Hydractiniidae. Our results confirm 10 species are present in the North Atlantic and Arctic Ocean, occurring from shallow waters to 2600 m depth and from coastal fjords to deep-sea hydrothermal vents.
items.author: Beckmann, L. M., Hosia, A., Ronowicz, M. et al.

items.title: Homologs of the Major Vault Protein defend bacteria against ribotoxins
items.summary: Bacteria use sophisticated mechanisms to defend themselves against antibiotics and bacteriophages, yet how they combat toxins deployed during interbacterial competition remains poorly understood. Bacteria use type VI secretion, bacteriocins, and contact dependent inhibition systems to deliver antibacterial toxins that inhibit growth by antagonizing essential processes. Here, we discover that Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses homologs of the eukaryotic major vault protein and a tRNA-like noncoding RNA to defend against RNA-damaging ribotoxins. Using an engineered pyocin delivery system, we showed that P. aeruginosa sensed ribotoxin damage and activated transcription of an RNA repair operon, which included band7, a homolog of the major vault protein.
items.author: Bullen, N. P., Holiday, L. C., Nagy, T. A. et al.

items.title: Defining the molecular interaction between influenza hemagglutinin and MHC-II
items.summary: The hemagglutinin (HA) of some influenza viruses can bind MHC-II, but how these proteins interact is unclear. Here we demonstrate that diverse H5 HAs can use avian or human MHC-II to enter cells. We define the molecular interface by using pseudovirus deep mutational scanning to measure how mutations to both H5 HA and an avian MHC-II affect the interaction between the two proteins. We leverage identification of mutations to HA and MHC-II that increase their binding to each other to determine a 3.4-angstrom cryo-EM structure of the complex. The structure shows that HA binds to MHC-II using a surface on the globular head distinct from the sialic acid receptor-binding pocket.
items.author: Dadonaite, B., Dosey, A., Ahn, J. J. et al.

items.title: Detecting behavioural oscillations with increased sensitivity: A modification of Brookshire's (2022) AR-surrogate method
items.summary: A core challenge of cognitive neuroscience is to understand how cognition changes over time within individuals. For example, the tendency for behavioural responses to oscillate over time has been documented extensively in a range of cognitive domains. Recently, however, the phenomenon of behavioural oscillations has been called into question by indications that past findings might reflect aperiodic temporal structure rather than true oscillations. Brookshire (2022) proposed methods to control for aperiodic temporal structure while examining oscillations in behavioural time-courses and found no evidence of behavioural oscillations in reanalyses of four published datasets. However, Brookshire's (2022) method has been criticised for having low sensitivity to detect effects of realistic magnitude, so it is currently unclear whether these findings suggest that behavioural oscillations are not present in these and perhaps many other datasets, or whether they are false negatives.
items.author: Harris, A. M., Beale, H. A.

items.title: Unexpected Long Range Actions of AAV8
items.summary: Adeno-associated virus vectors (AAVs) have broad utility in neuroscience. A variety of features, such as titer, capsid, enhancers and promoters, coding and non-coding elements, can be utilized to pursue diverse experimental ends. The net effects of titer and capsid have been used experimentally to pursue retrograde and anterograde studies, such as through the monosynaptic spread of high-titer AAV1. The literature on AAV8 is conflicting, with evidence for and against its long-range action outside of the infected starter population. Using the mouse corticopontocerebellar tract, we report that AAV8, when used at high titers, can be associated with long range recombination outside of the starter population.
items.author: Lahr, J. M., Ly, J., Erdem, E. et al.

items.title: Single-base 5mC and 5hmC profiling identifies a dynamic 5hmC-to-5mC transition at gene bodies and transcription end sites during neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells.
items.summary: 5-methylcytosine (5mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) are genome-wide epigenetic modifications involved in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation. Although Enzymatic Methyl-seq (EM-seq) can enable the combined profiling of 5mC and 5hmC, Enzymatic 5hmC-seq (E5hmC-seq) can provide selective profiling of 5hmC at single-base resolution. In this context, we systematically validated E5hmC-seq using diverse genomic DNA samples. Next, we integrated E5hmC-seq with EM-seq to distinguish between 5mC and 5hmC landscapes during neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we observed dynamic remodeling of both modifications throughout differentiation, with pronounced changes during the transition from embryoid bodies (EBs) to neural progenitor cells (NPCs), characterized by a global decrease in 5hmC accompanied by an increase in 5mC.
items.author: Evanich, D. J., Blum, L. N., Sen, S. et al.

items.title: Distinct innate immune states associate with divergent serological outcomes after syphilis treatment
items.summary: The global resurgence of syphilis poses a major public health challenge, even in the era of effective antibiotic therapy. Following treatment, some patients achieve seroreversion, whereas others remain serofast with persistent nontreponemal antibody reactivity. Although nontreponemal antibody titers guide clinical follow-up, it remains unclear how closely they reflect the resolution of inflammation and recovery of immune function. We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, immunophenotyping in clinical samples, and functional assays to characterize circulating monocytes and natural killer (NK) cells across seroreversion and low- and high-titer serofast states, and further examined the impact of HIV coinfection. CD14+ monocytes retained inflammatory and CD163-associated scavenging programs after seroreversion, whereas serofast patients showed additional IFN-STAT1 activation in this subset.
items.author: Wei, Q., Jin, Y., Zhang, Y. et al.

items.title: Chemolithoautotrophic acidophile phenotyping by measuring metabolic byproduct formation in microplates
items.summary: Chemolithoautotrophic acidophiles can support several low-pH biotechnologies, but their phenotyping remains limited by throughput and inconsistent methods. This study used an assay to monitor metabolic byproduct formation using absorbance indicators in static, oxic cultures in 96-well microplates. In abiotic experiments, ferric iron and/or pH measurements from 51 microplates containing simulant solutions span total iron concentrations of 0-1 M, pH 0.3-7.0, and incubation temperatures of 4-75 {degrees}C. Of these, 30 microplates tested different UV-transparency and gas-permeable membrane configurations. Another 12 microplates tested indicator compatibility with growth media containing ferrous iron and (in)soluble sulfur substrates. Biological experiments measured 438 microplates containing Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans ATCC 23270, Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans ATCC 19377, or Leptospirillum ferriphilum DSM 14647 with chemical additives across 1,400 concentration conditions, yielding 142,038 time-course points, including abiotic controls.
items.author: Dailey, D. A., Herishko, M. A., Wang, W. et al.

items.title: Minimal eukaryotic DNA polymerase zeta/Rev1 GC-pair mutasome
items.summary: In eukaryotes, translesion DNA synthesis (TLS) enables replication across DNA lesions, difficult DNA structures, and during replicative stress. While TLS prevents replication fork collapse, it is inherently mutagenic and requires tight regulation to prevent global mutation rates increase. Here, we show that elevated DNA polymerase pol {zeta}/Rev1 promotes spontaneous mutagenesis during replication. The five subunits of pol zeta complex (pol zeta5) are the catalytic subunit Rev3, the TLS polymerase Rev1, a dimer of accessory protein Rev7, the Pol31 and Pol32 subunits shared with replicative pol delta. Pol31 and Pol32 bind the Fe-S-containing C-terminal domain (CTD) of Rev3, which serves as a major assembly hub.
items.author: McNellis, C. T., Brown, M., Panteleev, D. D. et al.

items.title: Structural correlates of disease-associated CTSC variants in Papillon-Lefevre syndrome
items.summary: Objective: To quantify structural features of disease-associated CTSC missense substitutions and evaluate a structural rule for research prioritization in Papillon-Lefevre syndrome. Design: We compared 16 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic missense substitutions with 234 recurrent gnomAD substitutions in the mature cathepsin C structure (PDB 1K3B). An expanded exploratory analysis included 35 further literature-indexed substitutions. We audited the documentation used to date the historical holdout and compared AlphaGenome splice scores with a consequence-only baseline. Results: Median predicted destabilization was 2.209 versus 0.763 kcal/mol (AUC 0.764, 95% CI 0.612-0.897). Catalytic proximity was observed in 4/16 versus 9/234. The expanded comparison gave AUC 0.740.
items.author: VONO, F. M., Naufel, A., Santos, V.

items.title: Interspecies differences in lamina cribrosa fiber composition and architecture might arise from differences in optic nerve head size and mechanical constraints
items.summary: The lamina cribrosa (LC) is a complex network of fibers that plays an important mechanical role in protecting optic nerve axons as they exit the eye. Both the architecture and composition of the LC network varies throughout animal species. However, the function of these differences between species is unknown. We hypothesize that this variety in LC architecture and composition is a result of species-specific adaptations to the mechanical constraints present in each species' optic nerve head. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel optimization framework to systematically derive optimal LC fiber architecture and composition under different mechanical constraints. We then compared predicted LC architectures to instant polarized light microscopy images of actual human, tree shrew, monkey, cow, pig, and rat LCs.
items.author: Galloy, A. E., He, X., Sigal, I. A.

items.title: Nuclear quantum effects on ion permeation through the open transient receptor potential melastatin 7 pore: A continuum-electrostatics estimate
items.summary: We estimate how nuclear delocalization affects magnesium and calcium release from occupied wells in the naltriben-open pore of transient receptor potential melastatin 7 (TRPM7). We compare the equilibrium distributions of sodium, magnesium, and calcium in the same open structure and fixed continuum field. Thermal quantum states extend over nearby positions, so the ion can sample more than one local environment. For the divalent ions, the model combines a Gaussian test charge in the nonlinear Poisson--Boltzmann potential, spatial dielectric self-energy, and the free-energy cost of restricting a correlated first hydration shell. The hydration shell comprises the water molecules that directly coordinate the ion.
items.author: Li, Y., Lin, H.-H.

items.title: Beta-Myosin inhibition in skeletal muscle: Impact of Mavacamten on the diaphragm
items.summary: The diaphragm, a primary respiratory muscle, contains nearly equal proportions of slow, Type-1 and fast, Type-II muscle fibers. Muscle fiber types - classified based on their shortening velocities and force generation abilities - are largely determined by distinct myosin II isoforms. Mavacamten (MAVA), a small molecule inhibitor of beta-cardiac myosin ATPase, is currently used for the treatment of obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HOCM). Notably, beta-myosin heavy chain (beta-MyHC) is not restricted to the ventricular myocardium but is also expressed in slow fibers, raising concerns about off-target effects of therapy used to treat cardiomyopathic conditions. Given that nearly 50 % of the fibers express beta-MyHC in the diaphragm, we hypothesize that Mava may affect diaphragm muscle activity.
items.author: Sarfraz, A., Nayak, A., Holler, T. et al.

items.title: Deciphering the role of adenosine-related genes in regulating smooth muscle cell phenotypic switch in coronary heart disease via single-cell RNA sequencing
items.summary: Background: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is closely associated with dysregulated lipid metabolism, inflammation, and impaired adenosine signaling. However, the contribution of adenosine-related genes (ARGs) and their relationship with the immune microenvironment remain unclear. Methods: Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated with curated ARGs. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified candidate genes, and XGBoost, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination, and Boruta were used to select diagnostic features. Gene set enrichment, immune infiltration, regulatory-network, and single-cell RNA-sequencing analyses were performed, followed by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction validation. Results: We identified 4,884 differentially expressed genes and 243 ARG-associated module genes, yielding 231 candidate genes.
items.author: cao, k. k., Su, K., Wang, R. et al.

items.title: Training background shapes the exercise-induced extracellular vesicle proteome to acute exercise with partial overlap with cold exposure in humans
items.summary: Aim: Exercise and cold exposure changes circulating extracellular vesicle (EV) and modifies their molecular cargo. However, it remains unclear whether the acute exercise-induced EV proteome response is uniform or shaped by long-term training background, and to what extent it overlaps with the response to cold exposure. We therefore performed an exploratory proteomics study in humans with distinct training phenotypes and compared exercise-induced protein changes with an independent cold exposure dataset. Methods: Serum samples were collected before and immediately after a maximal bicycle ramp test from untrained sedentary controls, endurance-trained athletes, natural bodybuilders, and sprinters. For cold exposure studies, serum samples were collected before, immediately after, and 30 minutes after an ice bath (8-12 degree Celsius) for 5 minutes.
items.author: Tischer, D., Braunsperger, A., Schranner, D. et al.

items.title: Dual mRNA delivery corrects physical and biochemical deficits in a mouse model of hepatic onset trifunctional protein deficiency
items.summary: Mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency (TFP-D) is a rare, life threatening long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorder caused by variants in either the HADHA or HADHB subunits, leading to toxic metabolite accumulation and systemic energy deficiency. Current dietary management strategies are only partially effective and fail to prevent long term morbidity and mortality. Here, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) mediated mRNA replacement strategy to restore TFP function in a moderate severity TFP-D mouse model by delivering both Hadha and Hadhb mRNA. In cultured TFP-D mouse fibroblasts, dual mRNA delivery, but not single subunit replacement, rescued long-chain fatty acid oxidation and revealed a dominant negative effect exerted by the endogenous M404K variant Hadhb.
items.author: von Beck, T., Terranova, T., Marayati, B. F. et al.

items.title: MicroBioAgent: an AI agent for automated microbiome analysis
items.summary: Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption.
items.author: Li, Z., WANG, J., Wang, C. et al.

items.title: RADSuite: Improving Species-Level Identification in Microbiome Research
items.summary: In the last twenty years, the microbiome has become a central focus of biomedical research, with amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene considered the industry standard for taxon identification of prokaryotes due to its cost-effectiveness. However, common target regions in 16S amplicons often do not uniquely distinguish closely related species, restricting many analyses to the genus level. Additionally, curated databases such as NCBI's 16S curated database often do not contain all intragenomic variants of the 16S gene and lack annotation of the 16S genomic composition and gene structure. To address these limitations, our team created RADSuite, a collection of tools which includes a more robust database of 16S gene copies (RADlib), an application that identifies which V regions will allow for species level identification (RADx), and a step-by-step guide for how to integrate RADlib within existing metagenomic profiling software tools.
items.author: Christensen, R. N., Gilliland, M., Young, J. et al.

items.title: Macrophage signaling history constrains subsequent transcriptional responses to cytokine stimulation
items.summary: Macrophages perform a wide array of distinct and crucial functions, and therefore tightly regulate their responses to external stimuli. These cells must integrate sequential signals over time to mount an appropriate response to their immunological niche. How prior cytokine stimulation shares macrophage responses to a subsequent stimulus remains poorly understood, yet has important implications for pathogen clearance as well as tissue repair and homeostasis. Here, we systematically characterize transcriptional responses to sequential cytokine stimulation in primary human macrophages, as well as demonstrate the effect of interactions with bacterial pathogens on macrophage transcriptional responses and plasticity. We find that prior stimulation history constrains subsequent transcriptional responses in a stimulus-specific and asymmetric manner.
items.author: Hochfelder, J. B., McGinn, R. A., Gunnarsson, C. et al.

items.title: Astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D regulates hippocampal memory through extracellular matrix remodeling
items.summary: Astrocytes contribute to hippocampal cognitive functions, but how astrocyte-derived factors regulate memory formation remains unclear. Here, we identify astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D (CtsD) as a regulator of hippocampal learning and memory. Proteomic profiling of hippocampal astrocytes upon learning identified candidates predicted to be secreted, among which we focused on CtsD, whose extracellular brain functions are unknown. Neutralizing extracellular CtsD or astrocyte-selective CtsD knockdown (aCtsD-KD) impaired hippocampal long term potentiation (LTP) and memory acquisition, suggesting an extracellular role for astrocytic CtsD. In aCtsD-KD mice, these deficits were accompanied by alterations in excitatory transmission and synaptic structures. aCtsD-KD also caused abnormal extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, and its partial digestion by chondroitinase ABC rescued the memory deficit, indicating that astrocytic CtsD-dependent ECM degradation contributes to hippocampal memory.
items.author: Kim, H., Cha, S., Ji, M. et al.

items.title: M 4.9 - 113 km ESE of Pangai, Tonga
items.summary: A magnitude 4.9 earthquake was recorded 113 km ESE of Pangai, Tonga. The event happened on 20 November 2026 at 22:34 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Ohmic warm inflation
items.summary: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential.
items.author: Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia

items.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
items.summary: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile.
items.author: Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto Sánchez Vargas

items.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
items.summary: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ \lesssim_α ν^{1/α} \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$.
items.author: Artin Tajdini, Jasper C. H. Lee, Jonathan Scarlett et al.

items.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
items.summary: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.
items.author: Debarghya Chakraborty, Dario Rosa

items.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
items.summary: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each.
items.author: Hari Sitaula, Joseph Opitz

items.title: Nonperturbative Bounds on the Ground-State Energy of Lattice QED
items.summary: We establish nonperturbative bounds on the ground-state energy of lattice quantum electrodynamics with naive fermions in Coulomb gauge, within the Gaussian photon approximation. Our central result is a spectral comparison theorem showing that, in the thermodynamic limit, the minimum fermionic energy density over all link configurations coincides with that of the trivial gauge configuration. The proof exploits a logarithmic determinant representation and dimensional reduction, without relying on reflection positivity, and applies to lattices of either parity. Combining this result with the positivity of the electromagnetic and Coulomb Hamiltonians, we derive an explicit lower bound on the interacting ground-state energy. Finite-lattice counterexamples show that the thermodynamic limit is essential.
items.author: Paweł Zin, Andrzej Veitia

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems.
items.author: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco et al.

items.title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design
items.summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction.
items.author: Haoyang Wang, Weibo Gao, Zhengxiong Li et al.

items.title: Non-penetrating World Models
items.summary: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not.
items.author: Yuhang Dai, Yinwei Wu, Ziyue Lin et al.

items.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
items.summary: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run.
items.author: Kaden Zheng, Pratyusha Sharma

items.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO. The method constructs a compact coreset that preserves the relative ranking of hyperparameter configurations observed on the full training data. Coreset selection is formulated as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based configuration rankings while penalizing subset size. The selected coreset is then used for HPO with three evolutionary algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Cross-generational elitist Selection, Heterogeneous Recombination and Cataclysmic Mutation (CHC), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO).
items.author: Mamoona Tasadduq, Maryam Bashir

items.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
items.summary: Neuromorphic sensing and computing offer a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines for mobile robots, where perception must run continuously under tight latency and energy constraints. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored. In this technical report, a four-wheel rover platform is presented that combines three real-time perception pipelines: a classical audio tagging pipeline based on Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANNs) running on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU, a neuromorphic audio pipeline in which a spiking neural network (SNN) is deployed on the SynSense Xylo Audio~2 chip, and a neuromorphic vision pipeline in which events from an event-based camera are processed by the SpikeYOLO spiking detector for traffic cone detection.
items.author: Guillem Fustier-Castillo, Ruben Ribes-Serrano, Javier Naranjo-Alcazar et al.

items.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
items.summary: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling.
