Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage.
items.author: Dylan Forde

items.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
items.summary: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1,\star\}^{\mathcal X}$ be a partial concept class of finite VC dimension $d$. We construct a deterministic agnostic PAC learner that, for every $\varepsilon,δ\in(0,1)$, uses $O((d+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ i.i.d. examples from an arbitrary distribution $\mathcal D$ over $\mathcal X\times\{-1,+1\}$ and returns a total concept $\hat h:\mathcal X\to\{-1,+1\}$ satisfying $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(\hat h)\leq \min_{h\in\mathcal H}\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)+\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)=\mathbb P_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal D}[h(x)\neq y]$. This establishes the optimal sample complexity, matching the lower bound of Alon et al. (FOCS 2021).
items.author: Liang-Yu Zou

items.title: Probing CP violation in weak radiative and dielectron decays of $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ hyperons
items.summary: The rare decays $Λ\to ne^+e^-$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-e^+e^-$ can serve as sensitive probes of $CP$ violation, especially that induced by interactions from beyond the standard model. We demonstrate that this is so because the dominant long-distance components of these processes provide sizable absorptive phases that can give rise to significant $CP$ violation via interference with potential new-physics effects. Treating the new contributions model-independently, we find that this leads to $CP$-odd rate asymmetries that are currently allowed by kaon and hyperon data to reach the 10% and 20% levels in the $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ cases, respectively. Interestingly, we obtain comparable outcomes for the related weak radiative modes $Λ\to nγ$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-γ$.
items.author: Xiao-Gang He, Jusak Tandean, German Valencia

items.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
items.summary: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity.
items.author: David Rosser

items.title: What Must a Model Tell a Planner? Outcome Interfaces for Risk-Aware Planning After Robot Damage
items.summary: When a robot is damaged, it must decide which routes it can still afford, and the amount of risk it may accept can change from one mission to the next. We argue that whether a learned model helps such a robot depends on its decision interface, that is, on what the model hands to the planner. A decision policy tells the planner what to do, whereas an outcome model, a kind of world model, predicts the consequences of each route. We study simulated Unitree Go2 quadrupeds and H1 humanoids with weakened motors, added payloads, or reduced foot friction. We compare four interfaces.
items.author: Hassan Iqbal, Krishna Kumar

items.title: Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing
items.summary: Autonomous racing requires an accurate vehicle dynamics model near the limits of handling, yet a mismatch between the nominal and actual dynamics inevitably remains. To reduce this mismatch, existing methods learn from on-track data, i.e., data collected while the vehicle drives on the track under racing conditions, by adapting the physical parameters of the nominal model or by learning a residual that captures the remaining mismatch. However, these on-track learning methods typically handle either the physical parameters or the residual separately, which restricts their ability to resolve the mismatch. To address this limitation, we propose an interactive semi-parametric learning framework that learns both the physical parameters and the residual under a single shared prediction-error objective.
items.author: Jungbin Kim, Youngim Nam, Cheolhyeon Kwon

items.title: Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity
items.summary: Cluster schedulers already choose nodes, GPUs and accelerators for submitted workloads, enforce quotas and spread load. QPUs from several vendors are now schedulable resources in the same clusters, yet the user still names the device, usually the one with the best average fidelity. For a given circuit that choice is often wrong: compiling onto each device's qubit connectivity adds gates, so a job can meet its required success probability on one device and miss it on another with similar error rates, and checking this exactly by compiling for every candidate is too slow for a scheduling decision. We let the scheduler choose the QPU in two stages.
items.author: Ana Paula Appel

items.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
items.summary: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode enables prediction of megadalton complexes. Equilibrium distributions approximate MD references with free-energy errors near 1 kcal/mol across tested proteins and complexes.
items.author: Michael Gastegger, Adam E. Foster, José Jiménez-Luna et al.

items.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
items.summary: Reward-independent representations enable reinforcement learning agents to reuse knowledge across tasks, but limited representation capacity raises three fundamental questions: what statistical dependence should these representations capture, which components of that dependence should be retained for policy improvement, and how does discarding the remaining components affect decision-making? We address these questions through canonical dependence analysis. For a reference policy, we construct an action-centered, positive-lag canonical dependence matrix (CDM) that isolates the additional predictive contribution of the current action beyond the current state. Its singular value decomposition yields Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), paired features that recover delayed advantage through linear reward projections.
items.author: Huaze Tang, Runqing Miao, Tianren Peng et al.

items.title: M 5.1 - 32 km NE of Port-Olry, Vanuatu
items.summary: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake was recorded 32 km NE of Port-Olry, Vanuatu. The event happened on 20 November 2026 at 17:53 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 95 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations.
items.author: Chi Yan, Guoyang Zhao, Wentao Yuan et al.

items.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
items.summary: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law.
items.author: Aryan Gadhave, Asghar Ghorbanpour, Liam Hickey et al.

items.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
items.summary: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. Even when expert annotations exist, expert disagreement or structural delineation biases can yield split or merged reference instances, corresponding to over- or under-segmentation, respectively. Panoptic Quality (PQ) and related metrics capture both segmentation and detection quality while weighting all instances equally, regardless of size. Yet when the references are biased, these metrics can neither detect split or merged instances nor distinguish valid from invalid overor under-segmentation.
items.author: Erik Großkopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik Möller et al.

items.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
items.summary: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells.
items.author: JaeSeong Kim, KyungTae Lim

items.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
items.summary: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order $n$ could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order $n = 8$, and find both more efficient compositions and the first $8^{\textrm{th}}$ order general schemes.
items.author: Marko Maležič, Johann Ostmeyer

items.title: Thermo-electric Response Bound on Fluctuations in Coherent Transport
items.summary: We establish an accessible lower bound on current noise in coherent electron transport, expressed in terms of responses to reservoir temperatures and chemical potentials. Derived within the Floquet-Nambu scattering formalism using a Cramér-Rao-type inequality, it holds for arbitrary linear combinations of charge and heat currents in normal terminals, including those of hybrid superconducting systems, under static or periodic driving. The bound is tight in experimentally relevant regimes, notably in quantum point contacts with static or oscillating voltages and normal-superconductor junctions, often providing stronger constraints than thermodynamic uncertainty relations. It can be evaluated via experimentally accessible response coefficients, without inferring entropy production or dynamical activity, and provides useful constraints on the precision of nanoscale thermal and quantum devices.
items.author: Gianmichele Blasi, Rosa López, Mykhailo Moskalets et al.

items.title: Soft-photon resummation for low-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders
items.summary: We present resummed predictions for $e^+e^- \to μ^+μ^-(γ)$ and $π^+π^-(γ)$ in the multi-photon soft limit, matched to exact NLO. The resummation is performed within the Yennie-Frautschi-Suura framework at the amplitude level. The initial and final-state contributions are included coherently, and NLO accuracy with finite electron, muon and pion masses is achieved. We present our calculation, its implementation in a fast Fortran Monte Carlo integrator, and compare our predictions with the generators BabaYaga, KKMC, Phokhara and McMule, in scenarios inspired by the energy-scan (CMD) and radiative-return (KLOE, BES III, B factories) experiments. We find agreement with BabaYaga, which includes higher-order corrections through a parton shower, at the per-mille level in the cross-sections, and differences of up to two percent with the soft-photon resummation of KKMC.
items.author: Thomas Dave, Lois Flower, Jérémy Paltrinieri et al.

items.title: Quantum Dobrushin comparison and locality of fermionic equilibrium states
items.summary: We prove a quantum analogue of Dobrushin's comparison theorem for lattice fermions. As in the classical case, it is a tool for proving uniqueness of equilibrium states, decay of correlations, and stability of local expectations under distant perturbations. We apply it to fermions with weak many-body interactions added to a quadratic Hamiltonian, allowing pairing, spatial inhomogeneity and long-range interactions. If the quadratic Hamiltonian is gapped, there is a coupling strength below which the thermal equilibrium (KMS) state is unique at every positive temperature and its correlations decay uniformly in the temperature. Its local expectations converge to those of the unique gapped ground state exponentially fast in the inverse temperature.
items.author: Lennart Becker, Harman Preet Singh, Stefan Teufel

items.title: Linear Response Theory of Nitrogen K-Edge X-ray Absorption of TCNQ
items.summary: The linear response of the density is computed in the frequency domain within the generalized Kohn--Sham framework of adiabatic time-dependent density functional theory, employing hybrid exchange-correlation functionals. It is shown that the generalized Casida equations imply a Dyson-like equation for the linear-response of the full frequency-dependent one-electron reduced density matrix of the reference GKS system. We implement this formalism in the \textsc{Crystal} code and apply it to the nitrogen K-edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) of 7,7,8,8-tetracyano-$p$-quinodimethane (TCNQ), the acceptor in the charge-transfer salt TTF-TCNQ. We interpret the spectrum through a step-by-step construction by building blocks of increasing complexity.
items.author: Alberto Boccuni, Vita Ilakovac, Stéphane Carniato et al.

items.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
items.summary: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations.
items.author: Rak-Kyeong Seong

items.title: Humanoid robots for safety-critical electrical switching: A perception-informed runtime constraint filter
items.summary: Humanoid robots can reduce personnel exposure in electrical switching, but safe control is challenging because the tool must reach a target switch next to similar devices, where an imprecise operator command can contact a non-target switch. This study proposes a runtime safety filter that checks each operator command during virtual-reality teleoperation of a humanoid robot. The filter integrates a scene model estimated from the robot head camera and a target-conditioned control barrier function quadratic program that keeps the tool away from the non-target switch while passing safe commands unchanged. In real-world experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, with six rounds at each of two standing positions, target operations succeed in all ten rounds with an unchanged target and no non-target actuation.
items.author: Songyang Liu, Yu Hou, Yuqing Hu et al.

items.title: Prediction and characterisation of cation topology of pentanary high-entropy alloy (MoWNbTaV)S$_2$
items.summary: High-entropy transition-metal dichalcogenides offer properties tuned by composition, yet two basic questions remain open: which arrangement of the metals forms under synthesis conditions, and how it can be recognised in experiment. Density functional theory (DFT) cannot sample the vast space of possible arrangements, and the ground-state energies usually employed to screen them do not take into account the temperatures at which these materials are made. This work solves both issues for the pentanary (MoWNbTaV)S\textsubscript{2} monolayer with a Gaussian approximation potential trained on DFT data by iterative learning. Gibbs free energy calculations reveal that vibrational entropy reshapes the stability ranking, while five selected configurations retain their trigonal-prismatic framework during nanosecond molecular dynamics up to \qty{1300}{\kelvin}.
items.author: Shubham Agarwal, Tahir Wahab, Jesper Byggmästar et al.

items.title: Voltage-Controlled Dielectric Cavity Magnonics in Epitaxial Fe Films on SrTiO3 Single Crystal Substrates
items.summary: Cavity magnonics relies on the hybridization between collective spin excitations and well-defined photonic or mechanical cavity modes, enabling fast and efficient coupling of spintronic devices to microwave circuits and optical information carriers. In this work, we present a hybrid material heterostructure that combines an intrinsic dielectric microwave cavity with a ferromagnetic medium, establishing magnon-photon interaction with coupling rates in the order of 0.1-1 GHz. Demonstrating effective voltage-control of the hybrid mode spectrum at cryogenic temperatures, we achieve a highly tunable photo-magnonic material, that could provide significant advancements for high-performance and power-efficient cryogenic RF-applications, including hybrid quantum technology, superconducting electronics and nonlinear microwave devices for unconventional computation and signal processing.
items.author: Stijn Reniers, Ekaterina Gorokh, Lukas Nulens et al.

items.title: Heat cleaning kinetics and thermal degradation of MOCVD-grown GaAs photocathodes
items.summary: We evaluated metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaAs/GaAsP strained-superlattice photocathodes with integrated distributed Bragg reflectors in a low-voltage Mott polarimeter at Jefferson Lab. Without a protective arsenic cap, surface contamination can develop during transport and installation. Heat cleaning removes this contamination by thermally desorbing material bound to the surface, but excessive heating can also damage the photocathode. We modeled quantum efficiency (QE) in terms of surface contaminant coverage to describe its increase with heating time. QE rose more rapidly and reached a plateau nearly twice as high at $550^\circ\text{C}$ as at $450^\circ\text{C}$, while polarization remained near 83%. Further heating reduced QE and polarization.
items.author: Gregory Blume, Adam Masters, Colin Kirk et al.

items.title: BRINA: Bottom-Referenced Inertial Navigation with AKAZE, a Sonar SLAM for Autonomous Marine Vehicles
items.summary: Forward-looking sonar (FLS) provides reliable underwater perception where optical sensing is limited, but its use for navigation is hindered by the unobserved elevation of each return. As a result, motion estimated directly from sonar images suffers from an unknown metric scale that is commonly resolved using a Doppler velocity log (DVL). We present BRINA (Bottom-Referenced Inertial Navigation with AKAZE), a sonar-inertial SLAM system for marine vehicles that uses the FLS as its only exteroceptive sensor. BRINA estimates the sonar altitude from the first seabed return in each beam and uses it to project matched features onto the seabed, providing metric odometry without a DVL.
items.author: Adolfo Damiano Cafaro, Patrizio Mariani, Roberto Galeazzi

items.title: Generalist Action Critic: Harnessing Frontier Models in Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Frontier models have demonstrated remarkable general-purpose reasoning capabilities, opening new possibilities for intelligent decision making in the physical world. In autonomous driving, many recent approaches seek to leverage these capabilities through additional adaptation for action output, particularly in scenarios where existing models underperform. We introduce Generalist Action Critic (GAC), a zero-shot framework that combines frontier models' general-purpose reasoning with the planning competence of specialized driving models through an inference-time harness. In GAC, specialized planners generate multiple candidate trajectories and make an initial selection, while a frozen frontier model serves as an action critic that assesses the selected trajectory against scene evidence and either retains it or reselects from the available candidates.
items.author: Yun Yan, Shizhi Hu, Zhichao Li et al.

items.title: Quantifying the TKM-IKT ambiguity: translating the theoretical benchmark into experimental discriminants for future colliders
items.summary: This paper, the second of two companion works, translates the theoretical benchmark established in into quantitative predictions for high-energy $γγ$ interactions. We simultaneously confront the TKM and IKT dipole cross-section prescriptions across five representative saturation models (GBW, IIMS, rcBK, AGBS, WYKWC). Evaluating real and virtual cross sections, $F_2^γ$, and heavy-quark production, we demonstrate that the TKM--IKT discrepancy is an irreducible structural ambiguity reaching $48\pm12\%$ at LEP energies and expanding into the TeV regime. We propose three experimental discriminants for future colliders (ILC, CLIC, FCC-ee) --- emphasizing exclusive $γγ\to J/ψ+ J/ψ$ production where quadratic amplitude scaling ($[\mathcal{N}]^2$) magnifies the divergence --- elevating these comparisons from parameter choices to rigorous falsification tests of the foundational premises.
items.author: G. Zardo Becker, Benno Bodmann, César A. Zen Vasconcellos

items.title: Balancing heavy flavour: Quantum number compensation in the hadronisation of charm and beauty particles in proton-proton collisions
items.summary: The hadronisation of heavy quarks remains one of the least understood processes of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). While the production of heavy quark pairs can be calculated perturbatively in QCD, the subsequent formation of hadrons involves non-perturbative processes. The description of these processes is predominantly model dependent and sensitive to the underlying mechanisms of colour reconnection and string fragmentation. In particular, the conservation of flavour, baryon number and charge imposes constraints on how heavy-flavour hadrons are formed and balanced within the final state. In this work, we study how the quantum numbers associated with charm and beauty production are balanced in proton-proton collisions, using events simulated with the PYTHIA-8 event generator.
items.author: Iñaki Pardo Zambrana, Paul Veen, K. Keri Vos et al.

items.title: Shift current as a stacking spectroscopy of hexagonal boron nitride multilayers
items.summary: Out-of-plane polarization can be tuned by sliding polar monolayers in van der Waals materials; the bulk photovoltaic effect is emerging as a natural optical probe, provided the photocurrent tracks the polarization. We test that assumption by computing the polarization and the shift-current tensor from first principles across the stacking landscape of bi-, tri-, and tetralayer hexagonal boron nitride. The two quantities share one robust property: the vertical response reverses with the polarization while the in-plane one does not. Beyond this rule, the correspondence must be read with caution: stackings with identical polarization carry vertical monochromatic photocurrents of opposite sign; the spectra reorganize and even reverse sign at some photon energies along a constant-polarization plateau; and the strongest vertical peak of the entire pathway sits where the polarization crosses zero.
items.author: Sanber Vizcaya, Juan M. Florez, Eric Suárez Morell

items.title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
items.summary: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gaußian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand.
items.author: Kenji Fukushima, Friederike Ihssen, Renzo Kapust et al.

items.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
items.summary: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges, evaluating these integrals by residues determines the discrete closed-channel spectrum and yields expansions that agree with the analytic bootstrap predictions of Downing--Jacobsen--Nivesvivat--Ribault--Saleur.
items.author: Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu

items.title: General Transport Signatures of Odd-Parity Magnets: Charge--Spin Selection Rules and Temporal--Spectral Separation
items.summary: While even-parity altermagnets are known for spatially separating charge and spin currents via the crystal spin Hall effect, the defining transport counterpart for odd-parity magnets remains to be established. Here, we establish temporal and spectral charge--spin separation as a general transport signature across all spin-splitting classes of collinear and noncollinear odd-parity magnets with unitary spin-flip inversion $\mathcal U=[C_2^\perp\Vert P]$. This symmetry restricts charge responses to odd orders and $z$-polarized spin responses to even orders, independent of microscopic mechanism and without requiring spin conservation. For ac drives that reverse sign after half a period, charge and spin currents exhibit opposite half-period parities, and their spectra contain only odd charge and even spin harmonics.
items.author: Junxi Yu, Pu Zhang, Yichen Liu et al.

items.title: Atomistic theory of the $d$-wave phonon angular momentum splitter effect
items.summary: Phonons offer a bosonic route to angular-momentum transport in solids, but how their momentum-space textures manifest in transport remains unclear. Here we develop an atomistic theory of the phonon angular momentum splitter effect in an antiferromagnetic square lattice with checkerboard-modulated elastic couplings, analogous to the spin-splitter effect in $d$-wave altermagnets. We calculate the transport and accumulation of phonon angular momentum driven by a temperature gradient and find that the transverse response separates into Hall and $d_{xy}$-wave splitter contributions. The splitter contribution requires both the antiferromagnetic order and the checkerboard elastic modulation and exhibits a characteristic $d_{xy}$ angular dependence, whereas the Hall contribution is nearly isotropic.
items.author: Daniel A. Bustamante Lopez, Dominik M. Juraschek

items.title: Bulk Wilson Loops from $\mathscr{I}$
items.summary: A Carrollian description of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory on partially complexified future null infinity was recently proposed by Opreij, Skinner and Wang in arXiv:2604.09771. In this paper, we give a new form of the Carrollian Yang-Mills kinetic action on real future null infinity, and recover the logarithmic two-point function found by arXiv:2604.09771. We then extend the Carrollian description of Yang-Mills beyond scattering amplitudes by studying the expectation value of a null polygonal Wilson loop in Minkowski spacetime. We propose a boundary operator given by the trace of a cyclic product of holomorphic frames on the good cuts associated with the polygon's vertices.
items.author: James Drummond, Bruno Giménez Umbert, Prahar Mitra

items.title: Silver/alumina-capped Janus particles: a dispersible hyperbolic metamaterial
items.summary: Hyperbolic metamaterials (HMMs) made of alternating layers of metal and dielectric have been heralded as promising materials for super-resolution imaging and spontaneous emission enhancement sought after in biological applications. However, the practical utilization of HMMs has been limited, primarily by the solid and stiff nature of the underlying substrate, usually a silicon wafer or glass substrate. An ability to transfer HMMs to colloidal substrates would introduce dispersibility to HMMs and potentially enable their use in medical applications while extending the curved HMM geometry to discrete particles. Here, spherical particles with alternating metal and dielectric layers are used to fabricate hyperbolic metamaterial-capped Janus particles (HMMJPs).
items.author: Samhita Kattekola, Raymond R. Dagastine, Alexander Couzis et al.

items.title: Challenging the Körner-Pati-Woo Theorem in Charmed Baryon Decays
items.summary: The Körner-Pati-Woo (KPW) theorem is a long-standing selection rule widely used in heavy-baryon decays. In this work, we argue that the conventional valence-color argument underlying the KPW theorem does not, by itself, establish an exact selection rule. The $\rm KPW$-$\rm SU(3)_F$ prediction for $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_c^0\to pK^-)$, inferred from $Λ_c^+\to Ξ^0K^+$, is $17.2\pm6.0$ times the measured value. A joint likelihood fit to five observables in $Ξ_c^0\to pK^-$ and $Λ_c^+\to Ξ^0K^+$ yields a $6.3σ$ discrepancy under the $\rm KPW$-$\rm SU(3)_F$ ansatz. A comparison of $α(Λ_c^+\to Δ^{++}K^-)$ and $α(Λ_c^+\to Σ^{*}π)$ reveals a pronounced sign-sensitive tension. Accommodating these measurements within the KPW constraint requires anomalously large $\rm SU(3)_F$ breaking effects.
items.author: Di Wang, Ying-Xin Lai, Fu-Sheng Yu

items.title: Quark dipole operators in the gradient-flow scheme at NNLO QCD
items.summary: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the CP-even sector, the results are provided for general quark masses and arbitrary flavor content of the operators. Specifically, this concerns the quark CMDM operator and its mixing with lower-dimensional QCD operators. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.
items.author: Janosch Borgulat, Lars Georg, Robert V. Harlander et al.

items.title: Ultrasensitive measurement of phase dynamics by time-holographic dark-port readout of a marginally imbalanced interferometer
items.summary: Resolving displacements and surface irregularities far below a nanometer is now indispensable across fields, from precision manufacturing and biotechnology to nanoscience and fundamental metrology. High-precision optical interferometry reaches this $λ/1{,}000$ regime by reading out optical power, which provides a smooth response over the measurement range. Here we instead read out the complex dark-port field of a marginally imbalanced interferometer, whose phase response to small internal phase deviations $φ_{\textrm{in}}$ near destructive interference becomes extremely steep. For a small arm-amplitude imbalance $μ$, the tangent $T_{\textrm{out}}$ of the dark-port phase reduces to $μ^{-1}φ_{\textrm{in}}$, defining a phase magnification $M=μ^{-1}$. Crucially, this tangent estimator stays linear over a range $|φ_{\textrm{in}}|\lesssim\sqrt{|μ|}$---much larger than the imbalance $|μ|$ itself for $|μ|\ll1$---so that fine temporal substructure is resolved within much larger phase excursions.
items.author: F. Silva, A. Molina, A. Esteban-Martín et al.

items.title: M 4.7 - 94 km W of Illapel, Chile
items.summary: A magnitude 4.7 earthquake was recorded 94 km W of Illapel, Chile. The event happened on 20 November 2026 at 14:16 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: A hybrid mixture approach for clustering and characterizing biomedical data
items.summary: Model-based clustering (MBC) is widely used for identifying latent groups and characterizing heterogeneous structures in biomedical data. However, modern biomedical studies often generate datasets with large sample sizes and many variables, for which standard MBC approaches can be difficult to fit reliably and efficiently.
items.author: Kazeem A. Kareem, Fan Dai

items.title: Immune evasion in Mucorales species: From stealth spores to angioinvasive hyphae
items.summary: Mucormycosis is an invasive fungal infection caused by members of the order Mucorales, which employ stage- and species-specific mechanisms to evade host immunity. Resting spores of experimentally studied Rhizopus species can persist after macrophage uptake because macrophages restrict germination but do not efficiently kill all internalized resting spores.
items.author: Rajesh Palanisamy, Maldonado Gabriela, Soo Chan Lee

items.title: Structural and functional analysis of VYD222: A broadly neutralizing antibody against SARS-CoV-2 variants
items.summary: Extensive mutations in SARS-CoV-2 spike protein have rendered most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) ineffective. However, here we describe how VYD222 (pemivibart), a human mAb re-engineered from ADG20 (adintrevimab) exhibits substantially improved neutralization potency and breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants despite substantial virus evolution.
items.author: Meng Yuan, Brandyn R. West, William B. Foreman et al.

items.title: When and how is preregistration in experimental biology worth the effort?
items.summary: by Olavo B. Amaral, Clarissa F. D. Carneiro, Bruna Valério-Gomes, Kleber Neves, Mariana B. Abreu Preregistration can improve the credibility of published research, but its uptake in the life sciences remains low. What is hampering its adoption in experimental biology, and can the format be adapted to better suit the needs of researchers? Preregistration can improve the credibility of published research, but its uptake in the life sciences remains low. This Perspective asks what is hampering its adoption in experimental biology, and can the format be adapted to better suit the needs of researchers?
items.author: Olavo B. Amaral, Clarissa F. D. Carneiro, Bruna Valério-Gomes et al.

items.title: Ionic condition-dependent allostery shapes ribosomal dynamics
items.summary: by Danis Yangaliev, Gürol M. Süel, S. Banu Ozkan Ionic composition is a key determinant of ribosomal RNA structure and function. Metal cations such as potassium (K + ) and magnesium (Mg 2+ ) stabilize rRNA architecture. While certain positions in the ribosome are strictly occupied by either potassium or magnesium for distinct structural or functional reasons, their broader role in modulating ribosomal dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we use microsecond-scale coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of the bacterial 70S ribosome to examine how ionic composition affects structural flexibility and long-range communication. We compare a native ribosome with experimentally resolved ions to two variants: a magnesium-enriched model, in which K + ions are replaced with Mg 2+ , and a hydrated magnesium model.
items.author: Danis Yangaliev, Gürol M. Süel, S. Banu Ozkan

items.title: Inferring population-level physiologically based model parameters for sleep in infancy and young childhood
items.summary: by Lachlan Webb, Andrew J. K. Phillips, James A. Roberts The sleep patterns of infants and young children differ from adult sleep patterns, with longer duration and multiple bouts per 24 hours. There is also considerable heterogeneity in infant sleep, both between individuals and within individuals across development. While mathematical models have been used to understand the mechanisms that regulate adult sleep, the development of sleep from infancy through early childhood has remained largely unexplored. Here we used an established mathematical model for adult sleep regulation to investigate how the underlying mechanisms of sleep mature from ages 1 month to 5 years, and identify a basis for inter-individual differences at each age.
items.author: Lachlan Webb, Andrew J. K. Phillips, James A. Roberts

items.title: Rollout models of human planning with exact action probabilities
items.summary: by Jeroen Olieslagers, Wei Ji Ma One proposed mechanism for human planning is the mental simulation, or “rollout,” of potential action sequences to evaluate future outcomes. While rollout-based models have seen great success in artificial intelligence, cognitive models that describe how people use rollouts remain scarce, in part because they are difficult to fit to behavioral data. Existing methods rely on computationally intensive simulations that result in approximate, noisy estimates of latent planning parameters. We introduce ROSETTE (Rollouts with Stochastic Early Termination and Tractable Estimation), a rollout-based model for finite goal-directed tasks with absorbing goals that provides analytically tractable, simulation-free model fitting.
items.author: Jeroen Olieslagers, Wei Ji Ma

items.title: Simulation-guided design of exotendons to reduce the energetic cost of running
items.summary: by Jon Stingel, Nicholas Bianco, Carmichael Ong, Steve Collins, Scott Delp, Jennifer Hicks A passive device that attaches to the feet, called an exotendon, can reduce the energetic cost of running at moderate speeds, but its efficacy and optimal design parameters at higher speeds are unknown. Identifying optimal parameters at new speeds experimentally would require many experimental trials with different exotendon designs, which is challenging for participants at higher running speeds. We developed a muscle-driven simulation framework to predict the effect of various exotendon designs on the energetic cost of running at an experimentally untested speed (4 m/s). We used these predictions to select four designs, which we evaluated experimentally as users ran at this speed.
items.author: Jon Stingel, Nicholas Bianco, Carmichael Ong et al.

items.title: Pupil dynamics reflect uncertainty-driven adjustments of probability learning
items.summary: by Aaron Greenhouse-Tucknott, Cedric Foucault, Anne Buot, Florent Meyniel Adaptive learning in dynamic environments depends on the brain’s ability to represent and respond to uncertainty. Changes in arousal-mediated pupil diameter provide insight into the neural basis of this process. Prior work has focused on magnitude-based inference tasks and revealed that learning is primarily influenced by the detection of change points and the corresponding modulation of arousal. In comparison, the role of arousal systems in learning contexts where changes are harder to detect, such as in probability learning, remains poorly understood. Here, we combined pupillometry with a probability learning task in which human participants estimated a hidden generative probability of stimuli that changed abruptly and unpredictably.
items.author: Aaron Greenhouse-Tucknott, Cedric Foucault, Anne Buot et al.

items.title: A new therapeutic opportunity in Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever: Targeting the stalk domain of viral nucleocapsid protein for therapeutic intervention
items.summary: by Hoangvi Le, Anuradha Roy, Ethan Mir, Xin Li, Saima Ali, Austin Royster, Songyang Ren, Yongcheng Song, Sheema Mir, Mohammad Mir Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is a high-consequence pathogen for which no approved antivirals or vaccines exist. The viral nucleocapsid protein (N protein) is central to the Nairovirus life cycle, coordinating genomic RNA encapsidation and selective enhancement of viral mRNA translation through its interaction with the panhandle-like hairpin structure in the S-segment mRNA 5′ untranslated region (UTR). Here, we developed a robust fluorescence polarization anisotropy (FPA) based high-throughput assay capable of quantitatively monitoring the interaction between purified N protein and the viral 5′UTR hairpin.
items.author: Hoangvi Le, Anuradha Roy, Ethan Mir et al.

items.title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of a Narrative Comprehension Assessment (NCA) for Indian children
items.summary: by Ramandeep Kaur, Darryl Jeethesh Dsouza, Dency Davis, Melicia Shainy Dsouza Narrative comprehension requires children to understand explicitly presented information and integrate events to derive implicit meanings. Despite its developmental and educational importance, English-language narrative assessments developed within the Indian cultural context remain limited. This study developed and conducted a preliminary psychometric evaluation of the Narrative Comprehension Assessment (NCA), a picture-based assessment for Indian children aged 4–8 years. The NCA was developed across three phases. An initial set of 27 comprehension questions was refined through expert review to 20 items comprising 9 literal and 11 inferential questions. The final assessment used two wordless picture narratives and four sequential components: Picture Walk, Retelling, Prompted Comprehension, and Guided Story Narration.
items.author: Ramandeep Kaur, Darryl Jeethesh Dsouza, Dency Davis et al.

items.title: Prediction of a task-specific AI-reliance choice from facial expression and galvanic skin response signals
items.summary: by Hamid Shamszare, Avishek Choudhury Background Reliance on AI-supported health recommendations is consequential, but a single behavioral source-selection decision is not equivalent to multidimensional psychological trust. Biosignals may contain predictive information before a choice, although small-sample multimodal models require leakage-free evaluation and cautious interpretation. Purpose This study evaluated whether facial-expression probabilities and galvanic skin response (GSR) features predict a task-specific binary choice of an AI-labeled rather than doctor-labeled recommendation in a simulated ADHD assessment. The outcome is treated as a behavioral indicator of reliance rather than a direct measure of psychological trust. Method: This cross-sectional laboratory analysis included a cohort of 60 participants (40 AI-labeled and 20 doctor-labeled choices).
items.author: Hamid Shamszare, Avishek Choudhury

items.title: Comparative evaluation of single and multiple camera-based pose estimation methods for gait spatiotemporal parameter estimation
items.summary: by Bethany Weber, Brandon Schoenwether, Tyler Booth, Megan McFarland, Jennifer Britton, Moataz Eltoukhy Single-camera pose estimation may provide a more accessible approach to measure a person’s walking patterns (i.e., gait analysis) than multi-camera markerless motion capture (MMC), but its validity and test-retest reliability remain unclear. This study evaluated spatiotemporal gait parameters from a single iPad camera against an eight-camera MMC reference system across four visits, two weeks apart. Thirty-six healthy adults (18.7 ± 1.7, ranging 18‒27 years) completed usual-gait, bag-carrying, and phone-use walking conditions. Validity analyses included 458 paired trials from Visit 1 and used repeated-measures and mixed-effects methods. Reliability analyses included 33 participants with complete four-visit data and evaluated absolute agreement of single visit-level measurements.
items.author: Bethany Weber, Brandon Schoenwether, Tyler Booth et al.

items.title: Analysis of factors hindering the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: A qualitative study
items.summary: by Cuicui Dou, Yi Sun, Keke Dai, Man Wei, Jiawen Li, Kaili Qu, Qiongyan Hu, Huiyan Zhang Background Elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) have a high incidence of perioperative hypothermia due to anesthetic suppression of thermoregulation, prolonged surgical duration, and diminished endogenous thermoregulatory function, which can lead to poor outcomes. Effective prevention of hypothermia is a critical clinical issue; however, previous studies have lacked in-depth analysis of comprehensive continuous management and practical barriers. Objective This study aimed to identify barriers to the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients. Methods A qualitative study design was employed, conducted from January to February 2026 at a Grade III Level A hospital in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
items.author: Cuicui Dou, Yi Sun, Keke Dai et al.

items.title: Exploring barriers and facilitators to Hepatitis C virus treatment access in Los Angeles County: A mixed-methods study
items.summary: by Shikha Handa, Nathan Sudeep, Larisa Albers, Monica Pattarroyo, Juan Vasquez, Roberto E. Montgomerie, Ryan M. Nguyen, Kendall Dimson, Deena Afana, Chrysovalantis Stafylis, Jeffrey D. Klausner, Daniel Soto Diagnosed but untreated chronic Hepatitis C virus infection remains an important public health problem in Los Angeles County, particularly affecting underserved and minority groups. This mixed-methods study (October 2024-January 2025) aimed to identify and describe the barriers and facilitators to accessing Hepatitis C virus treatment among Los Angeles County residents. The study used de-identified programmatic data from 344 case-residents in a linkage-to-cure program and conducted thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with ten participants (seven untreated, three treated) from the linkage-to-cure program.
items.author: Shikha Handa, Nathan Sudeep, Larisa Albers et al.

items.title: Association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults: A cross-sectional analysis of CLHLS 2017-2018
items.summary: by Lunan Gao Background Prior studies have yielded inconsistent findings regarding the interplay between cognitive function, depression, self-care ability, and sleep quality in older adults, necessitating deeper exploration to elucidate these complex associations. Objectives This study aimed to examine whether self-care ability mediates the association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms, and whether sleep quality moderates this relationship in Chinese older adults. Methods We analyzed data from 7,580 older adults (aged ≥65 years) participating in a nationwide longitudinal survey in China (CLHLS, 2017−2018 wave). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 10-item Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D-10). Self-care ability was measured by physical activities of daily living (PADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL).
items.author: Lunan Gao

items.title: High blood pressure among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus in Uganda: A multicenter cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Charles Mwendwa Mutisya, Martin Nduwimana, Dickson Kajoba, Grace Ndeezi Background The coexistence of diabetes mellitus (DM) and hypertension (HTN) worsens the clinical outcomes of children with diabetes concerning both microvascular and macrovascular disease. It increases mortality risk by 5 times, with a higher risk of death in developing countries. Therefore, comprehensive care for patients with diabetes, including hypertension screening, must be provided. Methods This multicenter health facility-based cross-sectional study included 150 children and adolescents aged from 6 months to 18 years with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) who were treated at Jinja Regional Referral Hospital (JRRH), Mbale Regional Referral Hospital (MRRH) and Lira Regional Referral Hospital (LRRH).
items.author: Charles Mwendwa Mutisya, Martin Nduwimana, Dickson Kajoba et al.

items.title: Alginate hydrogel co-loaded with phellodendron bark extract and HucMSC-exosomes for combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-repair acne effects
items.summary: by Yu He, Yu Wang, Yaofeng Zhi, Minxian Li, Meimei Wu, Yanyang Mai, Jiadi He, Jiaqin Chen, KwanNin To, Meigong Zhong, Xiaohong Ruan, Wanli Zuo, Yanming Huang, Liping Liang, MengDie Ou, Guohua Cheng, Xin Zhang Acne vulgaris is a common inflammatory skin disorder involving follicular hyperkeratosis, Cutibacterium acnes proliferation, and aberrant inflammation, often leading to scarring. Current antibiotic treatments face resistance and limited repair capacity. Here, we developed an alginate-based hydrogel co-loaded with Phellodendron bark extract (PBE) and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (HucMSC-Exo) (PE gel). Antibacterial activity of PBE was evaluated against C. acnes , S. aureus , and E.
items.author: Yu He, Yu Wang, Yaofeng Zhi et al.

items.title: Association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways and postoperative delirium in geriatric hip fracture patients: A retrospective cohort study
items.summary: by Zixing Zhao, Jinsheng Yu, Yubin Lan, Baitao Yang, Qi Tan, Zaoxiong Wen, Yitao Yao, Cuitian He, Xinyu Fang Background Elderly hip fracture patients are at high risk of postoperative delirium (POD). The association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways and POD incidence remains poorly clarified. This study aimed to explore the association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways, internal fixation clinical pathway(IFCP), versus arthroplasty clinical pathway(ARCP), and POD occurrence in elderly hip fracture patients. Methods This retrospective cohort study examined the medical records of patients aged 65 years and older who underwent hip fracture surgery at a tertiary medical facility from January 2022 to December 2025.
items.author: Zixing Zhao, Jinsheng Yu, Yubin Lan et al.

items.title: Intelligent chemical production mode occupational health risk identification, assessment and intervention study
items.summary: by Yin Fei Shen, Jian Qing Xu The intelligent transformation of the chemical industry has reshaped petrochemical production workflows and altered occupational-health risk landscapes. This paper delineates four typical operating scenarios for intelligent chemical manufacturing and develops a four-tier hierarchical risk indicator system covering objectives, criteria, factors, and measurable indicators. A hybrid entropy-weighted Bayesian-network evaluation model is established, where entropy weights calibrate prior probabilities of root-node inputs while conditional-probability tables are retained to characterize risk-coupling behaviors. Model performance is validated via time-series partitioning, multi-model benchmark comparisons, and cross-validation using Monte-Carlo simulations. An entropy-weighted TOPSIS multi-criteria decision-making method is adopted to rank intervention-target priorities, and discrete time-series analysis quantifies outcomes from a six-month closed-loop intervention program.
items.author: Yin Fei Shen, Jian Qing Xu

items.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People’s Democratic Republic, 2018–2019
items.summary: by Vilaysone Khounvisith, Bounthome Samountry, Janko van Beek, Aurélie Sausy, Regina Brunnhoefer, Bounta Vongphachanh, Khamtim Samountry, Maude Pauly, Joel Mossong, Jessica Tapp, Claude P. Muller, Antony P. Black, Judith M. Hübschen Background Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women. Methods Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18–76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and Anyplex TM II HPV-HR detection.
items.author: Vilaysone Khounvisith, Bounthome Samountry, Janko van Beek et al.

items.title: Civic and community engagement among health profession students and professionals compared to the general population: A systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
items.summary: by Aria Ghasedi, Ramin Vahidi Background Physicians, nurses, and other health professionals encounter poverty, inequality, and the structural roots of ill health as a routine part of clinical work — an exposure that differs from that of most other occupations. The World Health Organization, the Global Consensus for Social Accountability of Medical Schools, and many professional bodies describe civic and community engagement as a professional responsibility. Whether health profession students and practitioners show higher, lower, or comparable levels of civic engagement relative to the broader public in non-crisis conditions has not been systematically reviewed. The existing literature is fragmented, limited to single professions, focused largely on pandemic volunteerism, and more concerned with attitudes than with behaviour.
items.author: Aria Ghasedi, Ramin Vahidi

items.title: Puncturable registered attribute-based keyword search for secure cloud data sharing
items.summary: by Zeyang Song, Yuyan Guo, Mingming Jiang, Zhiyao Yang Cloud data sharing requires methods that protect sensitive files while allowing authorized users to find and access them. Centralized key generation creates a risk of key escrow, while exposed user keys may compromise previously shared data. We develop a scheme that combines encrypted keyword search with selective restriction of decryption keys in a registered framework. Users generate their own secret keys, and a key curator verifies and aggregates public registration information. Owners attach descriptive keywords and tags to encrypted files. Search compares combined keyword representations, and each new index excludes users according to the owner’s current list.
items.author: Zeyang Song, Yuyan Guo, Mingming Jiang et al.

items.title: Elevated blood lead levels among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen: Socio-demographic correlates and associations with a history of spontaneous abortion
items.summary: by Lina Qasem, Abdulsalam Al-Shami, Tawfeek A. A. Yahya, Lutfi AS. Al-Maktari, Mohammed Al-Maqhafi, Akram Al-Marqasi Background Lead exposure in pregnant women is a critical public health concern, particularly in resource-limited settings where environmental regulations are less stringent. Prenatal lead exposure (Pb) is associated with various adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Therefore, this study aimed to assess blood lead levels (BLLs) among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen, and to identify health risks associated with environmental, behavioral, and socio-demographic factors. Methods A cross-sectional multi-center study was conducted between August and November 2024, involving a sample of 150 pregnant women (aged 20–41 years) recruited across public and private healthcare facilities in Amran.
items.author: Lina Qasem, Abdulsalam Al-Shami, Tawfeek A. A. Yahya et al.

items.title: Visuo-spatial perception deficit in ophthalmological disorders: Visual field extent matters
items.summary: by Hind Drissi, Marie Jauze, Eloise Perrier, Kenza Takani, Anne Céline Blanc, Armelle Laurens, Amandine Plaza, Jacqueline Jourdan, Julie Ferrotin, Elise Miclo, Lucie Loria, Florence De Saint-Etienne, Carole Malet, Laure Pisella Objectives Persons with Visual Impairment (VI) are more at risk to be without academic qualification. This is classically attributed to limited access to visual information, considered difficult due to reduced visual acuity. However, in some cases, visual acuity is preserved but visual field is reduced. Given the importance of visuo-spatial skills in learning, we assessed the accuracy of perceptual visuo-spatial judgements relative to visual field extent and visual acuity to question their respective contribution to the functional repercussions in VI.
items.author: Hind Drissi, Marie Jauze, Eloise Perrier et al.

items.title: Gender representation in highly cited endodontic research: A multivariate analysis
items.summary: by Esra Arılı Öztürk, Ceren Turan Gökduman, Şule Aktaş, Burhan Can Çanakçi To evaluate the representation of women as first, last, and corresponding authors in highly cited endodontic articles and investigate factors related to female authorship. The 200 most-cited endodontic articles published between 2015 and 2024 were identified in the Web of Science Core Collection. Authors’ genders were determined using an automated database and manually verified. Associations between female authorship and journal features, geographic origin, funding, collaboration patterns, and citation performance were analyzed using multivariable regression models. Among 1,262 authors, 31% were women. Women represented 36% of first authors, 24.5% of last authors, and 33.5% of corresponding authors; 77.5% of articles included at least one woman.
items.author: Esra Arılı Öztürk, Ceren Turan Gökduman, Şule Aktaş et al.

items.title: Calreticulin modulates the infection process and nodule organogenesis in the Phaseolus vulgaris-Rhizobium symbiosis
items.summary: by Yolanda Ortega-Ortega, Janet Carrasco-Castilla, Marco A. Juárez-Verdayes, Noreide Nava, Jorge Solis-Miranda, Ronal Pacheco, Carmen Quinto Calreticulin (CRT) is an endoplasmic-reticulum Ca 2 ⁺ -binding chaperone with established roles in Ca 2 ⁺ homeostasis and protein quality control, but its contribution to legume-rhizobium symbiosis is poorly understood. Here, we identified the CRT family of Phaseolus vulgaris and investigated the role of PvCRT08 during symbiosis with Rhizobium tropici CIAT 899. PvCRT08 showed dynamic transcript accumulation during the symbiosis; moreover, promoter activity was detected in root hairs, cortical cells, nodule primordia, and infected cells of mature nodules. RNAi-mediated downregulation of PvCRT08 increased the number of infection threads reaching cortical cells, whereas overexpression increased infection threads retained in root hairs and reduced those reaching the cortex.
items.author: Yolanda Ortega-Ortega, Janet Carrasco-Castilla, Marco A. Juárez-Verdayes et al.

items.title: A boundary-sensitive and structure-adaptive lightweight network for medical image segmentation
items.summary: by Yaodong Guo, Yuzhu Liu, Sai Ma Reliable medical image segmentation remains challenging in weak-contrast boundary regions, ambiguous anatomical transitions, and structurally heterogeneous areas. In addition, many high-performing models improve overlap-based metrics by introducing increasingly complex architectures, making it difficult to balance segmentation accuracy, boundary fidelity, and model compactness. To address these issues, this paper presents a boundary-sensitive and structure-adaptive lightweight framework for CT liver segmentation. The proposed method integrates three task-oriented components in a U-shaped architecture: Boundary-Sensitive Semantic Recalibration Attention (BSRA), Structure-Adaptive Scale Selection Fusion (SASF), and a Detail-Compensated Residual Lightweight Block (DCRB). Experiments were conducted on the CT subset of the CHAOS dataset under a patient-level five-fold cross-validation protocol.
items.author: Yaodong Guo, Yuzhu Liu, Sai Ma

items.title: Heterogeneous mixture-of-experts for long-horizon vessel trajectory prediction across regional datasets
items.summary: by Yuxiang Tan, Yingqiang Cai, Kuan Fan, Xiaowen Li, Guangyu Qiu Long-horizon vessel trajectory prediction for maritime traffic monitoring and route planning requires both a prompt response to manoeuvres and control of error accumulation. UnifiedInternalMoE combines a motion-prior residual expert with four temporal predictors in a separate checkpoint for each region and seed. Convex weights are fitted to validation predictions at 5, 10, and 60 min and interpolated to produce the complete future trajectory. A ten-seed comparison across four regions, together with capacity controls, learned gating, and internal ablations, evaluates the benefit of the heterogeneous combination and its sources. In a five-seed evaluation on an independent Finnish AIS subset, the fusion has the lowest mean average displacement error (ADE) at all six horizons, with ADE@60 of 1719.53±25.80 m; it does not consistently lead in long-horizon final displacement error (FDE) or frozen source-to-target transfer.
items.author: Yuxiang Tan, Yingqiang Cai, Kuan Fan et al.

items.title: Sleep hygiene, caffeine use, and academic performance among university students: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Razi Alshaikh, Wadea Jebriel, Mohammad Shahrouri, Tartil Zarura, Hasan Khouli Background Caffeine use is common among university students, but its associations with sleep hygiene and academic performance remain uncertain. This study examined these associations among Palestinian university students. Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted from March 21 to May 28, 2026. Among 379 participants, continuous grade point average (GPA) was available for 354. Measures included estimated caffeine intake, caffeine timing, Sleep Hygiene Index (SHI) score, sleep duration, sleep regularity, and study hours. Associations were assessed using analysis of variance, correlation, and multivariable linear regression. Caffeine intake was entered into the regression model as ln(mg/day + 1).
items.author: Razi Alshaikh, Wadea Jebriel, Mohammad Shahrouri et al.

items.title: Motor imagery-based brain-computer interface training for upper-limb rehabilitation after subacute stroke: A randomized sham-controlled trial
items.summary: by Qifeng Tong, Jianing Wu, Pengcheng Fan, Sunyue Cai, Minzhe Wang, Jianqiu Gong, Fangchao Wu Objective To determine whether motor imagery (MI) based brain-computer interface (BCI) training improves upper-limb motor function in patients with subacute stroke compared with a high-fidelity sham-BCI control, and to explore accompanying structural and resting-state functional MRI changes. Method In this participant-blinded randomized controlled trial, 32 patients with subacute stroke were randomized to a MI-based BCI group or a high-fidelity BCI sham-control group (n = 16 each). Both groups received dose-matched training (30 min/session, 5 sessions/week for 4 weeks) in addition to standard rehabilitation. Upper-limb motor outcomes were assessed using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE; primary outcome), Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT), Motor Assessment Scale (MAS), and Modified Barthel Index (MBI).
items.author: Qifeng Tong, Jianing Wu, Pengcheng Fan et al.

items.title: Impact of MRI sequence heterogeneity on deep learning–based segmentation of brain metastases
items.summary: by Dong-Won Shin, Chang Hyun Lee, Hyun Ju Kim, Kihoon Sung, Young Jae Kim, Kwang Gi Kim, Gi Taek Yee Brain metastases (BMs) require accurate delineation for treatment planning, yet magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) acquisition protocols vary substantially in clinical practice. Such protocol-level heterogeneity may affect the generalizability of deep learning-based segmentation models. This study evaluated the impact of heterogeneous T1-weighted MRI protocols on BM segmentation performance using two three-dimensional architectures, 3D Attention U-Net and DUCK-Net 3D. A retrospective dataset of 925 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI studies from 720 patients was analyzed. Models were trained under six sequence configurations, including multi-sequence, Black-Blood (BB), Non-Black-Blood (Non-BB), and three single-sequence cohorts.
items.author: Dong-Won Shin, Chang Hyun Lee, Hyun Ju Kim et al.

items.title: Forest proximity and habitat heterogeneity support insectivorous birds and arthropods in California vineyards
items.summary: by Eleanor K. MacDonald, Daniel S. Karp, Autumn Turner, Breanna L. Martinico, Houston Wilson, Erin E. Wilson-Rankin, Matthew D. Johnson Agricultural intensification often simplifies habitat structure, reshaping multi-trophic communities by altering arthropod prey and the insectivorous birds that depend on them throughout the year, particularly during breeding. In vineyards, insectivorous birds may also contribute to pest suppression, creating opportunities to link biodiversity conservation with agroecosystem function. We paired point count bird surveys with concurrent sticky trap arthropod sampling across 20 organic or near-organic vineyards in Napa Valley, California, USA, to test whether the same habitat features predict variation in insectivorous bird guilds and arthropod communities.
items.author: Eleanor K. MacDonald, Daniel S. Karp, Autumn Turner et al.

items.title: CogD-ML: Cognitive determinants of social commerce purchase intention in Bangladesh using machine learning and explainable AI
items.summary: by Saikat Barua, Raiyan Rahman, Abul Kalam Al Azad, Sifat Momen Cognitive factors are associated with online purchase intentions in developing economies, and the linear models conventionally used to study them can miss non-linear patterns. We report an applied integration of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with machine learning and explainable AI (XAI) to predict social media-driven e-commerce purchase intentions in Bangladesh. Survey data from 352 young, student-dominated consumers captured attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase behavior on validated Likert scale items. After reliability-based labeling and feature selection, we ran an ablation across seven classical classifiers and one multilayer perceptron, with stratified five-fold cross-validation, threshold sensitivity analysis, and a cross-domain check.
items.author: Saikat Barua, Raiyan Rahman, Abul Kalam Al Azad et al.

items.title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
items.summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.
items.author: Shuntaro Aoki, Lucas Pinol, Zhehan Qin et al.

items.title: Forbidden T-symmetry breaking in time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with gain and loss
items.summary: Parity-time ($PT$) symmetry has attracted significant interest in photonics and related fields in recent years. With sufficiently weak gain and loss, these systems typically exhibit entirely real energy levels, with all corresponding wave functions remaining $PT$ symmetric. As the strength of gain and loss increases, complex-conjugate energy levels are expected to emerge, signaling the onset of $PT$ symmetry breaking. Similar properties can be found in non-Hermitian systems with other antilinear symmetries as well, where parity is replaced by another operator such as rotation ($R$) or simply the identity operator, resulting in $RT$-symmetric and $T$-symmetric non-Hermitian systems.
items.author: Li Ge

items.title: Atomic interferometry based on a phase-jump error signal with suppression of the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift
items.summary: We develop a method for forming Ramsey fringes in atomic interferometers as a difference error signal using the phase-jump technique for Ramsey pulses (phase-jump error signal). In this case, the measurement procedure can be implemented as stabilization (locking) of the frequency chirp rate at the central zero of the error signal. We show analytically that this approach allows suppressing the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift (LACS). This shift was recently theoretically predicted and experimentally identified in the papers [V. I. Yudin et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{122}, 737 (2025); D. N. Kapusta et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{123}, 388 (2026)]. A characteristic feature of the LACS is an inverse cubic dependence $\propto 1/T^3$ (where $T$ is the time between adjacent Ramsey pulses), and it can become dominant for interferometers with a short baseline.
items.author: V. I. Yudin, O. N. Prudnikov, A. V. Taichenachev et al.

items.title: Wildfire White Oak Flat, Alleghany, Virginia
items.summary: NASA's Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker lists an open event in the category wildfires. 2 Miles NW from Clifton Forge, VA The tracker collects reports from official agencies and updates them as an event develops. Open the source page for the latest details and maps.
items.author: NASA EONET

items.title: Disentangling Lengthscales in Disordered Fracture
items.summary: The interplay between quenched disorder and collective interactions can generate multiple emergent lengthscales in damage processes, yet their roles in determining the strength of heterogeneous materials remain incompletely understood. Here, we develop a coarse-grained description of load redistribution in the two-dimensional random fuse model (RFM) with Weibull-distributed quenched disorder, interpreting shielding in the crack-tip damage density as a consequence of nonlocal current redistribution. Our numerical results distinguish this emergent screening length, identified as the size of the statistical fracture process zone, from the regularizing length in Bazant's established quasibrittle size-effect law (SEL), revealing their distinct disorder dependences, and challenging previous associations of the two.
items.author: Matthaios Chouzouris, Marcelo A. Dias

items.title: M 5.1 - 15 km SSW of Balangonan, Philippines
items.summary: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake was recorded 15 km SSW of Balangonan, Philippines. The event happened on 20 November 2026 at 13:09 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 73 km. About 6 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
items.summary: The emergence of inverse-designed, pixelated passives for microwave and millimeter-wave applications has been a major development in the field of RFIC design. These devices, which appear to be QR-code-like in structure, exist in a generalizable, high-dimensional design space that includes conventional passive topologies. However, these structures are naturally unintuitive for designers, and failures or deviations in performance are difficult to debug. In this work, we ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict, and edit the responses and layout structure of pixelated passives. The agent, run with all tools disabled, is first asked to read layouts on 18x18 and 27x27 tile grids and, in a single reply, predict the input impedance and loss of the structure from 20-100 GHz.
items.author: Jonathan Zhou, Kaushik Sengupta

items.title: Adaptive-Optics-Aware Uplink and Downlink Analysis of Ground-to-HAPS FSO Links
items.summary: In this paper, we present an adaptive optics (AO)-aware analytical framework for ground-to- high-altitude platform station (HAPS) free-space optical (FSO) links considering both uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) transmission. The proposed model combines atmospheric attenuation, Exponentiated Weibull (EW) turbulence, Beckmann-type pointing error (PE), and field-of-view (FoV)-limited angle-of-arrival (AOA) loss. Adaptive optics correction (AOC) is incorporated through the number of corrected modes, allowing the impact of partial and stronger wavefront compensation to be directly reflected in the channel statistics. Analytical and numerically tractable expressions are derived for the outage probability (OP), average bit-error rate (BER), and an ergodic achievable-rate lower bound (EALB) optical channel.
items.author: Yalçın Ata, Rudolf Saathof, Muhsin Caner Gökçe

items.title: Actively stabilized Fabry-Pérot notch filters for correlated photons from cold two-level atoms
items.summary: We report two actively stabilized Fabry-Pérot cavities operated as reflection-mode notch filters for biphotons generated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a cold two-level atomic ensemble. In this source, elastic scattering at the excitation frequency increases the single-detector count rates and the accidental-coincidence background, thereby limiting the observed nonclassical correlations. One cavity is placed in each photon-collection mode. An acousto-optic modulator frequency-dithers an auxiliary field, and synchronous demodulation of the transmitted power provides the locking discriminator. Light resonant with the auxiliary field is transmitted, whereas the detuned components are reflected toward the photon detectors. By tuning the auxiliary field to the same frequency as the excitation field, we filter these components and direct a larger portion of the quantum-correlated sidebands to the detection.
items.author: G. C. Borges, M. Duclerc, G. Palacios et al.

items.title: Sprouting Fields of Conducting Polymer Dendrites as Evolving Organic Electrochemical Frameworks to Interconnect Electrode Arrays
items.summary: Balancing high performance with sustainability in microelectronics is challenged by energy-intensive processes, scarce materials and limited recyclability. Inspired by nature, a promising solution relies on the evolution of the foundry model to transient microelectronics, using electrochemistry to grow adaptive circuits on demand and during operation. To this end, this study explores how to harness the morphogenesis of conducting polymer dendrites between stacks of micro-electrode arrays to dynamically interconnect them with voltage pulses. Using propylene carbonate as a solvent, we investigated the dynamics of the electroconvective growth of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT), revealing strong structural dependencies between the morphology of the electrogenerated polymer and the confinement of the micro-electrodes.
items.author: Antoine Baron, Ewelina Cechosz, Konrad Szaciłowski et al.

items.title: Emergent Fourfold Symmetry in Polarization Images: Local Origin and Diffractive Breakdown
items.summary: A polarization image can gain or lose rotational symmetry with no change in material symmetry. In axisymmetric anisotropic systems, covariance restricts the field to azimuthal orders $m=0,\pm2$, guaranteeing twofold but not fourfold symmetry; pointwise unitarity adds fourfold symmetry, which diffraction can destroy. Holographic Jones fields of liquid-crystal torons show propagation shifts the twofold--fourfold balance; for the same director, a marching-wave model qualitatively reproduces the twofold morphology missed by a local model. This establishes a symmetry hierarchy for polarization imaging.
items.author: Igor S. Lobanov, Tikhon V. Reztsov, Artem N. Shalev et al.

items.title: M 4.7 - southeast of the Loyalty Islands
items.summary: A magnitude 4.7 earthquake was recorded southeast of the Loyalty Islands. The event happened on 20 November 2026 at 10:48 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Single-shot holographic gradients for training wavefronts through disorder
items.summary: Training optical systems in situ needs the gradient of their loss, yet a camera records only intensity and the medium is never exactly known. We show that one off-axis hologram gives this gradient, an approach we call holographic gradients. Light passes through the medium only forward; the hologram measures the error, and a compact adjoint, fitted to ten probes, is refreshed in seconds during train- ing. Each step costs one modulated pattern. Through a thin diffuser, it focuses light and forms images as well as a measured transmission matrix, without its thousands of patterns.
